Deus enim illorum odit iniquitatem, quum sit essentialiter sanctus et bonus: unde scriptum est: Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Nam et ante hos annos, quum recessissent a via quam dederat illis Deus, exterminati sunt præliis a multis nationibus, et plurimi eorum captivi abducti sunt in terram non suam. Nuper autem reversi de Babylonica captivitate ex licentia Cyri regis, ex dispersione qua dispersi fuerant, adunati sunt, et ascenderunt montana hæc omnia, hoc est, ad terram hanc patrum suorum montuosam reversi sunt.
paras.en: [[5:16|Wheresoever they went in without bow and arrow, and without shield and sword|Ubicumque ingressi sunt sine sagitta et arcu, et absque scuto et gladio]], [[5:16|their God fought for them|Deus eorum pro ipsis pugnavit]]: that is, He gave them the victory chiefly by His divine power, not by strength of arms; yet they themselves sometimes fought with arms, but prevailed with God's help; [[5:16|and overcame|et vicit]]. [[5:18|But as often as beside their own God|Quotiescumque autem præter Deum suum]], that is, the God of their fathers, who willed to be worshipped by them in a special way and bestowed many great spiritual benefits on them, [[5:18|they worshipped any other|alterum coluerunt]] with the worship of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], [[5:18|they were given to spoil and to the sword, and to reproach|dati sunt in prædam et in gladium et in opprobrium]], as is plain in the book of Judges[[Judg 2:11||]]. [[5:19|And as often as they were penitent|Quotiescumque autem pœnituerunt]], [[5:19|the God of heaven gave them power to resist|dedit eis Deus cæli virtutem resistendi]]. [[5:21|for their God hateth iniquity|Deus enim illorum odit iniquitatem]], since He is essentially holy and good: hence it is written, [[Wis 14:9|But to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike.|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]] [[5:22|And even some years ago when they had revolted from the way which God had given them|Nam et ante hos annos, quum recessissent a via quam dederat illis Deus]], [[5:22|they were destroyed in battles by many nations and very many of them were led away captive into a strange land|exterminati sunt præliis a multis nationibus, et plurimi eorum captivi abducti sunt in terram non suam]]. [[5:23|But of late returning|Nuper autem reversi]] from the Babylonian captivity by leave of king Cyrus, [[5:23|from the different places wherein they were scattered, they are come together|ex dispersione qua dispersi fuerant, adunati sunt]], [[5:23|and are gone up into all these mountains|et ascenderunt montana hæc omnia]], that is, they have returned to this hilly land of their fathers.

paras.t: Nunc ergo, mi domine, perquire si est aliqua iniquitas eorum in conspectu Dei eorum, id est, diligenter investiga, an in aliquo magno facinore, præsertim in idololatria Deum suum jam offenderunt, nec inde pœnituerunt; et si sic, ascendamus ad eos debellandos, quoniam tradet Deus eorum eos tibi. Si autem non est offensio populi hujus coram Deo suo, non poterimus resistere illis, quoniam Deus eorum defendet illos; et erimus in opprobrium universæ terræ.
paras.en: [[5:24|Now therefore, my lord, search if there be any iniquity of theirs in the sight of their God|Nunc ergo, mi domine, perquire si est aliqua iniquitas eorum in conspectu Dei eorum]], that is, investigate diligently whether they have now offended their God by some great crime, especially by idolatry, and have not repented of it; and if so, [[5:24|let us go up to them|ascendamus ad eos]] to subdue them, [[5:24|because their God will surely deliver them to thee|quoniam tradet Deus eorum eos tibi]]. [[5:25|But if there be no offence of this people in the sight of their God, we cannot resist them because their God will defend them: and we shall be a reproach to the whole earth|Si autem non est offensio populi hujus coram Deo suo, non poterimus resistere illis, quoniam Deus eorum defendet illos; et erimus in opprobrium universæ terræ]].

paras.t: Et factum est, quum cessasset loqui Achior verba hæc, irati sunt omnes magnates Holofernis, hæc audientes, et cogitabant interficere illum, dicentes: Quis est iste qui filios Israel posse dicat resistere regi Nabuchodonosor, et exercitibus ejus, homines inermes et sine virtute, et sine peritia artis pugnæ? Quia ars pugnæ plus valet in præliis quam potestas, secundum Vegetium. Unde scriptum est: Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens quam fortis. Ideo Salomon in Proverbiis dixit: Consiliis tractanda sunt bella. Verumtamen impii isti verba Achior male intellexerunt, atque mendaciter repetierunt. Non enim dixit filios Israel posse resistere exercitui Nabuchodonosor regis, sed quod Deus eorum defenderet eos, et pugnaret pro ipsis, si justi essent.
paras.en: [[5:26|And it came to pass, when Achior had ceased to speak these words, all the great men of Holofernes were angry|Et factum est, quum cessasset loqui Achior verba hæc, irati sunt omnes magnates Holofernis]], hearing these things, [[5:26|and they had a mind to kill him, saying|et cogitabant interficere illum, dicentes]]: [[5:27|Who is this, that saith the children of Israel can resist king Nabuchodonosor, and his armies, men unarmed, and without force, and without skill in the art of war?|Quis est iste qui filios Israel posse dicat resistere regi Nabuchodonosor, et exercitibus ejus, homines inermes et sine virtute, et sine peritia artis pugnæ?]] For the art of fighting is worth more in battles than might, according to Vegetius. Hence it is written: [[Wis 6:1|Wisdom is better than strength: and a wise man is better than a strong man.|Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens quam fortis]] Therefore Solomon said in Proverbs that [[Prov 20:18|wars are to be managed|Consiliis tractanda sunt bella]] by counsels [Denis has *consiliis*, by counsels, where the Vulgate reads *gubernaculis*, by governments]. Yet these wicked men understood Achior's words badly and repeated them falsely. For he did not say that the children of Israel could resist the army of king Nabuchodonosor, but that their God would defend them and fight for them, if they were just.

paras.t: Ut ergo agnoscat Achior quoniam fallit nos. Superbissimi isti fuerunt animo, incorrigibiles et prorsus indociles. Ascendamus in montana; et quum capti fuerint a nobis potentes eorum, videlicet filiorum Israel, tunc cum eisdem gladio transverberabitur, ut sciat omnis gens, quoniam Nabuchodonosor deus terræ est. Circa hoc scribit quidam: Non dicunt, Deus cæli, sed terræ. Videntur enim illius erroris fuisse, qui dicebat divinam providentiam ad cœlestia se tantum extendere, secundum quod dicitur in Job: Circa cardines cæli perambulat, nec nostra considerat. Hoc autem nomen, Deus, impositum fuit a providentia rerum et gubernatione: ideo deum terræ dicebant, cujus regimen ad plura se extendit. Intentio autem regis Nabuchodonosor et sui exercitus fuit, omnem terram suo subjugare imperio. Propter quod a suis denominabatur deus terræ. Hæc ille. Cujus verbis non videtur concordare quod subditur, et præter ipsum alius non est, supple, deus. Unde videtur fuisse eorum error, quod non esset deus præter Nabuchodonosor. Nam et sequenti capitulo Holofernes ait ad Achior: Ut ostendam tibi, quia non est deus nisi Nabuchodonosor. Superius quoque dictum est: Præceperat Holoferni Nabuchodonosor rex, ut omnes deos terræ exterminaret, ut ipse solus diceretur deus ab his nationibus, etc.
paras.en: [[5:28|That Achior therefore may know that he deceiveth us|Ut ergo agnoscat Achior quoniam fallit nos]]. These men were most proud in mind, incorrigible and altogether unteachable. [[5:28|let us go up into the mountains|Ascendamus in montana]]; [[5:28|and when the bravest of them shall be taken|et quum capti fuerint a nobis potentes eorum]], that is, of the children of Israel, [[5:28|then shall he with them be stabbed with the sword|tunc cum eisdem gladio transverberabitur]], [[5:29|That every nation may know that Nabuchodonosor is god of the earth|ut sciat omnis gens, quoniam Nabuchodonosor deus terræ est]]. On this someone writes: They do not say *God of heaven*, but *of the earth*. For they seem to have held the error of those who said that the divine providence extends to heavenly things only, according to what is said in Job: [[Job 22:14|he walketh about the poles of heaven|Circa cardines cæli perambulat]], [[Job 22:14|and he doth not consider our things|nec nostra considerat]]. Now this name *God* was given from the providence and governance of things: so they called him the god of the earth whose rule extends to more things. And the intention of king Nabuchodonosor and of his army was [[Jdt 2:3|to bring all the earth under his empire|omnem terram suo subjugare imperio]]. That is why he was named by his own people the god of the earth. Thus far that writer. With whose words what follows does not seem to agree, [[5:29|and besides him there is no other|et præter ipsum alius non est]], supply *god*. Hence their error seems to have been that there was no god but Nabuchodonosor. For in the following chapter too Holofernes says to Achior: [[Jdt 6:2|to shew thee that there is no God, but Nabuchodonosor|Ut ostendam tibi, quia non est deus nisi Nabuchodonosor]]. And it was said above: [[Jdt 3:13|Nabuchodonosor the king had commanded him to destroy all the gods of the earth, that he only might be called God by those nations|Præceperat Holoferni Nabuchodonosor rex, ut omnes deos terræ exterminaret, ut ipse solus diceretur deus ab his nationibus]], etc.

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero, per Holofernem et bellatores ipsius, significantur tyranni et persecutores Ecclesiæ; per gentes autem quæ legatos suos miserunt ad Holofernem pro pace, et consenserunt subjici imperio ejus, intelliguntur pusilli et imperfecti, qui non valent aliquid magnæ adversitatis pro justitia pati, nec mori pro Christo: qui de talibus loquitur, quod tempore tentationis recedunt. Porro, per filios Israel metuentes, ne Holofernes faceret Jerusalem temploque Domini, quod fecerat aliis urbibus et diis ipsorum, intelliguntur fideles rite constantes, qui magis verentur irreverentiam Dei et Sanctorum ac sacramentorum ipsius, quam propriam mortem, maluntque mori quam christianæ religionis ac fidei catholicæ conculcationem videre: ideo spiritualibus armis, imo et corporalibus quandoque resistunt. Per Achior demum, boni catechumeni competenter instructi, ac fidem tenentes, sed nondum baptizati, signantur: qualis (ut in Actibus legitur) fuit Apollo ille electus, viam Dei edoctus, sciens tantum baptisma Joannis, et cœpit fideliter in Ecclesia agere.
paras.en: Spiritually, by Holofernes and his warriors are signified the tyrants and persecutors of the Church; by the nations that sent their ambassadors to Holofernes for peace and consented to be subject to his rule are understood the little ones and the imperfect, who are not strong enough to suffer any great adversity for justice, nor to die for Christ, who speaks of such men, that [[Luke 8:13|in time of temptation they fall away|tempore tentationis recedunt]]. Further, by the children of Israel, fearing lest Holofernes should do to Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord what he had done to other cities and their gods, are understood the faithful who are duly constant, who fear irreverence towards God and His Saints and sacraments more than their own death, and would rather die than see the Christian religion and the Catholic faith trampled underfoot: and so they resist with spiritual arms, and indeed sometimes with bodily ones too. By Achior, lastly, are signified good catechumens, fittingly instructed and holding the faith, but not yet baptized: such as (as is read in the Acts) was that chosen man Apollo, [[Acts 18:25|instructed in the way of the Lord|viam Dei edoctus]], [[Acts 18:25|knowing only the baptism of John|sciens tantum baptisma Joannis]], and he began to act faithfully in the Church[[Acts 18:26||]].

6.title: Declaratio capituli sexti: Factum est autem quum cessassent loqui
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: And it came to pass when they had left off speaking

paras.t: Factum est autem quum cessassent loqui magnates Holofernis ad Achior, ut habetur in fine præcedentis capituli, indignatus Holofernes, magnatibus suis consentiens et applaudens, dixit ad Achior: Quoniam prophetasti nobis: hoc irrisorie ait; dicens, quod gens Israel defendatur a Deo suo, quando obedit ei in omnibus; ut ostendam tibi quoniam non est Deus nisi Nabuchodonosor; quum percusserimus eos omnes, sicut hominem unum, hoc est, ita quod nullus eorum evadat, vel ita faciliter sicut hominem unum, tunc et ipse cum illis interibis, et omnis Israel tecum perditione disperiet; et probabis, id est, in te ipso experieris, et tua morte testaberis, quod Nabuchodonosor sit dominus universæ terræ. Tuncque gladius militiæ meæ transiet per latera tua, et confixus cades inter vulneratos Israel, et non respirabis ultra, donec extermineris cum illis. O quam stolidissima verba! quia et dato quod filii Israel et Achior permissi fuissent occidi ab Holoferne, ex hoc consequens non fuisset, quod Nabuchodonosor esset deus terræ, sed quod esset tyrannus et persecutor crudelis. Nam et impii in hac vita frequenter prævalent contra justos, quos Deus exercet, purgat, et coronat per impios.
paras.en: [[6:1|And it came to pass when they had left off speaking|Factum est autem quum cessassent loqui]], that is, the great men of Holofernes, to Achior, as is had at the end of the preceding chapter, [[6:1|that Holofernes being in a violent passion|indignatus Holofernes]], agreeing with his great men and applauding them, [[6:1|said to Achior|dixit ad Achior]]: [[6:2|Because thou hast prophesied unto us|Quoniam prophetasti nobis]] (this he says in mockery), [[6:2|saying: That the nation of Israel is defended by their God|dicens, quod gens Israel defendatur a Deo suo]], when it obeys him in all things; [[6:2|to shew thee that there is no God, but Nabuchodonosor|ut ostendam tibi quoniam non est Deus nisi Nabuchodonosor]]: [[6:3|When we shall slay them all as one man|quum percusserimus eos omnes, sicut hominem unum]], that is, so that none of them escapes, or as easily as one man, [[6:3|then thou also shalt die with them|tunc et ipse cum illis interibis]], [[6:3|and all Israel shall perish with thee|et omnis Israel tecum perditione disperiet]]; [[6:4|And thou shalt find|et probabis]], that is, thou shalt experience in thyself and bear witness by thy death, [[6:4|that Nabuchodonosor is lord of the whole earth|quod Nabuchodonosor sit dominus universæ terræ]]: [[6:4|and then the sword of my soldiers shall pass through thy sides, and thou shalt be stabbed and fall among the wounded of Israel, and thou shalt breathe no more till thou be destroyed with them|Tuncque gladius militiæ meæ transiet per latera tua, et confixus cades inter vulneratos Israel, et non respirabis ultra, donec extermineris cum illis]] [the scan is damaged in this verse; its words are restored from the Vulgate]. O what utterly stupid words! For even granted that the children of Israel and Achior had been allowed to be slain by Holofernes, it would not have followed from this that Nabuchodonosor was god of the earth, but that he was a tyrant and a cruel persecutor. For in this life the wicked often prevail against the just, whom God exercises, purges and crowns through the wicked.

paras.t: Porro si prophetiam tuam veram existimas, non concidat, hoc est, in mœrorem non cadat, vultus tuus, et pallor qui faciem tuam obtinuit, abscedat a te, si verba mea hæc putas impleri non posse. Ut autem noveris, quia simul cum illis hæc experieris, ecce ex hac hora illorum populo sociaberis, ut dum dignas gladii mei pœnas exceperint, ipse simul ultioni subjaceas. Quamvis autem Achior credidit se vera dixisse, non tamen mirum fuit quod timuit, quoniam ignoravit an filii Israel Deo placerent, et quoniam vidit verba sua recta intentione prolata, tam perverse, ægre, et erronee esse accepta.
paras.en: [[6:5|But if thou think thy prophecy true|Porro si prophetiam tuam veram existimas]], [[6:5|let not thy countenance sink|non concidat vultus tuus]] (*concidat*, that is, fall into grief), [[6:5|and let the paleness that is in thy face, depart from thee|et pallor qui faciem tuam obtinuit, abscedat a te]], [[6:5|if thou imaginest these my words cannot be accomplished|si verba mea hæc putas impleri non posse]]. [[6:6|And that thou mayst know that thou shalt experience these things together with them, behold from this hour thou shalt be associated to their people, that when they shall receive the punishment they deserve from my sword, thou mayst fall under the same vengeance|Ut autem noveris, quia simul cum illis hæc experieris, ecce ex hac hora illorum populo sociaberis, ut dum dignas gladii mei pœnas exceperint, ipse simul ultioni subjaceas]] [the scan is damaged in vv. 5–6; the words of the text there are restored from the Vulgate]. Now although Achior believed he had spoken the truth, it was no wonder that he was afraid, since he did not know whether the children of Israel were pleasing to God, and since he saw that his words, uttered with a right intention, had been taken so perversely, so ill and so wrongly.

paras.t: Tunc Holofernes præcepit servis suis, ut comprehenderent et ducerent eum, scilicet Achior, in Bethuliam, quæ de urbibus filiorum Israel fuit Holoferni vicinior, et traderent eum in manus filiorum Israel. Et accipientes eum servi Holofernis, profecti sunt per campestria; sed quum appropinquassent servi Holofernis cum Achior ad montana, exierunt contra eos fundibularii Israelitæ, jacientes saxa cum fundis, qui montium itinera observabant. Illi autem, servi scilicet Holofernis, divertentes a latere montis, ne a fundibulariis læderentur. Holofernes autem jubens servis suis perducere ipsum Achior usque Bethuliam, putavit quod filii Israel non auderent suos lædere servos. Ligaverunt Achior ad arborem manibus et pedibus, et sic vinctum dimiserunt eum, et reversi sunt ad dominum suum.
paras.en: [[6:7|Then Holofernes commanded his servants to take|Tunc Holofernes præcepit servis suis, ut comprehenderent]] [[6:7|Achior, and to lead him|et ducerent eum, scilicet Achior]] [[6:7|to Bethulia|in Bethuliam]], which of the cities of the children of Israel was nearest to Holofernes, [[6:7|and to deliver him into the hands of the children of Israel|et traderent eum in manus filiorum Israel]]. [[6:8|And the servants of Holofernes taking him, went through the plains|Et accipientes eum servi Holofernis, profecti sunt per campestria]]: [[6:8|but when they came near the mountains|sed cum appropinquassent ad montana]], [[6:8|the slingers came out against them|exierunt contra eos fundibularii]], Israelites, casting stones with slings, who were watching the ways through the mountains. [[6:9|Then turning out of the way by the side of the mountain|Illi autem divertentes a latere montis]] (the servants of Holofernes, that is), so as not to be hurt by the slingers (for Holofernes, in bidding his servants take Achior all the way to Bethulia, had thought the children of Israel would not dare to hurt his servants), [[6:9|they tied Achior to a tree hand and foot|Ligaverunt Achior ad arborem manibus et pedibus]], [[6:9|and so left him bound|et sic vinctum dimiserunt eum]], [[6:9|and returned to their master|et reversi sunt ad dominum suum]].

paras.t: Porro filii Israel solventes eum, duxerunt Bethuliam, atque in medium populi illum statuentes, percontati sunt, id est inquisierunt, quid rerum esset, id est quam ob causam, et ob cujus rei eventum, quod illum vinctum Assyrii reliquissent. In diebus illis erant illic principes, Ozias de tribu Simeon, et Charmi qui et Gothoniel. Circa hoc in Scholastica fertur historia, quod aliqui de Jerusalem miserant duos sacerdotes ad Oziam hunc in Bethuliam, sicut ad consolandum, dirigendum et confortandum cives Bethuliæ. In medio itaque seniorum et in conspectu omnium Achior dixit omnia quæ locutus ipse fuerat, ab Holoferne interrogatus.
paras.en: [[6:10|And the children of Israel|Porro filii Israel]], [[6:10|loosing him they brought him to Bethulia|solventes eum, duxerunt Bethuliam]], [[6:10|and setting him in the midst of the people, asked him|atque in medium populi illum statuentes, percontati sunt]], that is, inquired, [[6:10|what was the matter|quid rerum esset]], that is, for what reason and through what event, [[6:10|that the Assyrians had left him bound|quod illum vinctum Assyrii reliquissent]]. [[6:11|In those days the rulers there, were Ozias|In diebus illis erant illic principes, Ozias]] [[6:11|of the tribe of Simeon, and Charmi, called also Gothoniel|de tribu Simeon, et Charmi qui et Gothoniel]]. On this it is told in the Scholastic History that some from Jerusalem had sent two priests to this Ozias in Bethulia, as it were to console, direct and strengthen the citizens of Bethulia. [[6:12|And Achior related in the midst of the ancients, and in the presence of all the people, all that he had said being asked by Holofernes|In medio itaque seniorum et in conspectu omnium Achior dixit omnia quæ locutus ipse fuerat, ab Holoferne interrogatus]].

paras.t: Quumque universa Achior exposuisset, qualiter erat interrogatus ab Holoferne, et quid respondit eidem, omnis populus Bethuliæ hæc audiens, cecidit in faciem adorantes Dominum: quia ex verbis Achior compuncti fuerunt, et valde accensi ad invocationem Dei, spemque exauditionis conceperant, et zelo justo zelabantur pro Dei honore, pro veritatis ac justitiæ manifestatione: et communi lamentatione et fletu unanimes suas preces Domino effuderunt, dicentes: Domine, Deus cæli et terræ, intuere, id est, intuendo dejice et castiga, superbiam eorum, ut in præsenti puniti, non amplius peccent, nec cultui divino valeant adversari. Nempe pro dejectione hostium boni communis, orari potest ex zelo justitiæ, et boni communis amore. Et respice oculo pietatis ad nostram humilitatem, qui prostrati in toto corde et corpore, nos coram te humiliamus, et faciem sanctorum tuorum attende, id est mentes fidelium, seu preces et merita Patriarcharum ac Prophetarum sanctorum, per quos nos exaudire digneris; et ostende quia non derelinquis præsumentes de te, hoc est tua pietate et gratia, et præsumentes de se, et de sua virtute, id est potestate seu dignitate, gloriantes inaniter ac superbe, humilias, hoc est, dejicis, punis et damnas.
paras.en: [[6:14|And when Achior had declared all these things|Quumque universa Achior exposuisset]], how he had been questioned by Holofernes and what he had answered him, [[6:14|all the people|omnis populus]] of Bethulia, hearing this, [[6:14|fell upon their faces, adoring the Lord|cecidit in faciem adorantes Dominum]]: because they were pierced with compunction by Achior's words, and greatly kindled to call upon God, and had conceived hope of being heard, and were zealous with a just zeal for God's honour, for the showing forth of truth and justice: [[6:14|and all of them together mourning and weeping poured out their prayers with one accord to the Lord|et communi lamentatione et fletu unanimes suas preces Domino effuderunt]], [[6:15|Saying: O Lord God of heaven and earth|dicentes: Domine, Deus cæli et terræ]], [[6:15|behold their pride|intuere superbiam eorum]], that is, in beholding it cast it down and chastise it, so that, punished in this present time, they may sin no more nor be able to oppose the worship of God. For one may pray for the overthrow of the enemies of the common good out of zeal for justice and love of the common good. [[6:15|and look on our low condition|Et respice oculo pietatis ad nostram humilitatem]] with the eye of loving-kindness, we who, prostrate with all our heart and body, humble ourselves before thee, [[6:15|and have regard to the face of thy saints|et faciem sanctorum tuorum attende]], that is, the minds of the faithful, or the prayers and merits of the holy Patriarchs and Prophets, through whom mayest thou deign to hear us; [[6:15|and shew that thou forsakest not them that trust on thee|et ostende quia non derelinquis præsumentes de te]], that is, on thy loving-kindness and grace, [[6:15|and that thou humblest them that presume of themselves, and glory in their own strength|et præsumentes de se, et de sua virtute gloriantes, humilias]]: their own strength, that is, their power or rank, glorying vainly and proudly; humblest, that is, castest down, punishest and damnest.

paras.t: Finito itaque fletu, et per totam diem oratione populorum completa, consolati sunt ipsum Achior, dicentes: Deus patrum nostrorum, cujus tu virtutem prædicasti, ipse tibi hanc dabit vicissitudinem, id est recompensationem, ut eorum magis tu interitum videas. Quum vero Deus noster hanc libertatem dederit servis suis, hoc est liberationem ab Assyriis, quam tibi optamus, et affuturam speramus, sit et tecum Dominus in medio nostri per gratiam specialem, ut sicut placuerit tibi, ita cum omnibus tuis converseris nobiscum, id est, inter nos vivas et circumcisionem observantiasque legis nostræ accipias, si volueris. Non enim tenebantur gentiles ad legis mandata nisi moralia, cum fide Christi venturi: sed si voluerunt communicare Judæis in esu agni paschalis, aliisque quibusdam cærimonialibus legis, oportebat eos primitus circumcidi, juxta illud Exodi: Hæc est religio Phase: Si quis peregrinorum in vestram voluerit transire coloniam, circumcidetur prius omne masculinum ejus: si quis autem circumcisus non fuerit, non vescetur ex eo. Quemadmodum enim modo nullus admittitur ad evangelicæ legis sacramenta, nisi baptizatus, sic nec tunc ad Mosaicæ legis sacramenta, nisi circumcisus.
paras.en: [[6:16|So when their weeping was ended, and the people's prayer, in which they continued all the day, was concluded, they comforted Achior|Finito itaque fletu, et per totam diem oratione populorum completa, consolati sunt ipsum Achior]], [[6:17|Saying: The God of our fathers, whose power thou hast set forth, will make this return to thee|dicentes: Deus patrum nostrorum, cujus tu virtutem prædicasti, ipse tibi hanc dabit vicissitudinem]], that is, recompense, [[6:17|that thou rather shalt see their destruction|ut eorum magis tu interitum videas]]. [[6:18|And when the Lord our God shall give this liberty to his servants|Quum vero Deus noster hanc libertatem dederit servis suis]], that is, deliverance from the Assyrians, which we wish for thee and hope will come, [[6:18|let God be with thee also in the midst of us|sit et tecum Dominus in medio nostri]] by a special grace, [[6:18|that as it shall please thee, so thou with all thine mayst converse with us|ut sicut placuerit tibi, ita cum omnibus tuis converseris nobiscum]], that is, mayest live among us and receive the circumcision and observances of our law, if thou wilt. For the gentiles were not bound to the commandments of the law except the moral ones, with faith in Christ to come: but if they wished to share with the Jews in eating the paschal lamb and in certain other ceremonies of the law, they had first to be circumcised, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 12:43|This is the service of the Phase|Hæc est religio Phase]]: [[Ex 12:48|And if any stranger be willing to dwell among you|Si quis peregrinorum in vestram voluerit transire coloniam]], [[Ex 12:48|all his males shall first be circumcised|circumcidetur prius omne masculinum ejus]]: [[Ex 12:48|but if any man be uncircumcised, he shall not eat thereof|si quis autem circumcisus non fuerit, non vescetur ex eo]]. For as now no one is admitted to the sacraments of the law of the Gospel unless baptized, so neither then to the sacraments of the law of Moses unless circumcised.

paras.t: Tunc Ozias, finito consilio ejus, quo tractaverunt, quid in tam ardua causa eis restaret agendum, suscepit eum, videlicet Achior, in domum suam, et fecit cœnam magnam. Et vocatis omnibus presbyteris, hoc est senioribus seu sacerdotibus, simul, expleto jejunio, refecerunt. Postea convocatus est omnis populus, et per totam noctem intra ecclesiam, id est in synagoga, oraverunt. Habebant namque in singulis urbibus suis synagogas, in quibus vacabant orationi, devotioni, lectionique legis et prædicationi: et omnes pariter oraverunt, ut communis oratio exaudibilior esset. Non enim solet pia communitatis repelli oratio. Unde ad Corinthios ait Apostolus: Adjuvantibus vobis in oratione pro nobis, ut ex multarum personis facierum, ejus qui in nobis est donationis per multos gratiæ agantur pro nobis.
paras.en: [[6:19|Then Ozias, after the assembly was broken up|Tunc Ozias, finito consilio]] (the council, that is, in which they discussed what remained for them to do in so hard a case), [[6:19|received him into his house|suscepit eum, videlicet Achior, in domum suam]], namely Achior, [[6:19|and made him a great supper|et fecit cœnam magnam]]. [[6:20|And all the ancients were invited|Et vocatis omnibus presbyteris]], that is, the elders or priests, [[6:20|and they refreshed themselves together after their fast was over|simul, expleto jejunio, refecerunt]]. [[6:21|And afterwards all the people were called together, and they prayed all the night long within the church|Postea convocatus est omnis populus, et per totam noctem intra ecclesiam, id est in synagoga, oraverunt]] (*ecclesia*, that is, the synagogue). For they had synagogues in each of their cities, in which they gave themselves to prayer, devotion, the reading of the law and preaching: and they all prayed together, so that their common prayer might be the more readily heard. For the devout prayer of a community is not wont to be refused. Hence the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 1:11|You helping withal in prayer for us. That for this gift obtained for us, by the means of many persons, thanks may be given by many in our behalf|Adjuvantibus vobis in oratione pro nobis, ut ex multarum personis facierum, ejus qui in nobis est donationis per multos gratiæ agantur pro nobis]].

7.title: Explanatio capituli septimi: Holofernes autem altera die
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: But Holofernes on the next day

paras.t: Angustia et coarctatio filiorum Israel ex obsidione Assyriorum, hic describuntur.
paras.en: Here are described the distress and straits of the children of Israel from the siege of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Holofernes autem altera die, id est, die sequenti postquam tradidit ipsum Achior Israelitis, præcepit exercitibus suis. Fuit autem unus totalis exercitus, sicut et unus princeps militiæ, sed divisus fuit in aliquas turmas. Ut ascenderent contra Bethuliam, in alto inter montes locatam: ideo ait, Ascenderent. Voluitque statim indignationem, crudelitatem et comminationem suam implere. Indignanter quoque accepit, quod servi sui fuerunt a fundibulariis Israeliticis fugati. Erant autem pedites bellatorum centum viginti millia, et equites viginti duo millia. Supra legitur, quod erant duodecim millia equitum sagittariorum: ideo auctus videtur numerus equitum; vel equites non erant sagittarii omnes. Præter præparationes, id est præter turbam et numerum illorum virorum, quos occupaverat captivitas, id est, quos cepit et in auxiliarios sumpsit, et adducti fuerant de provinciis et urbibus universæ juventutis, id est omnium juvenum, quos sic in suum redegit obsequium. Omnes paraverunt se pariter ad pugnam contra filios Israel, et venerunt per crepidinem, id est summitatem seu extremitatem montis, usque ad apicem, id est summitatem loci, qui respicit super Dothain, hoc est locum seu oppidum sic vocatum, a loco qui dicitur Belma, usque ad Chelmon qui est contra Esdrelon.
paras.en: [[7:1|But Holofernes on the next day|Holofernes autem altera die]], that is, the day after he had handed Achior over to the Israelites, [[7:1|gave orders to his army|præcepit exercitibus suis]] [*exercitibus*, literally *armies*]. For there was one whole army, as there was one prince of the soldiery, but it was divided into several troops. [[7:1|to go up against Bethulia|Ut ascenderent contra Bethuliam]], which lay high up among the mountains: therefore he says *go up*. And he wished at once to fulfil his indignation, cruelty and threats; he also took it with indignation that his servants had been put to flight by the Israelite slingers. [[7:2|Now there were in his troops a hundred and twenty thousand footmen, and two and twenty thousand horsemen|Erant autem pedites bellatorum centum viginti millia, et equites viginti duo millia]]. Above it is read that there were twelve thousand archers on horseback[[Jdt 2:7||]]: so the number of horsemen seems to have been increased; or else the horsemen were not all archers. [[7:2|besides the preparations|Præter præparationes]], that is, besides the crowd and number [[7:2|of those men who had been taken|illorum virorum, quos occupaverat captivitas]], that is, whom he took and received as auxiliaries[[Jdt 3:8||]], [[7:2|and who had been brought away out of the provinces and cities of all the youth|et adducti fuerant de provinciis et urbibus universæ juventutis]], that is, of all the young men, whom he thus brought into his service. [[7:3|All these prepared themselves together to fight against the children of Israel|Omnes paraverunt se pariter ad pugnam contra filios Israel]], [[7:3|and they came by the hillside|et venerunt per crepidinem montis]], that is, by the summit or edge of the mountain, [[7:3|to the top|usque ad apicem]], that is, the summit of the place, [[7:3|which looketh toward Dothain|qui respicit super Dothain]], that is, a place or town so called, [[7:3|from the place which is called Belma, unto Chelmon, which is over against Esdrelon|a loco qui dicitur Belma, usque ad Chelmon qui est contra Esdrelon]].

paras.t: Filii autem Israel ut viderunt multitudinem illorum, quam in alto loco illo poterant cernere, prostraverunt se super terram, humiliter deprecantes divinum auxilium, sine quo sciverunt se nequaquam posse illis resistere, et nihilo minus quod in ipsis erat agentes, mittentes cinerem super capita sua, unanimes orantes, ut Deus Israel ostenderet misericordiam suam super populum suum. Et assumentes arma sua, sederunt per loca quæ angusti itineris tramitem, hoc est angustæ viæ callem compendiosum, dirigunt inter montosa, hoc est, inter loca montana ostendunt, sive rectificant; et erant custodientes ea, ne Assyrii per ea ad Bethuliam seu alia oppida sua possent accedere.
paras.en: [[7:4|But the children of Israel, when they saw the multitude of them|Filii autem Israel ut viderunt multitudinem illorum]], which they could see from that high place, [[7:4|prostrated themselves upon the ground|prostraverunt se super terram]], humbly begging for divine help, without which they knew they could by no means resist them, and nonetheless doing what was in them, [[7:4|putting ashes upon their heads, praying with one accord|mittentes cinerem super capita sua, unanimes orantes]], [[7:4|that the God of Israel would shew his mercy upon his people|ut Deus Israel ostenderet misericordiam suam super populum suum]]. [[7:5|And taking their arms of war|Et assumentes arma sua]], [[7:5|they posted themselves at the places, which by a narrow pathway lead directly between the mountains|sederunt per loca quæ ad angusti itineris tramitem dirigunt inter montosa]] (*pathway*, that is, the short track of a narrow way; *lead directly*, that is, show or make straight the way among the mountain places); [[7:5|and they guarded them|et erant custodientes ea]], so that the Assyrians could not reach Bethulia or their other towns through them.

paras.t: Porro Holofernes, dum circuivit per gyrum Bethuliæ a remoto, reperit quod fons influebat in aquæductum illorum qui in Bethulia erant, ad quos aqua fontis illius per aquæductum illum currebat. Hoc, ut Magister in historiis addit, invenit per aviculas quæ bibebant aquam de alveo, et per latentes rimulas aquæductus. Et incidi præcepit aquæductum illorum, ne per eum aqua in urbem illam decurreret. Erant tamen non longe ab urbe fontes, ex quibus cives Bethuliæ furtim, hoc est secrete, ne ab Assyriis notaretur, videbantur haurire aquam ad refocillandum ardorem et siccitatem sitis suæ, magis quam ad potandum. Sed filii Ammon et Moab, qui oderunt Israelitas, accesserunt ad Holofernem cupientes ei placere, et dixerunt: Filii Israel non in lancea, nec in sagitta confidunt, hoc est, tibi opponunt se, non ex confidentia armorum, sed locorum suorum. Ideo subditur: sed montes defendunt illos: quia propter loca illa montuosa difficile est illos accedere, et oporteret nos diu in obsidione manere; et muniunt, hoc est, protegunt ac confortant illos, colles in præcipitio, id est in magna altitudine, constituti. Ut ergo sine congressione pugnæ possis eos superare, pone custodes fontium, ut non hauriant ex eis, et sine gladio interficies eos; aut certe fatigati, tradent civitatem suam, quam putant, in montibus positam, superari non posse. Et placuerunt verba hæc coram Holoferne, et omnibus satellitibus ejus. Et constituit per gyrum centenarios per singulos fontes.
paras.en: [[7:6|Now Holofernes, in going round about|Porro Holofernes, dum circuivit per gyrum]] Bethulia at a distance, [[7:6|found that the fountain|reperit quod fons]] flowed into the aqueduct of those who were in Bethulia, to whom the water of that fountain ran through that aqueduct. This, as the Master adds in the Histories [Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*], he found out through the little birds that drank water from the channel, and through the hidden cracks of the aqueduct. [[7:6|and he commanded their aqueduct to be cut off|Et incidi præcepit aquæductum illorum]], so that no water should run down through it into that city. [[7:7|Nevertheless there were springs not far from the walls|Erant tamen non longe ab urbe fontes]], [[7:7|out of which they were seen secretly to draw water|ex quibus furtim videbantur haurire aquam]] (the citizens of Bethulia, *furtim*, that is, by stealth, so as not to be noticed by the Assyrians), [[7:7|to refresh themselves a little|ad refocillandum]] in the heat and dryness of their thirst, [[7:7|rather than to drink their fill|magis quam ad potandum]]. [[7:8|But the children of Ammon and Moab came to Holofernes|Sed filii Ammon et Moab, qui oderunt Israelitas, accesserunt ad Holofernem]], who hated the Israelites, wishing to please him, [[7:8|saying|et dixerunt]]: [[7:8|The children of Israel trust not in their spears, nor in their arrows|Filii Israel non in lancea, nec in sagitta confidunt]], that is, they set themselves against thee not out of confidence in arms but in their places. Hence it is added: [[7:8|but the mountains are their defence|sed montes defendunt illos]], because on account of those mountainous places it is hard to approach them, and we should have to remain long in the siege; [[7:8|and the steep hills and precipices guard them|et muniunt illos colles in præcipitio constituti]] (*muniunt*, that is, protect and strengthen them; *in præcipitio*, that is, at a great height). [[7:9|Wherefore that thou mayst overcome them without joining battle|Ut ergo sine congressione pugnæ possis eos superare]], [[7:9|set guards at the springs that they may not draw water out of them|pone custodes fontium, ut non hauriant ex eis]], [[7:9|and thou shalt destroy them without sword, or at least being wearied out they will yield up their city, which they suppose, because it is situate in the mountains, to be impregnable|et sine gladio interficies eos; aut certe fatigati, tradent civitatem suam, quam putant, in montibus positam, superari non posse]]. [[7:10|And these words pleased Holofernes, and his officers|Et placuerunt verba hæc coram Holoferne, et omnibus satellitibus ejus]], [[7:10|and he placed all round about a hundred men at every spring|Et constituit per gyrum centenarios per singulos fontes]].

paras.t: Quumque custodia ista fontium per dies viginti esset expleta, defecerunt cisternæ, hoc est aqua cisternarum, et collectiones aquarum, quæ ex fontibus solebant acquiri. Tunc ad Oziam congregati omnes viri, id est cives Bethuliæ, feminæque, juvenes et parvuli, omnes simul una voce dixerunt: Judicet Deus inter nos et te, hoc est, justitiam suam ostendat in eo qui inter nos culpam habet in causa hac, qui fecisti in nos mala, id est, afflictionem hanc induxisti super nos tuo consilio imprudenti, nolens loqui pacifice cum Assyriis, tractando cum eis, ut nos in servos susciperent. Et propter hoc vendidit nos Deus in manibus eorum, hoc est, propter istam rebellionem Deus jam quasi dedit nos potestati ipsorum, sicut res datur pro pretio. Et ideo non est qui adjuvet, quum prosternamur ante oculos eorum, id est, ipsis scientibus et nos circumvallantibus, corruamus in mortem, in siti, id est ex potus defectu, et perditione magna. Et nunc congregate universos qui in civitate sunt, ut sponte, hoc est sine diuturniore resistentia, tradamus nos Holoferni. Melius est enim ut captivi benedicamus Dominum viventes. Et sic habebant adhuc aliquam confidentiam evadendi mortem, si se traderent Holoferni. Parva tamen fuit spes ista. Quam moriamur, et simus opprobrium omni carni, quum videamus uxores nostras et infantes nostros mori ante oculos nostros. Contestamur hodie cælum et terram, hoc est, omnem creaturam, seu angelos et homines in testimonium sumimus, et cum attestatione tali rogamus. Contestamur quoque sic et Deum patrum nostrorum qui ulciscitur, id est, ulciscendo vitia nostra punit nos secundum peccata nostra, ut tradatis civitatem in manus militiæ Holofernis, ut sit finis noster, id est mors, brevis in ore gladii, qui longior efficitur in ariditate sitis.
paras.en: [[7:11|And when they had kept this watch for full twenty days|Quumque custodia ista fontium per dies viginti esset expleta]], [[7:11|the cisterns, and the reserve of waters failed|defecerunt cisternæ et collectiones aquarum]] (*cisternæ*, that is, the water of the cisterns), the reserves that used to be got from the springs. [[7:12|Then all the men|Tunc ad Oziam congregati omnes viri]], that is, the citizens of Bethulia, [[7:12|and women, young men, and children, gathering themselves together to Ozias, all together with one voice|feminæque, juvenes et parvuli, omnes simul una voce]], [[7:13|Said: God be judge between us and thee|dixerunt: Judicet Deus inter nos et te]], that is, may he show his justice upon the one among us who bears the blame in this matter, [[7:13|for thou hast done evil against us|qui fecisti in nos mala]], that is, thou hast brought this affliction upon us by thy imprudent counsel, [[7:13|in that thou wouldst not speak peaceably with the Assyrians|nolens loqui pacifice cum Assyriis]], treating with them so that they would receive us as servants. [[7:13|and for this cause God hath sold us into their hands|Et propter hoc vendidit nos Deus in manibus eorum]], that is, because of this rebellion God has now as it were given us into their power, as a thing is given for a price. [[7:14|And therefore there is no one to help us, while we are cast down before their eyes|Et ideo non est qui adjuvet, quum prosternamur ante oculos eorum]], that is, while they know it and hem us in, we sink into death, [[7:14|in thirst|in siti]], that is, from want of drink, [[7:14|and sad destruction|et perditione magna]]. [[7:15|And now assemble ye all that are in the city, that we may of our own accord|Et nunc congregate universos qui in civitate sunt, ut sponte]], that is, without longer resistance, [[7:15|yield ourselves|tradamus nos]] to Holofernes. [[7:16|For it is better, that being captives we should live and bless the Lord|Melius est enim ut captivi benedicamus Dominum viventes]]. And so they still had some confidence of escaping death if they gave themselves up to Holofernes; but that hope was small. [[7:16|than that we should die, and be a reproach to all flesh, after we have seen our wives and our infants die before our eyes|Quam moriamur, et simus opprobrium omni carni, quum videamus uxores nostras et infantes nostros mori ante oculos nostros]]. [[7:17|We call to witness this day heaven and earth|Contestamur hodie cælum et terram]], that is, we take all creation, or angels and men, to witness, and with such an attestation we beg; we call to witness thus also [[7:17|the God of our fathers, who taketh vengeance|et Deum patrum nostrorum qui ulciscitur]], that is, who in avenging our vices punishes us [[7:17|according to our sins|secundum peccata nostra]], [[7:17|to deliver now the city into the hand of the army of Holofernes|ut tradatis civitatem in manus militiæ Holofernis]], [[7:17|that our end may be short by the edge of the sword|ut sit finis noster, id est mors, brevis in ore gladii]], that is, our death, [[7:17|which is made longer by the drought of thirst|qui longior efficitur in ariditate sitis]].

paras.t: Et quum hæc dixissent, factus est fletus et ululatus magnus in ecclesia ab omnibus, et per multas horas una voce clamaverunt ad Dominum, dicentes: Peccavimus, injuste egimus. Tu qui pius es, in tuo flagello vindica iniquitates nostras, hoc est, per te ipsum seu angelico ministerio corrige nos, et noli tradere confitentes te, id est nos fideles qui te confitemur verum Deum, populo qui ignorat te. Juxta hunc modum dixit rex David: Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim sunt miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum. Ut non dicant inter gentes, id est, ne increduli inter se dicant: Ubi est Deus eorum? id est, jam apparet quod Deus eorum non curat de eis, non potest eis auxiliari. Ac si dicant: Pro tuo honore zelamus, et si non vis nos exaudire propter nos, saltem propter te ipsum et tui ipsius honorem et gloriam nos exaudi, ne blasphemeris a perfidis et iniquis: sicut per Isaiam testatus est, Propter me faciam, ut non blasphemer. In Ezechiele quoque: Non propter vos ego faciam: notum sit vobis: sed propter nomen sanctum meum.
paras.en: [[7:18|And when they had said these things, there was great weeping and lamentation of all in the assembly|Et quum hæc dixissent, factus est fletus et ululatus magnus in ecclesia ab omnibus]], [[7:18|and for many hours with one voice they cried to God, saying|et per multas horas una voce clamaverunt ad Dominum, dicentes]]: [[7:19|We have sinned|Peccavimus]], [[7:19|we have done unjustly|injuste egimus]]. Thou, [[7:20|because thou art good|Tu qui pius es]] [Denis passes over *miserere nostri, aut*, have mercy on us, or], [[7:20|punish our iniquities by chastising us thyself|in tuo flagello vindica iniquitates nostras]], that is, correct us by thyself or by the ministry of angels, [[7:20|and deliver not them that trust in thee|et noli tradere confitentes te]] [*confitentes te*, those who confess thee], that is, us the faithful who confess thee to be the true God, [[7:20|to a people that knoweth not thee|populo qui ignorat te]]. In this way King David said: [[2 Kings 24:14|it is better that I should fall into the hands of the Lord (for his mercies are many) than into the hands of men|Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim sunt miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum]]. [[7:21|That they may not say among the Gentiles|Ut non dicant inter gentes]], that is, lest the unbelievers say among themselves: [[7:21|Where is their God?|Ubi est Deus eorum?]] that is, it is now plain that their God does not care for them, cannot help them. As if they said: We are zealous for thy honour; and if thou wilt not hear us for our sakes, at least for thine own sake, and for thine own honour and glory, hear us, lest thou be blasphemed by the faithless and the wicked: as he testified through Isaias: [[Is 48:11|for my own sake will I do it, that I may not be blasphemed|Propter me faciam, ut non blasphemer]]. And in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:32|It is not for your sakes that I will do this|Non propter vos ego faciam]]: [[Ezech 36:32|be it known to you|notum sit vobis]]: [[Ezech 36:22|but for my holy name's sake|sed propter nomen sanctum meum]].

paras.t: Et quum fatigati his clamoribus, et his fletibus lassati siluissent, exsurgens Ozias infusus lacrimis, dixit: Æquo animo estote, fratres, sperando in Domino, et hos quinque dies exspectemus a Domino misericordiam. Ideo exprimit, Quinque dies, quoniam aqua quam habebant, quæ vix per unam diem suffecit ad satietatem, non videbatur ultra quinque dies posse servire, quamvis parcissime sumpta. Forsan enim indignationem suam abscindet, et dabit gloriam nomini suo. Si autem transactis quinque diebus non venerit adjutorium nobis a Deo, faciemus hæc verba quæ locuti estis, urbem tradendo. De hac præfixione quinque dierum reprehenditur iste Ozias sequenti capitulo, ut ibi patebit.
paras.en: [[7:22|And when being wearied with these cries, and tired with these weepings, they held their peace|Et quum fatigati his clamoribus, et his fletibus lassati siluissent]], [[7:23|Ozias rising up all in tears, said: Be of good courage, my brethren|exsurgens Ozias infusus lacrimis, dixit: Æquo animo estote, fratres]], hoping in the Lord, [[7:23|and let us wait these five days for mercy from the Lord|et hos quinque dies exspectemus a Domino misericordiam]]. He names *five days* because the water they had, which scarcely sufficed for one day to satisfy them, did not seem able to serve beyond five days, though taken most sparingly. [[7:24|For perhaps he will put a stop to his indignation, and will give glory to his own name|Forsan enim indignationem suam abscindet, et dabit gloriam nomini suo]]. [[7:25|But if after five days be past there come no aid|Si autem transactis quinque diebus non venerit adjutorium]] for us from God, [[7:25|we will do the things which you have spoken|faciemus hæc verba quæ locuti estis]], by surrendering the city. For this fixing of five days this Ozias is rebuked in the following chapter, as will be seen there.

8.title: Declaratio capituli octavi: Et factum est
8.title_en: Declaration of the eighth chapter: Now it came to pass

paras.t: Exhortatio, oratio et consilium venerabilis viduæ Judith, hic referuntur.
paras.en: Here are related the exhortation, the prayer and the counsel of the venerable widow Judith.

paras.t: Et factum est quum audisset hæc verba Oziæ, qui dixit quod traderet urbem post quinque dies, nisi interim veniret auxilium, Judith vidua de tribu Ruben, etc., cujus stirps in textu describitur. Et vir ejus Manasses in diebus messis mortuus est. Venit enim æstus super caput ejus, ex quo ardore solis fuit intus accensus, et ægritudinem incurrit letalem, sicut et quarto Regum legitur de filio Sunamitis suscitato per Eliseum; et sepultus est cum patribus suis. Erat autem Judith relicta ejus vidua jam annis tribus et mensibus sex. Voluit enim deinceps in viduali castimonia Deo servire.
paras.en: [[8:1|Now it came to pass, when Judith a widow had heard these words|Et factum est cum audisset hæc verba Judith vidua]] [the words *hæc verba* are garbled in the OCR] of Ozias, who said that he would deliver up the city after five days unless help came in the meantime, Judith, a widow of the tribe of Ruben, etc., whose lineage is described in the text. [[8:2|And her husband was Manasses|Et vir ejus Manasses]], [[8:2|who died in the time of the barley harvest|in diebus messis mortuus est]]. [[8:3|and the heat came upon his head|Venit enim æstus super caput ejus]], from which heat of the sun he was inflamed within and fell into a deadly sickness, as we read too in the fourth book of Kings of the Sunamitess's son, who was raised up by Eliseus[[4 Kings 4:19||]]; [[8:3|and was buried there with his fathers|et sepultus est cum patribus suis]]. [[8:4|And Judith his relict was a widow now three years and six months.|Erat autem Judith relicta ejus vidua jam annis tribus et mensibus sex]] For she wished from then on to serve God in the chastity of widowhood.

paras.t: Et in superioribus domus suæ fecit sibi cubiculum secretum, et in ipso cubiculo oratorium, ut sequenti patet capitulo; et camerula illa fuit etiam oratorium ejus, in quo cum puellis, id est ancillis, aut cognatis, clausa morabatur: ita quod raro exivit domum, soli Deo vacans in loco abstracto, et virorum vitans adspectus, familiaritates, colloquia, convivia, et ceteras lasciviæ occasiones, non solum ne ipsa ad carnalia incitaretur, sed ne appeteretur ab aliis; et habens super lumbos suos cilicium, pro carnis edomatione, majorisque gratiæ impetratione, jejunabat omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, quibus in viduitate permansit. Maritatis autem mulieribus non liceret sic jejunare sine consensu mariti. Præter sabbata et neomenias, hoc est exordia mensium, quia in primo die cujuslibet mensis fuit quædam festivitas legis, ut in Levitico et Deuteronomio patet; unde in Psalmo: Buccinate in neomenia tuba, in insigni die solennitatis vestræ. Et festa domus Israel, scilicet festa, Paschale et Tabernaculorum, et Hebdomadarum seu Pentecostes, quæ erant festa legis præcipua.
paras.en: [[8:5|And she made herself a private chamber in the upper part of her house|Et in superioribus domus suæ fecit sibi cubiculum secretum]], and in that chamber an oratory, as is plain from the following chapter[[Jdt 9:1||]]; and that little room was also her oratory, [[8:5|in which she abode shut up with her maids|in quo cum puellis suis clausa morabatur]], that is, handmaids, or kinswomen: so that she seldom went out of the house, giving herself to God alone in a withdrawn place, and shunning the sight of men, their familiarity, conversation and banquets, and the other occasions of wantonness, not only lest she herself should be stirred to carnal things, but lest she should be desired by others; [[8:6|And she wore haircloth upon her loins|et habens super lumbos suos cilicium]], to tame the flesh and to obtain greater grace, [[8:6|and fasted all the days of her life|jejunabat omnibus diebus vitæ suæ]] in which she remained a widow. But it would not be lawful for married women to fast so without their husband's consent. [[8:6|except the sabbaths, and new moons|Præter sabbata et neomenias]], that is, the beginnings of the months, since on the first day of every month there was a feast of the law[[Num 28:11||]], as is plain in Leviticus and Deuteronomy; hence in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:4|Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, on the noted day of your solemnity.|Buccinate in neomenia tuba, in insigni die solennitatis vestræ]] [[8:6|and the feasts of the house of Israel|Et festa domus Israel]], namely the feasts of the Pasch, of Tabernacles, and of Weeks or Pentecost, which were the chief feasts of the law.

paras.t: Erat autem eleganti, id est venusto, aspectu nimis, habens pulchritudinem corporalem, moralem et spiritualem. Cui vir suus reliquerat divitias multas et familiam copiosam: sicque ejus continentia fuit magna, et multum laudabilis, quia inter tot incitamenta libidinis, quæ sunt, juventus, pulchritudo, opulentia, et multitudo virorum præsentium, mansit tam casta. Et hæc erat in omnibus famosissima, quoniam timebat Dominum valde, filiali timore, qui perfectam et fervidam caritatem includit, facitque hominem coram Deo custoditum, sollicitum, et irreprehensibiliter conversantem: quia, ut Salomon loquitur, Qui timet Deum, nihil negligit. Nec erat qui loqueretur de illa verbum malum: quia Deo atque hominibus ex sua exemplari et sancta complacuit vita. Tales quoque erant beatissimi Joannis Baptistæ parentes, incedentes in omnibus justificationibus Domini sine querela.
paras.en: [[8:7|And she was exceedingly beautiful|Erat autem eleganti aspectu nimis]], having beauty of body, of character and of spirit. [[8:7|and her husband left her great riches, and very many servants|Cui vir suus reliquerat divitias multas et familiam copiosam]]: and so her continence was great and much to be praised, since amid so many incitements to lust, namely youth, beauty, wealth and a multitude of men about her, she remained so chaste. [[8:8|And she was greatly renowned among all|Et hæc erat in omnibus famosissima]], [[8:8|because she feared the Lord very much|quoniam timebat Dominum valde]], with filial fear, which includes perfect and fervent charity, and makes a man watchful and careful before God, and living blamelessly[[1 Tim 5:7||]]: for, as Solomon says, [[Eccles 7:19|he that feareth God, neglecteth nothing|Qui timet Deum, nihil negligit]]. [[8:8|neither was there any one that spoke an ill word of her|Nec erat qui loqueretur de illa verbum malum]]: for she pleased God and men by her exemplary and holy life. Such too were the parents of the most blessed John the Baptist, [[Luke 1:6|walking in all the commandments and justifications of the Lord without blame|incedentes in omnibus justificationibus Domini sine querela]].

paras.t: Hæc itaque quum audisset, hoc est, sedens in domo sua percepisset, quoniam Ozias promisisset, quod transacta quinta die traderet civitatem Assyriis: quia ut apparet, non aderat quando Ozias protulit ea. Nam subditur: misit ad presbyteros Chabri et Charmi, ut venirent ad se, quia invita processit in publicum. Et venerunt ad illam, et dixit illis: Quod est verbum, in quo consensit Ozias, ut tradat civitatem Assyriis, si intra quinque dies non venerit vobis adjutorium? quasi dicat, Illicitum est. Cur non direxit sermonem ad Oziam? Ad hoc aliqui dicunt quod nondum erat præsens: quibus objici potest, quod infra in isto capitulo Ozias et presbyteri leguntur ei pariter respondisse. Ad quod dici potest, quod interim forsan advenit. Vel si cum presbyteris venit, tamen presbyteros primo affatur, quoniam sacerdotum fuit etiam ipsum Oziam super hoc increpare.
paras.en: [[8:9|When therefore she had heard|Hæc itaque quum audisset]], that is, when, sitting in her house, she had learned, [[8:9|that Ozias had promised|quoniam Ozias promisisset]] [[8:9|that he would deliver up the city after the fifth day|quod transacta quinta die traderet civitatem]] to the Assyrians: for, as it appears, she was not present when Ozias said it. For it is added: [[8:9|she sent to the ancients Chabri and Charmi|misit ad presbyteros Chabri et Charmi]], that they should come to her, because she went out in public unwillingly. [[8:10|And they came to her, and she said to them|Et venerunt ad illam, et dixit illis]]: [[8:10|What is this word, by which Ozias hath consented to give up the city to the Assyrians, if within five days there come no aid to us?|Quod est verbum, in quo consensit Ozias, ut tradat civitatem Assyriis, si intra quinque dies non venerit vobis adjutorium?]] As if to say: it is unlawful. Why did she not direct her speech to Ozias? To this some say that he was not yet present; against whom it can be objected that further on in this chapter Ozias and the ancients are read to have answered her together[[8:28||]]. To which it can be said that perhaps he arrived meanwhile. Or, if he came with the ancients, she still addresses the ancients first, since it belonged to the priests to rebuke Ozias himself too in this matter.

paras.t: Et qui estis vos qui tentatis Dominum? quasi dicat: Merito essetis nimis prudentes ad hoc, nec aliquo modo vos decet. Non est iste sermo qui misericordiam provocet, id est exauditionem mereatur a pietate divina; sed potius qui iram excitet, et furorem accendat, id est, rigorem divinæ mereatur justitiæ in vindicta: quia tentare Deum, est grave peccatum. Nempe præfigere tempus, infra quod, si Deus non subvenerit, cessetur ab ejus invocatione contra perfidos, est infra tempus propria libertate determinatum velle experiri divini succursum subsidii, alioqui incredulis subjugari, etiam in destructionem cultus divini: quemadmodum fuit in isto casu. Si enim adversarii obtinuissent Bethuliam, de facili obtinuissent ac destruxissent Jerusalem. Et si objiciatur, quod Jeremias propheta consuluit Sedeciæ regi, ut traderet urbem Jerusalem Nabuchodonosor regi: dicendum, quod consuluit hoc, non in destructionem urbis et templi ac cultus divini, sed pro conservatione illorum, quia sciebat quod civitas et templum destruerentur a Chaldæis, nisi sponte eisdem traderentur.
paras.en: [[8:11|And who are you that tempt the Lord?|Et qui estis vos qui tentatis Dominum?]] As if to say: you would need to be very wise indeed for this [so the OCR reads; the sense seems ironic], and in no way does it become you. [[8:12|This is not a word that may draw down mercy|Non est iste sermo qui misericordiam provocet]], that is, that may merit a hearing from the divine goodness, [[8:12|but rather that may stir up wrath, and enkindle indignation|sed potius qui iram excitet, et furorem accendat]], that is, that may merit the rigour of the divine justice in punishment: for to tempt God is a grave sin. For to fix a time within which, if God has not come to help, one will cease to call upon Him against the faithless, is to wish to test the help of divine succour within a time determined by one's own choice, or else to be subjected to unbelievers, even to the destruction of the divine worship, as it would have been in this case. For if the enemy had taken Bethulia, they would easily have taken and destroyed Jerusalem. And if it be objected that the prophet Jeremias counselled king Sedecias to deliver up the city of Jerusalem to king Nabuchodonosor[[Jer 38:17||]], it must be said that he counselled this not for the destruction of the city and the temple and the divine worship, but for their preservation, since he knew that the city and the temple would be destroyed by the Chaldeans unless they were handed over to them of their own accord.

paras.t: Posuistis vos tempus miserationis Domini, hoc est tempus infra quod Deus clementer subveniat, et in arbitrio, id est judicio vestro, diem constituistis ei. Sed quia patiens est Dominus, id est longanimiter ferens offensam, non statim ulciscens. Patientia autem et virtutes morales quæ circa passiones versantur, non competunt Deo quoad passionum ordinationem, sed quantum ad operis conformitatem. In hoc ipso, id est de culpa hac, pœniteamus: et ex humilitate connumerat se eis, qui rei erant in illo peccato; et indulgentiam ejus cum lacrimis postulemus, ut sit vera contritio ex intimo cordis fundo proveniens. Sic enim placatur inveniturque Deus, juxta illud Deuteronomii: Quum quæsieris Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ. Non enim quasi homo, Deus sic comminabitur, id est non ex impetu passionis, neque ut mox inferat ultionem, neque sicut filius hominis ad iracundiam provocabitur, quum sit simplicissima et prorsus immaterialissima mens invariabilis in æternum. Qui per Malachiam protestatur: Ego Dominus, et non mutor. De quo et Balaam loquitur: Non est Deus quasi homo ut mentiatur, nec ut filius hominis ut mutetur.
paras.en: [[8:13|You have set a time for the mercy of the Lord|Posuistis vos tempus miserationis Domini]], that is, a time within which God is graciously to come to your help, [[8:13|and you have appointed him a day, according to your pleasure|et in arbitrium vestrum, diem constituistis ei]], that is, by your own judgment. [[8:14|But forasmuch as the Lord is patient|Sed quia patiens est Dominus]], that is, bearing offence long-sufferingly and not avenging it at once[[Job 35:15||]]. Now patience and the moral virtues that are concerned with the passions do not belong to God as regards the ordering of passions, but as regards a likeness in the work. [[8:14|let us be penitent for this same thing|in hoc ipso pœniteamus]], that is, for this fault: and out of humility she numbers herself with those who were guilty of that sin; [[8:14|and with many tears let us beg his pardon|et indulgentiam ejus cum lacrimis postulemus]], so that there may be true contrition coming from the inmost depth of the heart. For so God is appeased and found, according to that saying of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:29|when thou shalt seek there the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him: yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, and all the affliction of thy soul|Quum quæsieris Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ]]. [[8:15|For God will not threaten like man|Non enim quasi homo, Deus sic comminabitur]], that is, not from the impulse of passion, nor so as to bring vengeance at once, [[8:15|nor be inflamed to anger like the son of man|neque sicut filius hominis ad iracundiam provocabitur]], since He is a mind most simple and utterly immaterial, unchangeable for ever. He declares by Malachias: [[Mal 3:6|I am the Lord, and I change not|Ego Dominus, et non mutor]]. Of Him Balaam too says: [[Num 23:19|God is not a man, that he should lie, nor is the son of man, that he should be changed|Non est Deus quasi homo ut mentiatur, nec ut filius hominis ut mutetur]].

paras.t: Et ideo humiliemus illi animas nostras, id est, ad Dei honorem, recognoscamus humiliter proprias culpas. Et in spiritu contrito, hoc est corde compuncto, et humiliato servientes illi: quia ait per Isaiam: Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos? Dicamus flentes Domino, ut secundum suam voluntatem sic faciat nobiscum misericordiam suam. Hoc enim Deo gratissimum est, ut rationalis creatura propriam voluntatem plenarie Creatori suo resignet, mactet et offerat. Sic namque Christus passione instante exorans, Non mea, inquit, sed tua voluntas fiat. Ut sicut cor nostrum conturbatum est, hoc est, vehementer perterritum, contristatum, afflictum, in superbia eorum, id est ex ambitiosa et arroganti invasione, comminatione, obsidione Assyriorum istorum; ita de nostra humilitate gloriemur in Domino, hoc est de liberatione nostra humiliter postulata a Deo; quoniam non sumus secuti peccata patrum nostrorum, qui dereliquerunt Deum suum, idola adorando, sanguinem innocentem fundendo, aut occidendo Prophetas, aut consimilia perpetrando facinora: ideo merito in Deo nostro confidimus, quod ab hostibus istis nos eruet. Sicque verba hæc protulit Judith, non populum suum laudando simpliciter, sed ad augendum sibi ac populo spem in Deo, sicut et Ezechias angustiatus a rege Assyriorum, invocans Dominum: Obsecro, ait, memento quomodo coram te ambulaverim in veritate et corde perfecto. Pro quo scelere dati sunt in gladium, et in rapinam, et in confusionem inimicis suis. Nos autem alterum Deum nescimus per fidem et cultum, præter ipsum: quia nec alius Deus est.
paras.en: [[8:16|And therefore let us humble our souls before him|Et ideo humiliemus illi animas nostras]], that is, let us humbly acknowledge our own faults, to the honour of God. [[8:16|and continuing in an humble spirit, in his service|et in spiritu constituti humiliato, servientes illi]] [Denis reads *in spiritu contrito*, “in a contrite spirit”, glossed “with a compunct heart”; the margin gives *constituti*, “continuing”, as in the Vulgate]: for He says by Isaias: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos?]] [[8:17|Let us ask the Lord with tears, that according to his will so he would shew his mercy to us|Dicamus flentes Domino, ut secundum suam voluntatem sic faciat nobiscum misericordiam suam]]. For this is most pleasing to God, that the rational creature should fully resign, sacrifice and offer its own will to its Creator. For so Christ, praying as His passion drew near, said: [[Luke 22:42|not my will, but thine be done|Non mea, inquit, sed tua voluntas fiat]]. [[8:17|that as our heart is troubled|Ut sicut cor nostrum conturbatum est]], that is, greatly terrified, saddened and afflicted, [[8:17|by their pride|in superbia eorum]], that is, by the ambitious and arrogant invasion, threats and siege of these Assyrians, [[8:17|so also we may glorify in our humility|ita de nostra humilitate gloriemur]] in the Lord, that is, in our deliverance humbly asked of God; [[8:18|For we have not followed the sins of our fathers, who forsook their God|quoniam non sumus secuti peccata patrum nostrorum, qui dereliquerunt Deum suum]] by worshipping idols, shedding innocent blood, or slaying the Prophets, or committing like crimes: therefore we rightly trust in our God that He will deliver us from these enemies. And so Judith spoke these words not simply to praise her people, but to increase her own and the people's hope in God; as Ezechias too, in distress from the king of the Assyrians, calling upon the Lord, says: [[4 Kings 20:3|I beseech thee, O Lord, remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart|Obsecro, ait, memento quomodo coram te ambulaverim in veritate et corde perfecto]]. [[8:19|For which crime they were given up to their enemies, to the sword, and to pillage, and to confusion|Pro quo scelere dati sunt in gladium, et in rapinam, et in confusionem inimicis suis]] [these words are garbled in the OCR and are read with the Vulgate]. [[8:19|but we know no other God|Nos autem alterum Deum nescimus]] by faith and worship [[8:19|but him|præter ipsum]]: for there is no other God.

paras.t: Exspectemus humiles consolationem ejus. Non enim repellet in sempiternum Dominus: quia si abjecit, et miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum, ut in Threnis loquitur Jeremias. Et exquiret sanguinem nostrum de afflictionibus inimicorum nostrorum, hoc est, tribulationes nobis illatas ab hostibus, vindicabit in ipsis, eos affligendo, ut justum est; et humiliabit, id est dejiciet, omnes gentes quæ insurgunt contra nos, et faciet illas sine honore Dominus Deus noster. Hæc fuerunt verba bonæ fiduciæ, non prophetiæ, ut æstimatur, quamvis paulo post evenerint.
paras.en: [[8:20|Let us humbly wait for his consolation|Exspectemus humiles consolationem ejus]]. [[Lam 3:31|For the Lord will not cast off for ever|Non enim repellet in sempiternum Dominus]]: [[Lam 3:32|For if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies|quia si abjecit, et miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum]], as Jeremias says in the Lamentations. [[8:20|will require our blood of the afflictions of our enemies|Et exquiret sanguinem nostrum de afflictionibus inimicorum nostrorum]], that is, He will avenge on them the tribulations brought on us by the enemy, by afflicting them, as is just; [[8:20|and he will humble all the nations that shall rise up against us|et humiliabit, id est dejiciet, omnes gentes quæ insurgunt contra nos]], that is, cast them down, [[8:20|and bring them to disgrace|et faciet illas sine honore]], [[8:20|the Lord our God|Dominus Deus noster]]. These were words of good confidence, not of prophecy, as it is thought, although they came to pass a little later.

paras.t: Et nunc, fratres, quoniam vos estis presbyteri in populo Dei, hoc est sacerdotes et seniores, et ex vobis pendet anima illorum, id est, salus et prosperitas animarum ipsorum ex vestra salubri eruditione, virtuosaque conversatione, pro magna parte dependet: juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea. Hinc per Jeremiam Dominus asserit: Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Ad eloquium vestrum corda illorum erigite, hoc est, vestra salubri exhortatione corda ipsorum ad Deum reducite, ut confidant in ipso; memores sint quia tentati sunt patres nostri, id est multipliciter impugnati ab invisibilibus ac visibilibus inimicis, ut probarentur, si vere colerent Deum suum, id est, quatenus per adversa pateret, an Deo constanter atque fideliter adhærerent. Unde et in libro Judicum legitur: Dimisit Dominus Chananæos, ut in eis experiretur Israelem, utrum audiret mandata Domini, an non.
paras.en: [[8:21|And now, brethren, as you are the ancients among the people of God|Et nunc, fratres, quoniam vos estis presbyteri in populo Dei]], that is, priests and elders, [[8:21|and their very soul resteth upon you|et ex vobis pendet anima illorum]], that is, the salvation and welfare of their souls depends in great part on your wholesome teaching and virtuous life: according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 10:2|what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea]]. Hence by Jeremias the Lord declares: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly, and have not sought the Lord|Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. [[8:21|comfort their hearts by your speech|Ad eloquium vestrum corda illorum erigite]], that is, by your wholesome exhortation bring their hearts back to God, so that they trust in Him; [[8:21|that they may be mindful how our fathers were tempted|memores sint quia tentati sunt patres nostri]], that is, assailed in many ways by invisible and visible enemies, [[8:21|that they might be proved|ut probarentur]], [[8:21|whether they worshipped their God truly|si vere colerent Deum suum]], that is, so that it might appear through adversity whether they would cleave to God constantly and faithfully. Hence we read in the book of Judges too: The Lord left the Chanaanites, [[Judg 3:4|that he might try Israel by them, whether they would hear the commandments of the Lord|ut in eis experiretur Israelem, utrum audiret mandata Domini]], [[Judg 3:4|or not|an non]].

paras.t: Memores esse debent, quoniam pater noster Abraham tentatus est: juxta illud, Tentavit Deus Abraham; et per multas tribulationes probatus, Dei amicus effectus est. Nam ex caristia perrexit ex terra Chanaan in Ægyptum, et ibi ablata est ei propria uxor, et puteos ejus abstulerunt aut repleverunt Palæstini: quæ omnia leguntur in Genesi. Sic Isaac, qui exhibuit se paratum ut offerretur Deo in holocaustum. Sic Jacob, et Moyses, et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Sic ait Paulus: Quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cælorum. Illi autem qui tentationes non susceperunt cum timore Domini, id est, qui adversitates et impugnationes non toleraverunt patienter ac timorate, aut pravis suggestionibus non restiterunt idonee, et impatientiam suam et improperium murmurationis suæ contra Deum protulerunt, adversus ipsum murmurando, seu ipsum tentando, aut culpam retorquendo in ipsum, exterminati sunt ab exterminatore, id est, interfecti Deo præcipiente, et ejus sententiam angelo bono aut malo exsequente. Etenim in Numeris perversi filii Israel leguntur dixisse: Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto; utinam pereamus, et non inducat nos Dominus in terram istam, ne cadamus gladio. Propter quod in Deuteronomio Moyses loquitur eis: Noluistis ascendere, sed increduli ad sermonem Domini murmurati estis atque dixistis: Odit nos Dominus. Hinc Dominus dixit ad Moysen: Usquequo multitudo hæc pessima murmurat contra me? In solitudine hac jacebunt cadavera vestra. Et a serpentibus perierunt: secundum illud Numerorum, Immisit Dominus in populum ignitos serpentes. Ab infernalibus quoque serpentibus tales peccando spiritualiter necabantur.
paras.en: [[8:22|They must remember how our father Abraham was tempted|Memores esse debent, quoniam pater noster Abraham tentatus est]], according to that saying, [[Gen 22:1|God tempted Abraham|Tentavit Deus Abraham]]; [[8:22|and being proved by many tribulations, was made the friend of God|et per multas tribulationes probatus, Dei amicus effectus est]]. For because of a famine he went from the land of Chanaan into Egypt[[Gen 12:10||]], and there his own wife was taken from him[[Gen 12:15||]], and the Philistines took away or filled up his wells[[Gen 26:15||]]: all of which we read in Genesis. [[8:23|So Isaac|Sic Isaac]], who showed himself ready to be offered to God as a holocaust[[Gen 22:9||]]. [[8:23|so Jacob|Sic Jacob]], [[8:23|so Moses, and all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|et Moyses, et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. So Paul says: [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cælorum]] [Denis has *regnum cælorum*, “the kingdom of heaven”]. [[8:24|But they that did not receive the trials with the fear of the Lord|Illi autem qui tentationes non susceperunt cum timore Domini]], that is, who did not bear adversities and assaults patiently and with fear, or did not resist wicked suggestions as they should, [[8:24|but uttered their impatience and the reproach of their murmuring against the Lord|et impatientiam suam et improperium murmurationis suæ contra Deum protulerunt]], by murmuring against Him, or tempting Him, or throwing the blame back on Him, [[8:25|Were destroyed by the destroyer|exterminati sunt ab exterminatore]], that is, were slain at God's command, an angel, good or bad, carrying out His sentence. For in Numbers the perverse children of Israel are read to have said: [[Num 14:3|Would God that we had died in Egypt|Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto]]; [[Num 14:3|and would God we may die|utinam pereamus]], [[Num 14:3|and that the Lord may not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword|et non inducat nos Dominus in terram istam, ne cadamus gladio]]. Wherefore in Deuteronomy Moses says to them: [[Deut 1:26|And you would not go up, but being incredulous to the word of the Lord|Noluistis ascendere, sed increduli ad sermonem Domini]], [[Deut 1:27|You murmured|murmurati estis]], [[Deut 1:27|and said: The Lord hateth us|atque dixistis: Odit nos Dominus]]. Hence the Lord said to Moses: [[Num 14:27|How long doth this wicked multitude murmur against me?|Usquequo multitudo hæc pessima murmurat contra me?]] [[Num 14:29|In the wilderness shall your carcasses lie|In solitudine hac jacebunt cadavera vestra]]. [[8:25|and perished by serpents|Et a serpentibus perierunt]]: according to that saying of Numbers, [[Num 21:6|the Lord sent among the people fiery serpents|Immisit Dominus in populum ignitos serpentes]]. And such men, by sinning, were also slain spiritually by the serpents of hell.

paras.t: Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur, ex impatientia aut diffidentia; nec peccemus in Deum, contra ipsum murmurando, seu quasi volendo vindicare injurias nostras per offensam et inhonorationem ipsius Dei, derogando justitiæ ejus, aut adscribendo ei impatienter nostras miserias; sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse (ita ut fateamur ex corde, quod peccando meruimus pati adversa his graviora), flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur a Domino, id est castigationes istas Deo permittente aut ordinante atque volente nobis inflictas, ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus: ut scilicet per temporales pœnas purgati, tormenta evadamus æterna: vel etiam a præsenti persecutione eripiamur, Dominum invocando, et quæ illata sunt, æquanimiter sustinendo.
