paras.en: [[8:26|As for us therefore let us not revenge ourselves for these things which we suffer|Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur]], out of impatience or distrust; nor let us sin against God by murmuring against Him, or as though wishing to avenge our wrongs by offending and dishonouring God Himself, by detracting from His justice, or impatiently ascribing our miseries to Him; [[8:27|But esteeming these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve|sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse]] (so that we confess from the heart that by sinning we have deserved to suffer adversities heavier than these), let us believe that [[8:27|these scourges of the Lord|flagella Domini]], [[8:27|with which like servants we are chastised|quasi servi qui corripimur]] by the Lord, that is, these chastisements inflicted on us by God's permission, or ordering and will, [[8:27|have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction|ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse]]: namely, that being purged by temporal punishments we may escape eternal torments; or even that we may be delivered from the present persecution, by calling upon the Lord and bearing with equanimity what has been brought upon us.

paras.t: Et dixerunt illi Ozias et presbyteri, qui exhortationem et increpationem feminæ patienter et humiliter susceperunt propter virtuositatem ipsius: quia et ipsa ex zelo justitiæ, caritatis fervore, et ex inspiratione divina humiliter, non jactanter, fuit locuta: Omnia quæ locuta es, vera sunt, et non est in sermonibus tuis ulla reprehensio. Nunc ora pro nobis Dominum, quoniam mulier sancta es et timens Deum.
paras.en: [[8:28|And Ozias and the ancients said to her|Et dixerunt illi Ozias et presbyteri]], who received the woman's exhortation and rebuke patiently and humbly because of her virtue: for she too had spoken from zeal for justice, from the fervour of charity and by divine inspiration, humbly and not boastfully: [[8:28|All things which thou hast spoken are true, and there is nothing to be reprehended in thy words|Omnia quæ locuta es, vera sunt, et non est in sermonibus tuis ulla reprehensio]]. [[8:29|Now therefore pray for us|Nunc ora pro nobis Dominum]], [[8:29|for thou art a holy woman, and one fearing God|quoniam mulier sancta es et timens Deum]].

paras.t: Et dixit illis Judith: Sicut quod loqui potui, Dei esse cognoscitis, id est verum atque salubre; ita quod facere disposui probate, id est, suo tempore considerate, et nunc interim exspectate, donec per effectum propositi mei pensetis, si ex Deo est, et orate ut firmum faciat Deus consilium meum, id est, illud perficiat, et ad salutarem ducat effectum. Stabitis vos ad portam nocte ista, et ego exeam cum abra mea, id est cum ancilla mea, et orate, ut sicut dixistis, diebus quinque respiciat Dominus populum suum. Vos autem nolo ut scrutemini actum meum, id est, non interrogetis a me quid agere velim; et usquedum renuntiem vobis quid egerim, vel per me ipsam, sive per alium, nihil aliud fiat, nisi oratio pro me ad Dominum Deum nostrum. Et dixit ad eam Ozias princeps Juda, id est unus de principalibus et rectoribus tribus seu populi Juda, secundum quod Nicodemus vocatur princeps Judæorum: Vade in pace, et Dominus sit tecum in ultionem inimicorum nostrorum, id est infligendo per te hostibus nostris justam punitionem in vindictam iniquitatum eorum adversum nos.
paras.en: [[8:30|And Judith said to them|Et dixit illis Judith]]: [[8:30|As you know that what I have been able to say is of God|Sicut quod loqui potui, Dei esse cognoscitis]], that is, true and wholesome, [[8:31|So that which I intend to do prove ye|ita quod facere disposui probate]], that is, consider it in its own time, and wait meanwhile, until by the effect of my purpose you weigh it, [[8:31|if it be of God|si ex Deo est]], [[8:31|and pray that God may strengthen my design|et orate ut firmum faciat Deus consilium meum]], that is, may accomplish it and bring it to a saving effect. [[8:32|You shall stand at the gate this night|Stabitis vos ad portam nocte ista]], [[8:32|and I will go out with my maidservant|et ego exeam cum abra mea]] [*abra*, a waiting-maid], that is, with my handmaid, [[8:32|and pray ye, that as you have said, in five days the Lord may look down upon his people|et orate, ut sicut dixistis, diebus quinque respiciat Dominus populum suum]]. [[8:33|But I desire that you search not into what I am doing|Vos autem nolo ut scrutemini actum meum]], that is, do not ask me what I mean to do; [[8:33|and till I bring you word|et usquedum renuntiem vobis]] of what I have done, either by myself or through another, [[8:33|let nothing else be done but to pray for me to the Lord our God|nihil aliud fiat, nisi oratio pro me ad Dominum Deum nostrum]]. [[8:34|And Ozias the prince of Juda said to her|Et dixit ad eam Ozias princeps Juda]], that is, one of the chief men and rulers of the tribe or people of Juda, as Nicodemus is called a ruler of the Jews[[John 3:1||]]: [[8:34|Go in peace, and the Lord be with thee to take revenge of our enemies|Vade in pace, et Dominus sit tecum in ultionem inimicorum nostrorum]], that is, by inflicting through thee on our enemies just punishment in vengeance for their iniquities against us.

paras.t: Ex isto capitulo accipere possumus multa moralia et optima documenta. Nempe in primis ex isto informantur capitulo viduæ universæ, ut quamvis formosæ, juvenes, nobiles, divitesque consistant, attamen in viduali castimonia perseverent; et quo appetibiliores fuerint, eo plus vitent occasiones lasciviæ ac scandala aliorum, et corpus suum in spiritus redigant servitutem aspero (aut etiam cilicino) vestitu, jejuniis, orationibus, disciplinis, vigiliis. Insuper hic docemur, ne Deum aliquo modo tentemus, sed in ipso usque in finem, etiamsi nos occiderit, confidamus: et dum Dei misericordiam imploramus, ipsum nequaquam verbis aut actibus seu negligentia offendamus. In omni quoque necessitate, tribulatione, angustia, in spiritu contrito et humiliato Dominum invocemus. Cuncta demum adversa cum invicta patientia amplectamur, humiliter confitentes quod peccata nostra multo majora mereantur supplicia; neque nos ulciscamur, nec contra Dominum ullatenus murmuremus. Sicque sanctorum patrum exempla considerantes, eadem totis viribus imitemur, et proximos, ut pro nobis assidue orent, pulsemus.
paras.en: From this chapter we can take many excellent moral lessons. For first, all widows are taught by this chapter that, however beautiful, young, noble and rich they may be, they should persevere in the chastity of widowhood; and the more desirable they are, the more they should shun the occasions of wantonness and of scandal to others, and bring their body into subjection to the spirit[[1 Cor 9:27||]] by rough (or even haircloth) clothing, by fasts, prayers, disciplines and vigils. Further, we are taught here not to tempt God in any way, but to trust in Him to the end, even if He should kill us[[Job 13:15||]]; and, while we implore God's mercy, in no way to offend Him by words or deeds or negligence. In every need, tribulation and distress, too, let us call upon the Lord with a contrite and humbled spirit[[Dan 3:39||]]. Lastly, let us embrace all adversities with unconquered patience, humbly confessing that our sins deserve far greater punishments; and let us neither avenge ourselves nor in any way murmur against the Lord[[1 Cor 10:10||]]. And so, considering the examples of the holy fathers, let us imitate them with all our strength, and urge our neighbours to pray constantly for us.

9.title: Expositio capituli noni: Quibus abscedentibus
9.title_en: Exposition of the ninth chapter: And when they were gone

paras.t: Oratio Judith hic introducitur. Quibus abscedentibus Judith ingressa est oratorium suum, quod erat in superioribus, ut patuit præcedenti capitulo; et induens se cilicio, posuit cinerem super caput suum. Dicunt aliqui, quod præter cilicium quo fuit supra nudum corpus vestita, etiam jam vestivit se cilicina veste exterius. Et prosternens se Domino, cui se humiliavit vestitu et cinere, corde et corpore, clamavit ad Dominum ex vehementi affectionis suæ ardore, dicens: Domine, Deus patris mei Simeon. Ex quibus verbis apparet, quod fuit de tribu Simeon; quum præcedenti sit dictum capitulo, quod fuit de tribu Ruben. Ad quod nonnulli respondent, quod fuit de tribu Ruben ex parte patris, atque ex tribu Simeon ex parte matris: quod et in Scholastica affirmatur historia.
paras.en: Here Judith's prayer is introduced. [[9:1|And when they were gone|Quibus abscedentibus]], [[9:1|Judith went into her oratory|Judith ingressa est oratorium suum]], which was in the upper part of the house, as appeared in the preceding chapter[[Jdt 8:5||]]; [[9:1|and putting on haircloth, laid ashes on her head|et induens se cilicio, posuit cinerem super caput suum]]. Some say that besides the haircloth with which she was clothed next to her bare body, she now also clothed herself outwardly in a garment of haircloth. And [[9:1|falling down prostrate before the Lord|prosternens se Domino]], to whom she humbled herself in dress and in ashes, in heart and in body, [[9:1|she cried to the Lord|clamavit ad Dominum]] from the vehement ardour of her affection, [[9:1|saying|dicens]]: [[9:2|Lord God of my father Simeon|Domine, Deus patris mei Simeon]]. From these words it appears that she was of the tribe of Simeon, whereas in the preceding chapter it was said that she was of the tribe of Ruben[[Jdt 8:1||]]. To this some answer that she was of the tribe of Ruben on her father's side, and of the tribe of Simeon on her mother's: which is also affirmed in the Scholastic History.

paras.t: Contra quod arguit quidam satis prolixe. Primo, quoniam mulieres non debebant conjungi viris alterius tribus. Secundo, quia Ruben ad quem reducitur generatio Judith, non videtur fuisse Ruben patriarcha filius Jacob, sed alius, quoniam inter patriarcham et Judith multo plures fuerunt generationes quam præcedenti capitulo inducuntur. Tertio, quia nec in Genesi, nec in Paralipomenon scribitur aliquis filiorum ipsius Ruben vocatus fuisse Simeon, sicut in præcedenti capitulo. Ad quæ omnia faciliter posset respondere, qui præfatam responsionem vellet tenere: respondendo ad primum, quod mulieres quæ non successerunt in hæreditate paterna, poterant contrahere cum viris tribuum aliarum, sicut David de tribu Juda sumpsit Michol de Benjamin tribu; ad secundum, quod non omnes, sed quædam præcipuæ generationes ipsius Judith in ascendendo ponuntur capitulo præcedenti; ad tertium, quod Simeon ille filius Ruben mediatus aut immediatus binomius fuit.
paras.en: Against this a certain writer argues at some length. First, because women ought not to be joined to men of another tribe[[Num 36:8||]]. Second, because the Ruben to whom Judith's line is traced back does not seem to have been Ruben the patriarch, the son of Jacob, but another, since between the patriarch and Judith there were many more generations than are set down in the preceding chapter[[Jdt 8:1||]]. Third, because neither in Genesis[[Gen 46:9||]] nor in Paralipomenon[[1 Par 5:3||]] is any of the sons of Ruben himself written to have been called Simeon, as in the preceding chapter. To all of which anyone who wished to hold the aforesaid answer could easily reply: answering the first, that women who did not succeed to their father's inheritance could marry men of other tribes, as David, of the tribe of Juda, took Michol of the tribe of Benjamin[[1 Kings 18:27||]]; the second, that not all, but certain principal generations of Judith's line, going upwards, are set down in the preceding chapter[[Jdt 8:1||]]; the third, that this Simeon, the son of Ruben, mediate or immediate [that is, either a later descendant of Ruben or his own son], had two names.

paras.t: Denique prætactus, dicens ipsam Judith fuisse de tribu Simeon ex parte patris et matris, in argumentationis suæ processu affirmat, quod Jacob cito postquam Esau quadragenarius duxit uxores, perrexit ad Mesopotamiam, et quadraginta octo annorum fuisse videtur dum genuit Ruben.
paras.en: Lastly, the writer mentioned above, who says that Judith was of the tribe of Simeon on both her father's and her mother's side, affirms in the course of his argument that Jacob went to Mesopotamia soon after Esau, at forty years of age, took wives, and that he seems to have been forty-eight years old when he begot Ruben.

paras.t: Circa quod dico, quod Jacob erat octoginta annorum aut circiter, quando ad Mesopotamiam est profectus. Siquidem in Genesi legitur ipse Jacob filium suum Joseph præ ceteris dilexisse, quia in senectute sua genuit eum. Rursumque fertur, qualiter Jacob ingressus Ægyptum, locutus sit Pharaoni: Dies peregrinationis vitæ meæ super terram, centum triginta anni sunt parvi et mali. Et tunc Joseph nondum erat quadragenarius: triginta namque fuit annorum, quando a Pharaone constitutus est princeps Ægypti, ut habetur in Genesi. Deinde fluxerunt septem anni fertilitatis: quibus evolutis, primo anno caristiæ venerunt fratres ejus ad eum, quibus secunda vice ad se reversis locutus est: Biennium est quod cœpit esse fames: adhuc quinque anni restant, quibus nec arari poterit nec meti. Et tunc erat triginta novem annorum. Moxque misit pro patre suo, qui tunc fuit centum triginta annorum, sicque in nativitate Joseph fuit nonagenarius. Porro in Mesopotamia habitavit annis viginti. Quæ omnia patent in Genesi. Et dato quod Joseph fuisset natus in ultimo illorum viginti annorum, tamen pater ejus fuisset septuagenarius, quando Mesopotamiam est ingressus. Joseph autem natus fuit quartodecimo circiter anno habitationis Jacob in Mesopotamia, ut in Genesi patet. Unde concluditur, quod Jacob fuerit circiter septuaginta sex annorum, quando venit ad Mesopotamiam.
paras.en: On this I say that Jacob was eighty years old, or thereabouts, when he set out for Mesopotamia [so the print; the reckoning that follows gives about seventy-six]. For in Genesis we read that Jacob loved his son Joseph above the rest, because he begot him in his old age[[Gen 37:3||]]. And again it is told how Jacob, having entered Egypt, said to Pharao: [[Gen 47:9|The days of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years, few, and evil|Dies peregrinationis vitæ meæ super terram, centum triginta anni sunt parvi et mali]] [Denis reads "the days of the pilgrimage of my life upon earth"]. And Joseph was then not yet forty: for he was thirty years old when he was made prince of Egypt by Pharao, as is said in Genesis[[Gen 41:46||]]. Then the seven years of plenty went by; and when they were over, in the first year of the dearth his brothers came to him, and when they had come back to him a second time he said to them: [[Gen 45:6|it is two years since the famine began to be upon the land, and five years more remain, wherein there can be neither ploughing nor reaping|Biennium est quod cœpit esse fames: adhuc quinque anni restant, quibus nec arari poterit nec meti]]. And he was then thirty-nine years old. And soon he sent for his father, who was then a hundred and thirty years old; and so at Joseph's birth he was ninety. Further, he dwelt in Mesopotamia twenty years[[Gen 31:41||]]. All this is plain in Genesis. And granted that Joseph had been born in the last of those twenty years, his father would still have been seventy when he entered Mesopotamia. But Joseph was born in about the fourteenth year of Jacob's stay in Mesopotamia, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 30:25||]]. Hence it is concluded that Jacob was about seventy-six years old when he came to Mesopotamia.

paras.t: Qui dedisti illi gladium in defensionem alienigenarum, id est ad ulciscendum stuprum quod alienigenæ seu infideles Chananæi commiserunt in filia Jacob, qui violatores exstiterunt in coinquinatione sua, id est, sua pollutione corruperunt Dinam filiam Jacob. Unde subjungitur, et denudaverunt femur virginis in confusionem: et sumitur hic plurale pro singulari, quoniam solus Sichem filius Hemor illam corrupit. Vel ideo ait pluraliter, Violatores, quoniam aliqui adjuverunt eum ad perpetrandum hoc scelus. Et dedisti mulieres eorum in prædam, et filias eorum in captivitatem, et omnem prædam in divisionem servis tuis, videlicet filiis Jacob, qui zelaverunt, id est, per amorem secuti sunt, zelum tuum, id est fervorem tibi placentem contra injustitiam.
paras.en: [[9:2|who gavest him a sword|Qui dedisti illi gladium]] [[9:2|to execute vengeance against strangers|in defensionem alienigenarum]] [literally "for defence against strangers"], that is, to avenge the rape which strangers, namely the unbelieving Chanaanites, committed upon Jacob's daughter; [[9:2|who had defiled by their uncleanness|qui violatores exstiterunt in coinquinatione sua]], that is, by their pollution corrupted Dina, Jacob's daughter. Hence it is added: [[9:2|and uncovered the virgin unto confusion|et denudaverunt femur virginis in confusionem]] [literally "uncovered the thigh of the virgin"]: and here the plural is taken for the singular, since Sichem, the son of Hemor, alone corrupted her[[Gen 34:2||]]. Or else she speaks in the plural, *violators* [Latin *violatores*, where the Douay-Rheims has "who had defiled"], because some helped him to commit this crime. [[9:3|And who gavest their wives to be made a prey, and their daughters into captivity|Et dedisti mulieres eorum in prædam, et filias eorum in captivitatem]]: [[9:3|and all their spoils to be divided to the servants|et omnem prædam in divisionem servis tuis]], namely to the sons of Jacob, [[9:3|who were zealous|qui zelaverunt]], that is, followed out of love, [[9:3|with thy zeal|zelum tuum]], that is, a fervour against injustice that is pleasing to thee.

paras.t: Videtur quasi totum istud repugnare Scripturæ canonicæ, quoniam Jacob redarguit ultionem præfatam, dicens Simeon et Levi: Turbastis me, et odiosum fecistis habitatoribus terræ hujus. In extremis quoque agens, valde abhorruit illam vindictam, dicens: Simeon et Levi vasa iniquitatis bellantia. In consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, et in cœtu eorum non sit gloria mea: quia in furore suo occiderunt virum, et in voluntate sua suffoderunt murum. Unde elicitur, quod non zelo Deo placente seu zelo Dei, sed ex furore et indignatione illud fecerunt. Ad istud Magister in historiis breviter dicit: Judith non commendavit factum Simeonis, quod detestatus est Jacob, sed ultionem factam a Domino per manus ipsius.
paras.en: All this seems almost to conflict with canonical Scripture, since Jacob rebuked the aforesaid vengeance, saying to Simeon and Levi: [[Gen 34:30|You have troubled me, and made me hateful|Turbastis me, et odiosum fecistis]] to [[Gen 34:30|the inhabitants of this land|habitatoribus terræ hujus]]. At the end of his life, too, he greatly abhorred that vengeance, saying: [[Gen 49:5|Simeon and Levi brethren: vessels of iniquity waging war|Simeon et Levi vasa iniquitatis bellantia]]. [[Gen 49:6|Let not my soul go into their counsel, nor my glory be in their assembly: because in their fury they slew a man, and in their self-will they undermined a wall|In consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, et in cœtu eorum non sit gloria mea: quia in furore suo occiderunt virum, et in voluntate sua suffoderunt murum]]. Hence it is gathered that they did it not with a zeal pleasing to God, or the zeal of God, but out of fury and indignation. To this the Master [Peter Comestor, author of the Scholastic History] says briefly in the Histories: Judith did not commend the deed of Simeon, which Jacob detested, but the vengeance wrought by the Lord through his hands.

paras.t: Alius quidam prolixius respondens: In illo (inquit) facto duo fuerunt, videlicet zelus ulciscendi stuprum, et illud fuit justum et licitum, quia non habebat judicem qui vellet factum punire, cujus auctor erat princeps civitatis et populus ejus imitator: et sic loquitur hic Judith. Alius est modus ulciscendi, qui fuit malus et proditorius, in quantum filii Jacob transgressi sunt pactum habitum cum Sichimitis: et sic reprehendit illud Jacob. Verum ista responsio non videtur idonea. Primo, quoniam juxta prætacta factum illud non processit ex zelo Dei, sed ex indignatione atque rancore. Secundo, quia tam opus illud, quam modus operis, vitiosa fuerunt. Opus namque ex prava processit radice, non ex justo zelo, ut patuit, et modus fuit fraudulentus. Tertio, quia post initum fœdus nequaquam licuit filiis Jacob illam facere ultionem, nec potuerunt ad hoc habere zelum Dei secundum scientiam post initum pacis pactum. Quod totum patet ex verbis Hieronymi, affirmantis: Significavit Jacob non sui fuisse consilii, quod Simeon et Levi ipsum Hemor et Sichem filium ejus viros sibi fœderatos interfecerunt, et contra jus pacis et amicitiarum sanguinem effuderunt innocentem, et crudelitate quasi furore rapti, muros hospitæ urbis everterunt.
paras.en: Another writer, answering at greater length, says: In that deed there were two things. One was the zeal to avenge the rape, and this was just and lawful, since they had no judge willing to punish the deed, whose author was the prince of the city[[Gen 34:2||]] and his people its imitator: and in this sense Judith speaks here. The other is the manner of avenging, which was wicked and treacherous, inasmuch as the sons of Jacob broke the pact they had made with the Sichemites: and in this sense Jacob rebukes it. But this answer does not seem adequate. First, because, according to what was said above, that deed did not proceed from the zeal of God, but from indignation and rancour. Second, because both the work itself and the manner of the work were vicious: for the work proceeded from an evil root, not from just zeal, as has appeared, and the manner was fraudulent. Third, because after the covenant had been made it was in no way lawful for the sons of Jacob to take that vengeance, nor could they have the zeal of God according to knowledge[[Rom 10:2||]] for it, after the pact of peace had been entered into. All of which is plain from the words of Jerome, who affirms: Jacob signified that it was not by his counsel that Simeon and Levi slew Hemor himself and his son Sichem[[Gen 34:26||]], men in league with them, and against the law of peace and friendship shed innocent blood, and, carried away by cruelty as by fury, overthrew the walls of the city that had received them as guests.

paras.t: Insuper, quod dicitur filios Jacob non habuisse judicem, qui factum vellet punire, non apparet. Quamvis enim Hemor erat rex Sichimorum, non tamen totius terræ illius: et sic habuit superiorem, ad quem potuisset referri. Unde in Josue scriptum est: Asor inter omnia regna antiquitus primatum tenebat. Præterea, quamvis judicem talem non habuissent, tamen postquam Hemor et Sichem tam magnam præbuerunt emendam et satisfactionem, et pacis conditionem inierunt cum Jacob et filiis ejus, ac circumciderunt se, non licuit filiis Jacob illam exercere vindictam. Propter quod ipse Jacob asseruit, furorem eorum et indignationem esse maledictionis, quia tam pertinax fuit furor eorum, atque tam dura ipsorum indignatio, quod post tanta benevolentiæ signa, satisfactionisque dona oblata, et inita pacis pacta, non fuerant emolliti.
paras.en: Moreover, what is said, that the sons of Jacob had no judge willing to punish the deed, does not appear to be so. For though Hemor was king of the Sichemites, he was not king of that whole land[[Gen 34:2||]]; and so he had a superior to whom the matter could have been referred. Hence it is written in Josue: [[Jos 11:10|Asor of old was the head of all these kingdoms|Asor inter omnia regna antiquitus primatum tenebat]]. Further, even if they had had no such judge, yet after Hemor and Sichem had offered so great an amends and satisfaction[[Gen 34:12||]], and had entered into terms of peace with Jacob and his sons, and had circumcised themselves[[Gen 34:24||]], it was not lawful for the sons of Jacob to take that vengeance. For which reason Jacob himself declared that their fury and indignation deserved a curse[[Gen 49:7||]], because their fury was so stubborn and their indignation so cruel that after such signs of goodwill, after gifts of satisfaction offered and pacts of peace entered into, they had not been softened.

paras.t: Amplius, responsio ex Scholastica historia introducta, videtur obscura: quoniam ultio ejus non videtur commendanda fuisse secundum prædicta, nisi forsan quoad divinum judicium, quoniam Hemor et Sichem non videntur vere pœnituisse de scelere illo. Sicque quantum ad hoc, justa fuit illa vindicta, quamvis Simeon et Levi non recte ex zelo laudabili, sed ex furore et indignatione exsecuti sint eam. Juxta quem modum justa fuit Judæorum exterminatio, punitio, captivatio facta per Assyrios et Chaldæos, quamvis Assyrii et Chaldæi ex vitiosa radice inflixerint talia filiis Israel. Sicque aliquo modo videntur verba Judith posse salvari.
paras.en: Further, the answer brought from the Scholastic History seems obscure: since, according to what has been said, that vengeance does not seem to have been commendable, unless perhaps as regards the divine judgement, since Hemor and Sichem do not seem truly to have repented of that crime. And so in this respect that vengeance was just, though Simeon and Levi carried it out not rightly, from a praiseworthy zeal, but from fury and indignation. In the same way the extermination, punishment and captivity of the Jews by the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]] and Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:1||]] was just, though the Assyrians and Chaldeans inflicted such things on the children of Israel from a vicious root. And so in some way Judith's words can, it seems, be saved [that is, given a sound sense].

paras.t: Subveni, quæso te, Domine Deus meus, mihi viduæ, qui (teste Psalmista) pater est orphanorum, judexque viduarum; de quo iterum dicitur in Psalmo, Pupillum et viduam suscipiet. Tu enim fecisti priora, id est, pristinas dedisti victorias filiis Israel descriptas in libris Moysis, Josue, Judicum, Regum, Paralipomenon, et illa post illa cogitasti, id est, unum post aliud facere decrevisti. Omnia tamen simul in ipso æternitatis instanti plenissime cognoscis, cogitas, intueris, non successive unum post aliud: et hoc factum est quod ipse voluisti, quia omnipotens es. Ideo ait Propheta: Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit in cœlo et in terra. Omnes enim viæ tuæ paratæ sunt, id est, a te prædispositæ sunt tuæ actiones, atque in promptu habes agere omnibus modis tibi placentibus, et exhibere actus quoscumque volueris; et tua judicia, id est justa et judicialia opera tua, in tua providentia posuisti, id est in præordinatione et libertate sapientiæ atque potentiæ tuæ, ita quod quidquid forinsecus agis et judicas, ex certa et æterna providentia procedit. Unde et Paulus: Omnia (inquit) operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ.
paras.en: [[9:3|assist, I beseech thee, O Lord God, me a widow|Subveni, quæso te, Domine Deus meus, mihi viduæ]], who (as the Psalmist bears witness) is [[Ps 67:6|the father of orphans, and the judge of widows|pater est orphanorum, judexque viduarum]]; of whom it is said again in the Psalm: [[Ps 145:9|he will support the fatherless and the widow|Pupillum et viduam suscipiet]]. [[9:4|For thou hast done the things of old|Tu enim fecisti priora]], that is, thou didst give the children of Israel the victories of former times, described in the books of Moses[[Ex 17:10||]], of Josue[[Jos 10:10||]], of Judges[[Judg 7:19||]][[Judg 11:32||]], of Kings[[4 Kings 19:35||]] and of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 20:22||]]; [[9:4|and hast devised one thing after another|et illa post illa cogitasti]], that is, thou didst decree to do one thing after another. Yet thou knowest, thinkest and beholdest all things together, most fully, in the very instant of eternity, not successively one after another: [[9:4|and what thou hast designed hath been done|et hoc factum est quod ipse voluisti]], because thou art almighty. Therefore the Prophet says: [[Ps 134:6|Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth|Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit in cœlo et in terra]]. [[9:5|For all thy ways are prepared|Omnes enim viæ tuæ paratæ sunt]], that is, thy actions are disposed beforehand by thee, and thou hast it in readiness to act in every way that pleases thee, and to put forth whatever acts thou wilt; and [[9:5|thy judgments|et tua judicia]], that is, thy just and judicial works, [[9:5|in thy providence thou hast placed|in tua providentia posuisti]], that is, in the foreordaining and freedom of thy wisdom and power, so that whatever thou doest and judgest outwardly proceeds from a sure and eternal providence. Hence Paul too: [[Eph 1:11|all things|Omnia]] (he says) he [[Eph 1:11|worketh|operatur]] [[Eph 1:11|according to the counsel of his will|secundum consilium voluntatis suæ]].

paras.t: Respice castra Assyriorum nunc, id est, exercitus istos Assyriorum oculo tuæ justitiæ per justam eorum punitionem intuere, in quantum sunt hostes boni communis ac cultus divini, sicut tunc castra videre Ægyptiorum dignatus es, quando post servos tuos armati currebant, dum scilicet filii Israel, Moyse duce, exierunt Ægyptum. Sed adspexisti super castra eorum, id est, per districtam vindictam ostendisti te impios illos adspicere: secundum illud Exodi, Et ecce respiciens Dominus supra castra Ægyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis, interfecit exercitum eorum; et tenebræ fatigaverunt eos, id est, affligebantur Ægyptii ex hoc, quod nubes tenebrosa stetit inter eos et filios Israel, ita quod tota nocte Israelitas accedere non valebant, juxta quod in Exodo fertur: Tollens se angelus Domini, qui filios Israel præcedebat, abiit post eos, et cum eo pariter columna nubis inter castra Ægyptiorum et castra Israel; et erat nubes tenebrosa, ita ut ad se invicem toto noctis tempore accedere non valerent. Tenuit pedes eorum abyssus, et aquæ operuerunt eos, id est, aqua maris Rubri divisi ad priorem refluens locum, impedivit pedes Ægyptiorum a processu.
paras.en: [[9:6|Look upon the camp of the Assyrians now|Respice castra Assyriorum nunc]], that is, behold these armies of the Assyrians with the eye of thy justice, by justly punishing them, inasmuch as they are enemies of the common good and of divine worship, [[9:6|as thou wast pleased to look upon the camp of the Egyptians|sicut tunc castra videre Ægyptiorum dignatus es]], [[9:6|when they pursued armed after thy servants|quando post servos tuos armati currebant]], that is, when the children of Israel went out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses[[Ex 14:8||]]. [[9:7|But thou lookedst over their camp|Sed adspexisti super castra eorum]], that is, by strict vengeance thou didst show that thou didst look upon those wicked men: according to that word of Exodus: And [[Ex 14:24|behold the Lord looking upon the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, slew their host|Et ecce respiciens Dominus supra castra Ægyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis, interfecit exercitum eorum]]; [[9:7|and darkness wearied them|et tenebræ fatigaverunt eos]], that is, the Egyptians were afflicted because the dark cloud stood between them and the children of Israel, so that all night long they could not come near the Israelites, as is told in Exodus: [[Ex 14:19|And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removing, went behind them: and together with him the pillar of the cloud|Tollens se angelus Domini, qui filios Israel præcedebat, abiit post eos, et cum eo pariter columna nubis]], [[Ex 14:20|between the Egyptians' camp and the camp of Israel|inter castra Ægyptiorum et castra Israel]]; [[Ex 14:20|and it was a dark cloud|et erat nubes tenebrosa]], [[Ex 14:20|so that they could not come at one another all the night|ita ut ad se invicem toto noctis tempore accedere non valerent]] [Denis reads "the angel of the Lord, who went before the children of Israel"]. [[9:8|The deep held their feet, and the waters overwhelmed them|Tenuit pedes eorum abyssus, et aquæ operuerunt eos]], that is, the water of the Red Sea, which had been divided, flowing back to its former place, stopped the feet of the Egyptians from going forward.

paras.t: Sic fiant isti, puta Assyrii, Domine, qui confidunt in multitudine sua, et in curribus suis, et in contis, id est perticis præacutis ferro seu cuspide, quas loco hastarum rustici portant, et in sagittis suis, et in lanceis suis gloriantur; et nesciunt quia, id est quod, tu ipse verus, omnipotens et omnia intuens, es Dominus Deus noster, qui conteris bella ab initio, id est, ab antiquis temporibus contrivisti bellatores iniquos, et bella eorum cassasti: sicut in Josue et Judicum libro narratur; et Dominus nomen est tibi, quia tu propria potestate et auctoritate universis et singulis dominaris, cujus respectu omnis creatura dominans, est instrumentum et serva, imbecillis, dependens, exigua. Ideo ait Psalmista: Qui dominatur in virtute sua in æternum. Unde per Isaiam testatur: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum.
paras.en: [[9:9|So may it be with these also|Sic fiant isti]], namely the Assyrians, [[9:9|O Lord, who trust in their multitude|Domine, qui confidunt in multitudine sua]], [[9:9|and in their chariots|et in curribus suis]], [[9:9|and in their pikes|et in contis]], that is, poles sharpened to a point with iron or a tip, which country folk carry instead of spears, [[9:9|and in their arrows|et in sagittis suis]], [[9:9|and glory in their spears|et in lanceis suis gloriantur]]; and [[9:10|know not that|nesciunt quia]], that is, *that* [Denis glosses *quia* by *quod*, both meaning "that"], [[9:10|thou|tu ipse]], the true, the almighty, who seest all things, [[9:10|art our God|es Dominus Deus noster]] [Denis reads "art the Lord our God"], [[9:10|who destroyest wars from the beginning|qui conteris bella ab initio]], that is, from ancient times thou hast crushed wicked warriors and brought their wars to nothing, as is told in the books of Josue and of Judges; [[9:10|and the Lord is thy name|et Dominus nomen est tibi]], because by thine own power and authority thou rulest over all and each, and compared with thee every creature that rules is an instrument and a handmaid, weak, dependent and slight. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 65:7|Who by his power ruleth for ever|Qui dominatur in virtute sua in æternum]]. Hence he bears witness through Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum]].

paras.t: Erige brachium tuum, id est omnipotentiam tuam sublimiter per effectus tuos ostende, sicut ab initio, et allide virtutem eorum in virtute tua, id est, propria potestate confringe potestatem atque exercitum Assyriorum; cadat virtus eorum in iracundia tua, id est in rigore justitiæ tuæ, qui promittunt se violare sancta tua, id est, jactanter præsumunt quod sacra templi contaminabunt ac destruent, et polluere tabernaculum nominis tui, id est templum tuæ majestati deputatum seu inchoatum, et dejicere gladio suo cornu altaris tui. Fac ut gladio proprio ejus superbia amputetur, id est, superbum caput Holofernis amputetur manu mea ipsius mucrone. Capiatur laqueo oculorum suorum in me, id est, incauto suo intuitu sic afficiatur ad me, ut id fiat occasio suæ interfectionis, et percuties eum ex labiis caritatis meæ, id est, per verba labiorum meorum, quæ ex caritate filiorum Israel pronuntiabo, facies eum seu permittes decipi, atque corruere seu occidi, ut spero. Hæc enim dixit ex bona fiducia, non ex certitudine absoluta.
paras.en: [[9:11|Lift up thy arm|Erige brachium tuum]], that is, show forth thine almighty power on high by thy works, [[9:11|as from the beginning|sicut ab initio]], [[9:11|and crush their power with thy power|et allide virtutem eorum in virtute tua]], that is, by thine own might break the might and the army of the Assyrians; [[9:11|let their power fall in their wrath|cadat virtus eorum in iracundia tua]] [the Latin has "in thy wrath"], that is, in the rigour of thy justice, [[9:11|who promise themselves to violate thy sanctuary|qui promittunt se violare sancta tua]], that is, who boastfully presume that they will defile and destroy the holy things of the temple, [[9:11|and defile the dwelling place of thy name|et polluere tabernaculum nominis tui]], that is, the temple appointed, or begun, for thy majesty, [[9:11|and to beat down with their sword the horn of thy altar|et dejicere gladio suo cornu altaris tui]]. [[9:12|Bring to pass, O Lord, that his pride may be cut off with his own sword|Fac ut gladio proprio ejus superbia amputetur]], that is, may the proud head of Holofernes be cut off by my hand with his own blade. [[9:13|Let him be caught in the net of his own eyes in my regard|Capiatur laqueo oculorum suorum in me]], that is, may he be so affected towards me by his unwary gazing that it becomes the occasion of his being slain; [[9:13|and do thou strike him by the graces of the words of my lips|et percuties eum ex labiis caritatis meæ]] [literally "by the lips of my charity"], that is, by the words of my lips, which I shall speak out of charity for the children of Israel, thou wilt make, or permit, him to be deceived, and to fall or be slain, as I hope. For she said this out of good confidence, not from absolute certainty.

paras.t: Verumtamen circa hæc, est præcipua difficultas, quæ et in sequentibus quoque occurrit. Videtur etenim Judith optasse ac postulasse, quod Holofernes eam intuendo, accenderetur libidinoso ejus amore et carnali affectu, quatenus sic deceptus, perimeretur ab ea in lecto aut camera. Alium autem ad mortale peccatum ex proposito incitare, seu velle inducere, est mortale peccatum, et caritati Dei ac proximi directe contrarium, quantumcumque hoc ultra ordinetur ad commendabilem finem: imo bonus finis est appetendus et exquirendus seu obtinendus per proportionata et licita media. Ad istud dicendum videtur, quod Judith, quæ erat virtuosa et prudens matrona, non intendebat Holofernem inducere ad libidinosum amorem aut concupiscentiam vitiosam, sed ad concupiscentiam talem ac tantam, quod acciperet eam ad suam familiaritatem, vel optaret habere eam et accipere conjugem: non quod ipsa intenderet cum ipso contrahere, quod nec voluit nec licuit ei, videlicet Holoferni.
paras.en: But concerning these words there is a principal difficulty, which also comes up in what follows. For Judith seems to have wished and asked that Holofernes, by looking at her, should be inflamed with lustful love of her and carnal affection, so that, thus deceived, he might be slain by her in bed or in his chamber. But to incite another to mortal sin on purpose, or to wish to lead him into it, is a mortal sin, and directly contrary to the charity of God and of our neighbour, however much it be further directed to a praiseworthy end: rather, a good end is to be sought, pursued and obtained by fitting and lawful means. To this it seems we must say that Judith, who was a virtuous and prudent matron, did not intend to lead Holofernes into lustful love or vicious desire, but into a desire such and so great that he would take her into his familiarity, or would wish to have her and take her as his wife: not that she herself intended to marry him, which she neither wished, nor was it lawful for her[[Deut 7:3||]], namely with Holofernes.

paras.t: Circa hoc refert Lyra positionem quorumdam, dicentium quod Judith non peccavit in prædicta oratione et sua compositione, quoniam aliud intendebat, et aliud prævidebat. Intendebat quippe sic grata fieri Holoferni, quod posset familiariter esse cum ipso ad ejus interitum perpetrandum: quod ei licitum erat, quoniam fuit adversarius Dei et boni communis ac cultus divini. Prævidebat autem amorem Holofernis illicitum circa se. Non tamen propter hoc debuit dimittere bonum prædictum, sicut nec Deus dimittit peccatorem punire, quamvis videat eum ex hoc deteriorari, ut patuit in Pharaone. Sed contra positionem hanc objicit prætactus expositor, quoniam eadem est intentio finis, et eorum quæ sunt ad finem, quando apprehenduntur ut ordinata ad finem: sicut mobile eodem motu movetur in medium et terminum. Judith autem intendebat mortem Holofernis, tanquam finem intentum, ad quem intendebat pertingere per privatam familiaritatem: et hanc familiaritatem intendebat per ardorem concupiscentiæ Holofernis in ipsam, et sic intendebat eum inducere ad peccatum mortale.
paras.en: On this Lyra reports the position of some who say that Judith did not sin in the aforesaid prayer and in adorning herself, since she intended one thing and foresaw another. For she intended to become so pleasing to Holofernes that she could be with him familiarly in order to bring about his death: which was lawful for her, since he was an adversary of God, of the common good and of divine worship. She foresaw, however, Holofernes' unlawful love for her. Yet for this she ought not to have given up the good just mentioned, just as God does not give up punishing a sinner, although he sees that he grows worse by it, as appeared in Pharao[[Ex 10:1||]] [the margin's reference here is barely legible; Exodus is meant]. But against this position the expositor mentioned above objects that the intention of the end and of the things that are for the end is the same, when these are apprehended as directed to the end: as a moving body is moved by the same motion towards the midpoint and towards the terminus. Now Judith intended the death of Holofernes as the end intended, which she meant to reach through private familiarity; and this familiarity she meant to gain through the ardour of Holofernes' desire for her; and so she intended to lead him into mortal sin.

paras.t: Sed qui vult positionem istam, quæ satis probabilis reputatur, defendere, dicere habet, quod Judith non intendebat familiaritatem illam Holofernis acquirere per vitiosum ardorem concupiscentiæ sensualis in ipsam, sed per concupiscentiam talem ac tantam, qua cuperet eam ducere in uxorem; et quamvis ipsa facillime poterat conjicere, quod Holofernes eam vitiose appeteret, non tamen ob hoc debuit procurationem familiaritatis illius vitare: sicut qui ab usurariis accommodat ad usuram, non peccat, quamvis sciat quod illi non mutuabunt sibi sine usura, quoniam ipse non intendit eos ad usuram inducere, sed propriæ necessitati consulere; et sic malo illorum utitur ad bonum suum, sicut et Deus ex malis aliorum elicit multa bona. Hinc in secunda secundæ, quæstione 78, loquitur Thomas: Nullatenus licitum est alium ad peccandum inducere; sed malo ac peccato alterius uti in bonum, est licitum. Nam et Deus utitur peccatoribus in bonum, dum ex eorum malis elicit bona. Hinc Augustinus Publicolæ sciscitanti, an liceat uti juramento jurantis per falsos deos, respondit, quod utens juramento ita jurantis, non se sociat peccato illius, sed bono ejus pacto, quo fidem servavit: peccaret autem, si illum induceret ad jurandum per falsos deos.
paras.en: But whoever wishes to defend this position, which is held to be quite probable, must say that Judith did not intend to gain that familiarity with Holofernes through a vicious ardour of sensual desire for her, but through a desire such and so great that he would wish to take her to wife; and although she could very easily guess that Holofernes would desire her viciously, she was not on that account bound to forgo procuring that familiarity: just as one who borrows at usury from usurers does not sin, though he knows that they will not lend to him without usury, since he does not intend to lead them into usury, but to provide for his own need; and so he uses their evil for his own good, as God too draws many goods out of the evils of others. Hence Thomas says in the Secunda Secundae, question 78: It is in no way lawful to lead another into sin; but to use another's evil and sin for good is lawful. For God too uses sinners for good, when he draws good out of their evils. Hence Augustine, when Publicola asked whether it is lawful to make use of the oath of one who swears by false gods, answered that one who makes use of the oath of such a swearer does not associate himself with his sin, but with his good pact, by which he kept faith: but he would sin if he led him to swear by false gods.

paras.t: Da mihi in animo constantiam, ne feminea instabilitate aut mollitie seu formidine vincar aut flectar, ut contemnam illum, non in quantum homo est et in officio constitutus, sed in quantum iniquus est ac tyrannus, hostis divini cultus fidelisque populi, et virtutem, id est abusum potestatis ejus, ut evertam illum. Sic enim de justo cantatur: Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus. Et justus fatetur: Despexit oculus meus inimicos meos. Erit enim hoc memoriale nominis tui, id est opus commemoratione dignissimum, in quo omnipotentiæ ac sapientiæ atque justitiæ tuæ excellentia relucebit ac recoletur, imo laudabitur, quum manus feminæ dejecerit eum, id est tam superbum, crudelem ac superbissimum hominem, cui nullus virorum seu principum potest aut audet resistere: unde apertissime innotescet, hoc esse opus providentiæ tuæ justissimæ, quæ superbos humiliat, et tam arrogantissimum, tam confusibiliter (ut confido) calcabit. Unde Abimelech videns se per mulierem letaliter vulneratum, dixit armigero suo: Evagina gladium tuum, et percute me, ne forte dicatur quod a femina interfectus sim.
paras.en: [[9:14|Give me constancy in my mind|Da mihi in animo constantiam]], that I may not be overcome or bent by a woman's instability, softness or fear, [[9:14|that I may despise him|ut contemnam illum]], not inasmuch as he is a man and set in office, but inasmuch as he is wicked and a tyrant, an enemy of divine worship and of the faithful people; [[9:14|and fortitude|et virtutem]] [Denis seems to take *virtutem* with *contemnam*: "that I may despise him and his power"], that is, the abuse of his power, [[9:14|that I may overthrow him|ut evertam illum]]. For so it is sung of the just man: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]]. And the just man confesses: [[Ps 91:12|My eye also hath looked down upon my enemies|Despexit oculus meus inimicos meos]]. [[9:15|For this will be a glorious monument for thy name|Erit enim hoc memoriale nominis tui]], that is, a work most worthy of remembrance, in which the excellence of thy almighty power, wisdom and justice will shine forth and be recalled, nay praised, [[9:15|when he shall fall by the hand of a woman|quum manus feminæ dejecerit eum]] [literally "when the hand of a woman shall cast him down"], that is, a man so proud, cruel and most proud, whom none of men or princes can or dare resist: whence it will be most plainly known that this is the work of thy most just providence, which humbles the proud and will trample, so shamefully (as I trust), one so very arrogant. Hence Abimelech, seeing himself mortally wounded by a woman, said to his armour-bearer: [[Judg 9:54|Draw thy sword, and kill me: lest it should be said that I was slain by a woman|Evagina gladium tuum, et percute me, ne forte dicatur quod a femina interfectus sim]].

paras.t: Non enim in multitudine est virtus tua, Domine: id est, potestas tua non consistit in copioso exercitu, sicut potestas regis terreni sita est in multitudine adjuvantium eum; sed tu ex te et per te omnipotens es, et tua potestate potes dare triumphum tam bene per unum, sicut per multos: quemadmodum primo Regum libro Jonathas ait, Non est Domino difficile salvari in multis vel in paucis. Secundo quoque Paralipomenon Asa rex, Domine, inquit, non est apud te ulla distantia, utrum in paucis auxilieris, an in pluribus. Neque in equorum viribus voluntas tua est, id est, beneplacitum tibi non est in fortitudine equorum, sed in spe et devotione tuorum fidelium: juxta illud Psalmistæ, Non in fortitudine equi voluntatem habebit, nec in tibiis viri beneplacitum erit ei. Ideo in Proverbiis asseritur: Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet. Neque superbi ab initio placuerunt tibi: imo in prima ætate mundi superbos gigantes, et in principio creationis superbientes angelos dejecisti; sed humilium et mansuetorum tibi semper placuit deprecatio: quum in Ecclesiastico scriptum sit, Oratio humiliantis se nubes penetrabit: atque in Psalmo, Exaltabit mansuetos in salutem. Hæ namque duæ virtutes Deo præcipue placent, et invicem sunt germanæ, ac tantæ excellentiæ, ut eas Christus potissime commendaverit a se esse discendas: Discite, inquiens, a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Unde et divinus Dionysius in epistola ad Demophilum scribit: Moyses, David et Joseph maximam apud Dominum gratiam invenerunt, quoniam mansueti fuerunt.
paras.en: [[9:16|For thy power, O Lord, is not in a multitude|Non enim in multitudine est virtus tua, Domine]]: that is, thy might does not consist in a large army, as the might of an earthly king lies in the multitude of those who help him; but thou art almighty of thyself and through thyself, and by thy power canst give the victory as well through one as through many: as Jonathas says in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 14:6|it is easy for the Lord to save either by many, or by few|Non est Domino difficile salvari in multis vel in paucis]]. And in the second of Paralipomenon King Asa says: [[2 Par 14:11|Lord,|Domine]] he says, [[2 Par 14:11|there is no difference with thee, whether thou help with few, or with many|non est apud te ulla distantia, utrum in paucis auxilieris, an in pluribus]]. [[9:16|nor is thy pleasure in the strength of horses|Neque in equorum viribus voluntas tua est]], that is, thy good pleasure is not in the strength of horses, but in the hope and devotion of thy faithful: according to that word of the Psalmist: [[Ps 146:10|He shall not delight in the strength of the horse: nor take pleasure in the legs of a man|Non in fortitudine equi voluntatem habebit, nec in tibiis viri beneplacitum erit ei]]. Therefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 21:31|The horse is prepared for the day of battle: but the Lord giveth safety|Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet]]. [[9:16|nor from the beginning have the proud been acceptable to thee|Neque superbi ab initio placuerunt tibi]]: rather, in the first age of the world thou didst cast down the proud giants[[Gen 6:4||]], and at the beginning of creation the angels who grew proud[[Is 14:12||]]; [[9:16|but the prayer of the humble and the meek hath always pleased thee|sed humilium et mansuetorum tibi semper placuit deprecatio]], since it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:21|The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds|Oratio humiliantis se nubes penetrabit]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 149:4|he will exalt the meek unto salvation|Exaltabit mansuetos in salutem]]. For these two virtues especially please God, and are sisters to each other, and of such excellence that Christ most especially commended them as to be learnt from him: [[Matt 11:29|learn|Discite]], he says, [[Matt 11:29|of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. Hence the divine Dionysius too writes in his letter to Demophilus: Moses[[Num 12:3||]], David[[Ps 131:1||]] and Joseph[[Gen 45:5||]] found the greatest grace with the Lord, because they were meek.

paras.t: Deus cælorum, creator aquarum, et Domine totius creaturæ, cujus potestati nullus potest resistere, exaudi me miseram deprecantem, id est afflictam et populo meo intime condolentem, ac periculo magno expositam, nisi succurras: quia quum pulchra sim, me impii illi in primis fœdarent; et de tua misericordia præsumentem, quia per te facere spero, quod meis viribus me posse implere diffido. Memento, Domine, testamenti tui, id est pacti quod cum patribus nostris inisti, quibus et promisisti quod posteritati eorum ad te confugienti succurreres; et memor sis observantiæ ac religionis testamenti, quod per Moysen nobis mandasti, ut eas conserves; et da verbum efficax, sapientiale et bene sonans, in ore meo, dando mihi gratiam sic loquendi, quod propositum meum sortiatur effectum, et in corde meo consilium corrobora, ut bene judicem de agendis: ut domus tua, videlicet templum, in tua sanctificatione, id est in sancto cultu tuo et in consecratione, permaneat, nec violetur per impios. Et omnes gentes agnoscant, per victoriam nobis tua virtute præstandam, quoniam tu es Deus, et alius non est præter te, id est, quod tu solus sis verus Deus, imo quod nullus habeat esse plenum atque perfectum, nisi tu, cujus comparatione omne creatum esse, est velut non esse.
paras.en: [[9:17|O God of the heavens|Deus cælorum]], [[9:17|creator of the waters|creator aquarum]], [[9:17|and Lord of the whole creation|et Domine totius creaturæ]], whose power none can resist, [[9:17|hear me a poor wretch, making supplication to thee|exaudi me miseram deprecantem]], that is, afflicted and grieving inwardly with my people, and exposed to great danger unless thou help: for since I am fair, those wicked men would defile me first of all; [[9:17|and presuming of thy mercy|et de tua misericordia præsumentem]], because I hope to do through thee what I distrust that I can accomplish by my own strength. [[9:18|Remember, O Lord, thy covenant|Memento, Domine, testamenti tui]], that is, the pact which thou madest with our fathers, to whom thou didst also promise to help their posterity when it fled to thee; and be mindful of the observance and religion of the covenant which thou didst command us through Moses, that thou mayest preserve them [Latin *eas*, apparently the observances]; [[9:18|and put thou words|et da verbum]], effective, wise and well-sounding, [[9:18|in my mouth|in ore meo]], giving me the grace so to speak that my purpose may obtain its effect, [[9:18|and strengthen the resolution in my heart|et in corde meo consilium corrobora]], that I may judge well what is to be done: [[9:18|that thy house|ut domus tua]], namely the temple, [[9:18|may continue|permaneat]] [[9:18|in thy holiness|in tua sanctificatione]], that is, in thy holy worship and in its consecration, and not be violated by the wicked. [[9:19|And all nations may acknowledge|Et omnes gentes agnoscant]], through the victory to be granted us by thy power, [[9:19|that thou art God|quoniam tu es Deus]], [[9:19|and there is no other besides thee|et alius non est præter te]], that is, that thou alone art the true God[[Ex 20:2||]][[Deut 32:39||]], nay, that none has full and perfect being but thou, in comparison with whom all created being is as not being.

10.title: Expositio capituli decimi: Factum est autem quum cessasset clamare ad Dominum
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: And it came to pass, when she had ceased to cry to the Lord

paras.t: Quomodo Judith se ornavit, et Holoferni occurrit, hic recitatur.
paras.en: How Judith adorned herself and went out to meet Holofernes is told here.

paras.t: Factum est autem quum cessasset clamare ad Dominum, id est, orationem suam complesset: in qua clamavit potius fervore devotionis, quam altitudine vocis; surrexit de loco in quo jacuerat prostrata ad Dominum, vocavitque abram suam, id est ancillam, non qualemcumque, sed valde electam, quam noverat aliis ancillis prudentiorem et constantiorem ac multum fidelem. Vel dicitur abra, quia paulo post eam libertati donavit. Et descendens in domum suam, abstulit a se cilicium, et exuit se vestimentis viduitatis suæ. Viduas enim decet humilis, simplex, non curiosus vestitus. Unde in Genesi legitur, Thamar deposuisse vestimenta viduitatis.
paras.en: [[10:1|And it came to pass, when she had ceased to cry to the Lord|Factum est autem quum cessasset clamare ad Dominum]], that is, when she had finished her prayer, in which she cried out with the fervour of devotion rather than with a loud voice, [[10:1|that she rose from the place wherein she lay prostrate before the Lord|surrexit de loco in quo jacuerat prostrata ad Dominum]]; [[10:2|And she called her maid|vocavitque abram suam]], that is, her handmaid: not just any one, but one carefully chosen, whom she knew to be more prudent and steadfast than her other handmaids, and very faithful. Or she is called *abra* [a favoured handmaid] because a little later she gave her her freedom [see 16:28]. Then, [[10:2|going down into her house she took off her haircloth, and put away the garments of her widowhood|descendens in domum suam, abstulit a se cilicium, et exuit se vestimentis viduitatis suæ]]. For a humble, simple dress, not studied, becomes widows. Hence we read in Genesis that Thamar put off the garments of her widowhood[[Gen 38:14||]] [the margin prints Gen. xxxvi, 14; the passage is Gen 38:14].

paras.t: Et lavit corpus suum, forsan in balneo, ut capacius fieret unctionis. Et unxit se myrrho optimo, id est unguento odorifero facto de myrrha. Et discriminavit, id est divisit et ornate distinxit, crinem capitis sui, per discriminalia seu pectines: de quibus in Isaia legitur. Et imposuit mitram super caput suum, id est sertum quoddam caput decorans. Et induit se vestimentis jucunditatis, id est vestibus quibus in magnis solenniis utebatur, vel viro suo vivente solebat aliquando uti, sive in nuptiis, et consimilibus jucundis negotiis. Induitque sandalia pedibus suis, id est calceamenta pulchra: in quibus solent celebrare Papa et præsules. Assumpsitque dextraliola, id est dextræ ornamenta, et lilia, id est ornamenta ad caput pendentia, instar liliorum formata, et inaures, id est aurium ornamenta, et annulos, qui ponuntur in digitis, et omnibus ornamentis suis ornavit se. Cui etiam Dominus contulit splendorem, augendo gratiose ejus decorem. Quoniam omnis ista compositio non ex libidine, sed ex virtute pendebat, id est ex magnitudine caritatis populi sui, quem cupivit a periculo liberare, et ex plenitudine devotionis qua affectavit cultum Dei in suo conservare vigore. Et ideo Dominus in illa hanc pulchritudinem ampliavit, ut incomparabili decore omnium oculis appareret.
paras.en: [[10:3|And she washed her body|Et lavit corpus suum]], perhaps in a bath, so that it might better take the anointing; [[10:3|and anointed herself with the best ointment|Et unxit se myrrho optimo]], that is, with a fragrant ointment made of myrrh; [[10:3|and plaited|Et discriminavit]], that is, parted and neatly arranged [*discriminavit*, properly “parted”], [[10:3|the hair of her head|crinem capitis sui]], with *discriminalia* or combs [the Douay-Rheims renders *discriminalia* “bodkins”], of which we read in Isaias[[Is 3:20||]]; [[10:3|and put a bonnet upon her head|Et imposuit mitram super caput suum]], that is, a kind of chaplet adorning the head; [[10:3|and clothed herself with the garments of her gladness|Et induit se vestimentis jucunditatis]], that is, with the clothes she used to wear at great solemnities, or used sometimes to wear while her husband was living, at weddings and other such joyful occasions; [[10:3|and put sandals on her feet|Induitque sandalia pedibus suis]], that is, fine shoes, such as the Pope and prelates are wont to wear when they celebrate; [[10:3|and took her bracelets|Assumpsitque dextraliola]], that is, ornaments of the right arm [*dextraliola*, from *dextra*, the right hand], [[10:3|and lilies|et lilia]], that is, ornaments hanging from the head, shaped like lilies, [[10:3|and earlets|et inaures]], that is, ornaments of the ears, [[10:3|and rings|et annulos]], which are worn on the fingers, [[10:3|and adorned herself with all her ornaments|et omnibus ornamentis suis ornavit se]]. [[10:4|And the Lord also gave her more beauty|Cui etiam Dominus contulit splendorem]], graciously increasing her comeliness, [[10:4|because all this dressing up did not proceed from sensuality, but from virtue|Quoniam omnis ista compositio non ex libidine, sed ex virtute pendebat]], that is, from the greatness of her love for her people, whom she longed to deliver from danger, and from the fulness of devotion with which she strove to keep the worship of God in its vigour; [[10:4|and therefore the Lord increased this her beauty, so that she appeared to all men's eyes incomparably lovely|Et ideo Dominus in illa hanc pulchritudinem ampliavit, ut incomparabili decore omnium oculis appareret]].

paras.t: Imposuit itaque abræ suæ ascopam, id est mensuram seu utrem vini, et vas olei, id est vasculum cum oleo, et polentam, id est subtilem farinam aut cibum inde confectum; vel est genus leguminis; et lapates, id est cibos de oleribus, vel secundum quosdam de ficubus factos, et panem, et caseum, ut his interim vescerentur, non gentilium escis; et profecta est.
paras.en: [[10:5|And she gave to her maid a bottle|Imposuit itaque abræ suæ ascopam]] [the margin gives the reading *ascoperam*, the Vulgate's], that is, a measure or skin [[10:5|of wine|vini]], [[10:5|and a vessel of oil|et vas olei]], that is, a little vessel with oil in it, [[10:5|and parched corn|et polentam]], that is, fine meal or food made from it, or else it is a kind of pulse, [[10:5|and dry figs|et lapates]], that is, dishes of herbs, or, according to some, of figs [Denis's text reads *lapates*, which the first gloss takes as a pot-herb (*lapathum*, sorrel); the margin gives the Vulgate's *palathas*, cakes of dried figs], [[10:5|and bread and cheese|et panem, et caseum]], so that they might live on these meanwhile, and not on the food of the Gentiles; [[10:5|and went out|et profecta est]].

paras.t: Quumque venissent ad portam civitatis Bethuliæ, invenerunt exspectantem Oziam et presbyteros civitatis. Qui quum vidissent eam, stupentes, mirati sunt nimis pulchritudinem ejus Ozias et sacerdotes. Nihil tamen interrogantes, eam dimiserunt, dicentes: Deus patrum nostrorum det tibi gratiam, id est prosperum successum in exsecutione tui propositi, et omne consilium tui cordis sua virtute corroboret, et glorietur super te Jerusalem, et sit nomen tuum in numero sanctorum. Et dixerunt hi qui illic erant, omnes una voce: Fiat, fiat. Judith vero orans Dominum, transivit per portas.
paras.en: [[10:6|And when they came to the gate of the city|Quumque venissent ad portam civitatis]] of Bethulia, [[10:6|they found Ozias, and the ancients of the city waiting|invenerunt exspectantem Oziam et presbyteros civitatis]]. [[10:7|And when they saw her they were astonished, and admired her beauty exceedingly|Qui quum vidissent eam, stupentes, mirati sunt nimis pulchritudinem ejus]], Ozias and the priests. [[10:8|But they asked her no question, only they let her pass, saying|Nihil tamen interrogantes, eam dimiserunt, dicentes]]: [[10:8|The God of our fathers give thee grace|Deus patrum nostrorum det tibi gratiam]], that is, good success in carrying out thy purpose, [[10:8|and may he strengthen all the counsel of thy heart with his power|et omne consilium tui cordis sua virtute corroboret]], [[10:8|that Jerusalem may glory in thee|et glorietur super te Jerusalem]], [[10:8|and thy name may be in the number of the holy|et sit nomen tuum in numero sanctorum]] [the print is damaged in this verse; its words are read with the help of the Vulgate]. [[10:9|And they that were there said, all with one voice: So be it, so be it.|Et dixerunt hi qui illic erant, omnes una voce: Fiat, fiat]] [[10:10|But Judith praying to the Lord, passed through the gates|Judith vero orans Dominum, transivit per portas]].

paras.t: Factum est autem quum descenderet montem, qui erat extra et prope Bethuliam, circa ortum diei, occurrerunt ei exploratores Assyriorum, id est observatores qui per gyrum urbis observabant, ne quis de urbe effugeret, et tenuerunt eam, dicentes: Unde venis? aut quo vadis? Quæ respondit: Filia sum Hebræorum. Ideo ego fugi a facie eorum, quoniam futurum agnovi quod dentur vobis in deprædationem, id est, vestræ voluntati exponantur ad deprædandum, pro eo quod contemnentes vos, noluerunt ultro, id est sponte, tradere se ipsos in manus vestras, ut invenirent misericordiam in conspectu vestro. Hac de causa cogitavi mecum, dicens: Vadam ad faciem principis Holofernis, ut indicem illi secreta illorum, et ostendam illi quo aditu, id est accessu, possit obtinere eos, ita ut non cadat unus de exercitu ejus. Et quum audissent viri illi verba ejus, considerabant faciem ejus, et erat in oculis eorum stupor, quoniam pulchritudinem ejus mirabantur nimis. Et dixerunt ad eam: Conservasti animam tuam, eo quod tale reperisti consilium, ut descenderes ad dominum nostrum. Hoc autem scias, quoniam quum steteris in conspectu ejus, bene tibi faciet, et eris gratissima in corde ipsius.
paras.en: [[10:11|And it came to pass, when she went down the hill|Factum est autem quum descenderet montem]], which was outside and near Bethulia, [[10:11|about break of day, that the watchmen of the Assyrians met her|circa ortum diei, occurrerunt ei exploratores Assyriorum]], that is, the observers who kept watch round about the city lest anyone should escape from it, [[10:11|and stopped her, saying: Whence comest thou or whither goest thou?|et tenuerunt eam, dicentes: Unde venis? aut quo vadis?]] [[10:12|And she answered: I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I am fled from them, because I knew they would be made a prey to you|Quæ respondit: Filia sum Hebræorum. Ideo ego fugi a facie eorum, quoniam futurum agnovi quod dentur vobis in deprædationem]], that is, that they would be given over to your will to be plundered, [[10:12|because they despised you, and would not of their own accord|pro eo quod contemnentes vos, noluerunt ultro]], that is, willingly, [[10:12|yield themselves|tradere se ipsos]] into your hands, [[10:12|that they might find mercy in your sight|ut invenirent misericordiam in conspectu vestro]]. [[10:13|For this reason I thought with myself, saying: I will go to the presence of the prince Holofernes, that I may tell him their secrets, and shew him by what way|Hac de causa cogitavi mecum, dicens: Vadam ad faciem principis Holofernis, ut indicem illi secreta illorum, et ostendam illi quo aditu]], that is, by what approach, [[10:13|he may take them, without the loss of one man of his army|possit obtinere eos, ita ut non cadat unus de exercitu ejus]]. [[10:14|And when the men had heard her words, they beheld her face, and their eyes were amazed, for they wondered exceedingly at her beauty.|Et quum audissent viri illi verba ejus, considerabant faciem ejus, et erat in oculis eorum stupor, quoniam pulchritudinem ejus mirabantur nimis]] [[10:15|And they said to her: Thou hast saved thy life by taking this resolution, to come down to our lord.|Et dixerunt ad eam: Conservasti animam tuam, eo quod tale reperisti consilium, ut descenderes ad dominum nostrum]] [[10:16|And be assured of this, that when thou shalt stand before him, he will treat thee well, and thou wilt be most acceptable to his heart|Hoc autem scias, quoniam quum steteris in conspectu ejus, bene tibi faciet, et eris gratissima in corde ipsius]].

paras.t: Circa hæc dubia duo occurrunt. Primum, an licite ita ornavit se. Et videtur quod non, quum sancti patres testentur quod vir aut mulier ornate se vestiens seu adornans, et suo ornatu oculos hominum in se provocans, etiamsi nullum damnum inde sequatur, tamen æternum supplicium patietur, quia venenum præbuit, si fuisset qui biberet. Qui enim sic agit, alios, quantum in se est, scandalizat. Et væ homini per quem scandalum venit. Aliud est, an mentita sit, et mentiendo peccaverit, proferendo verba jam tacta. Et videtur evidenter esse mentita et peccasse, falsum scienter et ex proposito proferendo.
paras.en: Two doubts arise about these things. The first is whether she adorned herself so lawfully. And it seems not, since the holy Fathers testify that a man or woman who dresses or adorns himself finely, and by that finery draws men's eyes to himself, even if no harm follows from it, will nevertheless suffer eternal punishment, because he offered poison, had there been anyone to drink it. For whoever acts so gives scandal to others, as far as in him lies; and [[Matt 18:7|woe to that man by whom the scandal cometh|væ homini per quem scandalum venit]]. The other is whether she lied, and sinned by lying, in speaking the words just touched on. And it seems plain that she lied and sinned, saying what was false knowingly and of set purpose.

paras.t: Ad primum horum videtur dicendum, secundum prætacta in præcedenti articulo, quod ornatus ille excusetur a culpa, quia sic decoravit se, ut posset congruenter appeti ab Holoferne in conjugem, et hoc ultra retulit ad populi sui liberationem: quamvis talia non sint passim ad imitationem trahenda, sicut nec alia multa quæ in Scripturis leguntur, et ex inspiratione divina processisse creduntur, nec aliter excusarentur.
paras.en: To the first of these it seems we must say, according to what was touched on in the preceding article[[Jdt 9:1||]] [the margin gives Judith ix], that this adornment is excused from fault, because she so adorned herself that she might fittingly be desired by Holofernes as a wife, and she referred this further to the deliverance of her people; although such things are not to be drawn into imitation at large, any more than many other things which we read in the Scriptures, and which are believed to have proceeded from divine inspiration, and would not otherwise be excused.

paras.t: Ad aliud quidam respondent, quod Judith mystice sit locuta. Alii dicunt, secundum quod littera sonat, quod mentita sit mendacio officioso, venialiterque peccavit. Quibus objici posset, quia mendacium officiosum est, quod est alicui utile et nulli nocivum. Hæc autem verba Judith referebantur ab ea ad Holofernis deceptionem, imo et interfectionem. Verum ad hoc posset responderi, quod Holofernes promeruit sic decipi et occidi, atque utilius ei fuit tolli de medio, quam vivendo diutius tot crimina perpetrare. Videtur quoque dici posse, quod ironice sit locuta, secundum quod tertio Regum Michæas ait ad Achab: Ascende et vade prospere, et tradet Dominus in manu regis. Et tales locutiones sunt etiam in Scripturis frequentes. Tamen, ut probabiliter dicitur, non oportet ipsam Judith a veniali mendacio excusari.
paras.en: To the other, some answer that Judith spoke mystically. Others say, according to the sound of the letter, that she lied with an officious lie [that is, a lie told to help someone, not to harm], and sinned venially. Against these it could be objected that an officious lie is one that is useful to someone and harmful to no one; but these words of Judith were directed by her to the deceiving of Holofernes, nay, even to his killing. Yet to this it could be answered that Holofernes deserved to be so deceived and slain, and that it was more useful to him to be taken out of the way than to commit so many crimes by living longer. It seems too that it can be said that she spoke ironically, as in the third book of Kings Micheas says to Achab: [[3 Kings 22:15|Go up, and prosper|Ascende et vade prospere]], [[3 Kings 22:15|and the Lord shall deliver it into the king's hands|et tradet Dominus in manu regis]] [the margin, partly unreadable, seems to give III Reg. xxii, 12, 15: the false prophets say this at v. 12, where the Vulgate, like Denis, has no word for *it*; Micheas repeats it in irony at v. 15]. And such ways of speaking are frequent in the Scriptures too. Yet, as is said with good reason, there is no need to clear Judith herself of a venial lie.

paras.t: Duxeruntque illam ad tabernaculum Holofernis. Quumque intrasset ante faciem ejus, statim captus est in oculis suis, id est, mox ut eam vidit, vulneratus est concupiscentia, quæ fuit ei deceptionis et mortis occasio. Dixeruntque ad eum satellites ejus: Quis contemnat populum Hebræorum, qui tam decoras habet mulieres, ut non pro his merito pugnare debeamus contra eos? quasi dicant: Non sunt Hebræi isti tam aspernandi, quin dignum sit nos contra eos pugnare, eo quod uxores eorum ac filiæ sint tam pulchræ. Istud fuit et unum malum, præter intentionem venerabilis Judith, ex ejus ornatu secutum, quod scilicet Assyrii ex ea sic decorata, amplius accendebantur ad invadendum Judæos, et ad violandum eorum filias et uxores.
paras.en: [[10:16|And they brought her to the tent of Holofernes|Duxeruntque illam ad tabernaculum Holofernis]]. [[10:17|And when she was come into his presence, forthwith|Quumque intrasset ante faciem ejus, statim]] Holofernes [[10:17|was caught by his eyes|captus est in oculis suis]], that is, as soon as he saw her he was wounded with concupiscence, which was the occasion of his being deceived and of his death. [[10:18|And his officers said to him: Who can despise the people of the Hebrews, who have such beautiful women, that we should not think it worth our while for their sakes to fight against them?|Dixeruntque ad eum satellites ejus: Quis contemnat populum Hebræorum, qui tam decoras habet mulieres, ut non pro his merito pugnare debeamus contra eos?]] As if to say: These Hebrews are not so much to be despised that it is not worth our while to fight against them, since their wives and daughters are so beautiful. This too was one evil that followed from her adornment, beyond the intention of the venerable Judith: namely, that the Assyrians, from seeing her so adorned, were the more inflamed to invade the Jews and to violate their daughters and wives.

paras.t: Videns itaque Judith Holofernem sedentem in conopeo, id est in throno seu solio suo, ad cujus sedis magnificentiam et ornatum fuit appensum subtilissimum rete, sericumve resticulum, defendens adversus muscarum et culicum morsum, quod erat ex auro et bysso, et purpura, et smaragdo, et lapidibus pretiosis intextum, id est insertum. Et quum in faciem ejus intendisset, adoravit eum adoratione duliæ: vel ex simulatione, vel ex potestatis ipsius consideratione, quia non est potestas nisi a Deo: imo ad procurandum sibi benevolentiam ejus in interitum ipsius; prosternens se super terram. Et elevaverunt eam servi Holofernis, jubente domino suo.
paras.en: [[10:19|And Judith seeing Holofernes sitting under a canopy|Videns itaque Judith Holofernem sedentem in conopeo]], that is, on his throne or seat, to the magnificence and adornment of which a very fine net was hung, or a little net of silk, protecting against the bites of flies and gnats, [[10:19|which was woven of purple and gold, with emeralds and precious stones|quod erat ex auro et bysso, et purpura, et smaragdo, et lapidibus pretiosis intextum]] [Denis's text adds *et bysso*, “and fine linen”], that is, set in. [[10:20|After she had looked on his face, bowed down to him|Et quum in faciem ejus intendisset, adoravit eum]] with the adoration of dulia [that is, the honour paid to a creature, as distinct from *latria*, the worship due to God alone]: either in pretence, or out of regard for his power, since [[Rom 13:1|there is no power but from God|non est potestas nisi a Deo]]; nay rather, to win his goodwill for herself, to his destruction; [[10:20|prostrating herself to the ground. And the servants of Holofernes lifted her up, by the command of their master|prosternens se super terram. Et elevaverunt eam servi Holofernis, jubente domino suo]].

11.title: Explanatio capituli undecimi: Tunc Holofernes dixit ei: Æquo animo esto
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: Then Holofernes said to her: Be of good comfort

paras.t: Responsio Judith ad Holofernem, hic scribitur.
paras.en: Here is written Judith's answer to Holofernes.

paras.t: Tunc Holofernes dixit ei: Æquo animo esto, et noli pavere in corde tuo. Jam per concupiscentiam victus, cœpit molliter loqui, cupiens feminæ complacere. Quoniam ego nunquam nocui, id est læsi, viro qui voluit absque omni renisu servire Nabuchodonosor regi. Populus autem tuus, si non contempsisset me, non allevassem lanceam meam super eum. Nunc autem, dic mihi, qua ex causa recessisti ab illis, et placuit tibi ut venires ad nos.
paras.en: [[11:1|Then Holofernes said to her: Be of good comfort, and fear not in thy heart|Tunc Holofernes dixit ei: Æquo animo esto, et noli pavere in corde tuo]]. Being now overcome by concupiscence, he began to speak softly, wanting to please the woman. [[11:1|for I have never hurt|Quoniam ego nunquam nocui]], that is, injured, [[11:1|a man that was willing|viro qui voluit]] without any resistance [[11:1|to serve Nabuchodonosor the king|servire Nabuchodonosor regi]]. [[11:2|And if thy people had not despised me, I would never have lifted up my spear against them.|Populus autem tuus, si non contempsisset me, non allevassem lanceam meam super eum]] [[11:3|But now tell me, for what cause hast thou left them, and why it hath pleased thee to come to us?|Nunc autem, dic mihi, qua ex causa recessisti ab illis, et placuit tibi ut venires ad nos]]

paras.t: Et dicit Judith: Sume ancillæ tuæ verba, quoniam si secutus fueris verba ancillæ tuæ, faciet rem perfectam Dominus tecum, id est, perfectum opus justitiæ faciet in te, interficiendo te per me. Hæc fuit intentio Judith. Quæ tamen per verba hic dedit Holoferni intelligere, quod Deus daret ei perfectam victoriam de Hebræis. Intendebat namque eum decipere, secundum quod in bello justo licet uti insidiis, ut Josue ostendit, ac in Judicum libro patet simile. Nam et verbis obscuris licitum est veritatem celare, non autem mentiri.
paras.en: [[11:4|And Judith said|Et dicit Judith]]: [[11:4|Receive the words of thy handmaid|Sume ancillæ tuæ verba]], [[11:4|for if thou wilt follow the words of thy handmaid, the Lord will do with thee a perfect thing|quoniam si secutus fueris verba ancillæ tuæ, faciet rem perfectam Dominus tecum]], that is, he will do a perfect work of justice upon thee, by killing thee through me. This was Judith's intention. Yet by these words she gave Holofernes to understand that God would give him a perfect victory over the Hebrews. For she meant to deceive him, inasmuch as in a just war it is lawful to use ambushes, as Josue shows[[Jos 8:1||]], and the like is plain in the book of Judges[[Judg 9:1||]][[Judg 20:1||]] [the margin's Josue vii (or viii) is taken as Jos 8, the ambush at Hai; its Judic. ix and a second, partly unreadable chapter as Judg 9 and 20, the ambushes of Abimelech and at Gabaa]. For it is lawful to hide the truth with obscure words, but not to lie.

paras.t: Vivit enim Nabuchodonosor rex terræ, non totius terræ, sed magnæ partis ipsius, intelligendo per terram, habitatores ejus; et vivit virtus ejus quæ est in te, id est, potestas ejus tibi commissa viget, et operatur per te ad correptionem omnium animarum errantium, id est ad castigandum et emendandum quosdam de omni genere peccantium, circa quos Holofernes et rex ejus erant flagellum divinæ justitiæ. Dicuntque aliqui, ipsam Judith dixisse hæc verba jurando, sicut consuetudinis est Scripturæ, per hanc formam verborum, Vivit Dominus, jurare. Et sic Joseph legitur per salutem Pharaonis jurasse. Sed contra hoc objicit quidam, quod Judith non excusaretur a falso juramento, quod est mortale peccatum. Quæ objectio non apparet idonea: quod enim mox subditur, ad cujus assertionem verba illa inducuntur, est verum, videlicet, quoniam non solum homines serviunt ei per te, sed et bestiæ agri obtemperant illi. Quod de hominibus certum est. De bestiis vero, verificatur eo modo, quo per Jeremiam et Ezechielem [Deus] prædixit: Insuper et bestias agri dedi ei, seu bestiæ agri obedient illi, videlicet Nabuchodonosor regi Chaldæorum. Dicuntur autem bestiæ obtemperare homini metaphorice.
paras.en: [[11:5|For as Nabuchodonosor the king of the earth liveth|Vivit enim Nabuchodonosor rex terræ]]: not of the whole earth, but of a great part of it, understanding by the earth its inhabitants; [[11:5|and his power liveth which is in thee|et vivit virtus ejus quæ est in te]], that is, his power entrusted to thee is strong, and works through thee [[11:5|for chastising of all straying souls|ad correptionem omnium animarum errantium]], that is, for chastising and amending some of every kind of sinner, for whom Holofernes and his king were the scourge of divine justice. And some say that Judith spoke these words by way of an oath, as it is the custom of Scripture to swear by this form of words: As the Lord liveth.
