And so we read that Joseph swore [[Gen 42:15|by the health of Pharao|per salutem Pharaonis]] [the margin's numerals are partly unreadable; the passage is Gen 42:15]. But against this someone objects that Judith would then not be excused from a false oath, which is a mortal sin. This objection does not seem sound: for what is added straight after, for the assertion of which those words are brought in, is true, namely, that [[11:5|not only men serve him through thee, but also the beasts of the field obey him|non solum homines serviunt ei per te, sed et bestiæ agri obtemperant illi]]. This is certain of men. Of the beasts it is made true in the way in which God foretold through Jeremias and Ezechiel: [[Jer 27:6|moreover also the beasts of the field I have given him|Insuper et bestias agri dedi ei]], or, the beasts of the field shall obey him, that is, Nabuchodonosor king of the Chaldeans. Now the beasts are said to obey a man metaphorically.

paras.t: Nuntiatur enim industria, id est solertia, animi tui universis gentibus, id est quibusdam de omnibus, et indicatum est omni sæculo, id est cunctis habitantibus nunc in mundo, id est quibusdam de cunctis: ut sit distributio accommoda atque locutio hyperbolica: quoniam tu solus bonus et potens es in omni regno ejus, id est præcipue bonus in tuo officio, et potens in civili regimine, ac summus post regem. Constitutis enim in officio publico solet attribui bonitas dignitatis, quamvis vitiosi exsistant, sicut et Paulus apostolus in Actis ait judici incredulo: Non insanio, optime Feste. Et disciplina tua, id est informatio seu increpatio pungitiva circa rebelles, omnibus provinciis prædicatur.
paras.en: [[11:6|For the industry|Nuntiatur enim industria]], that is, the skill, [[11:6|of thy mind is spoken of among all nations|animi tui universis gentibus]], that is, among some of all of them, [[11:6|and it is told through the whole world|et indicatum est omni sæculo]], that is, to all who now dwell in the world, that is, to some of all of them; so that it is an accommodated distribution [that is, *all* taken for some of every kind, not for every one] and a hyperbolic way of speaking: [[11:6|that thou only art excellent, and mighty in all his kingdom|quoniam tu solus bonus et potens es in omni regno ejus]], that is, especially good in thy office, and mighty in civil government, and highest after the king. For to those set in public office the goodness of their dignity is wont to be ascribed, though they be wicked, as the apostle Paul too says in the Acts to an unbelieving judge: [[Acts 26:25|I am not mad, most excellent Festus|Non insanio, optime Feste]]. [[11:6|and thy discipline|Et disciplina tua]], that is, thy stinging instruction or rebuke of the rebellious, [[11:6|is cried up in all provinces|omnibus provinciis prædicatur]].

paras.t: Nec hoc latet quod locutus est Achior: cujus verba supra habentur; nec illud latet, quod jusseris ei evenire: quod itidem continetur supra. Constat enim, Deum nostrum sic peccatis offensum a populo nostro, ut mandaverit, id est insinuaverit, per Prophetas suos ad populum Hebræorum, quod tradat eum adversariis, pro peccatis suis. Hoc simpliciter est verum, si referatur ad tempora præcedentia, seu subsequentia tempus Judith, non autem videtur verificari pro tempore illo. Et quoniam sciunt se offendisse Deum suum filii Israel, tremor tuus super ipsos est, id est, in eis est tremor ex consideratione excellentiæ et iracundiæ tuæ adversus eos. Insuper etiam fames invasit eos; et ab ariditate aquæ, id est præ siccitate sitis quam patiuntur ex carentia aquæ seu potus: juxta quem modum loquendi fertur in Psalmo: Caro mea immutata est propter oleum, id est ex defectu olei: jam inter mortuos computantur, id est, quasi mortui sunt: sicut de homine agonizante dicimus, quod sit mortuus homo. Unde et primo libro Regum David fatetur: Ego et mors uno tantum gradu dividimur. Ista ad litteram ita erant.
paras.en: [[11:7|It is known also what Achior said|Nec hoc latet quod locutus est Achior]], whose words are given above[[Jdt 5:5||]] [the margin gives Judith v, 5–25]; [[11:7|nor are we ignorant of what thou hast commanded to be done to him|nec illud latet, quod jusseris ei evenire]], which likewise is contained above[[Jdt 6:7||]] [the margin note here is unreadable; the order is given at 6:7]. [[11:8|For it is certain that our God is so offended with sins|Constat enim, Deum nostrum sic peccatis offensum]] by our people, [[11:8|that he hath sent word|ut mandaverit]], that is, made known, [[11:8|by his prophets to the people|per Prophetas suos ad populum]] of the Hebrews, [[11:8|that he will deliver them up|quod tradat eum]] to their adversaries, [[11:8|for their sins|pro peccatis suis]]. This is true without qualification if it is referred to the times before or after the time of Judith, but it does not seem to be borne out for that time. [[11:9|And because the children of Israel know they have offended their God, thy dread is upon them|Et quoniam sciunt se offendisse Deum suum filii Israel, tremor tuus super ipsos est]], that is, there is trembling in them from considering thy greatness and thy wrath against them. [[11:10|Moreover also a famine hath come upon them|Insuper etiam fames invasit eos]]; [[11:10|and for drought of water|et ab ariditate aquæ]], that is, for the dryness of the thirst which they suffer from want of water or drink (according to which manner of speaking it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 108:24|and my flesh is changed for oil|Caro mea immutata est propter oleum]], that is, for want of oil), [[11:10|they are already to be counted among the dead|jam inter mortuos computantur]], that is, they are as good as dead; as we say of a man in his agony that the man is dead. Hence in the first book of Kings David too confesses: [[1 Kings 20:3|there is but one step (as I may say) between me and death|Ego et mors uno tantum gradu dividimur]]. These things were so according to the letter.

paras.t: Denique hoc ordinant, ut interficiant pecora sua, et sanguinem eorum bibant: quod in Levitico prohibetur. Istud interdum ab obsessis seu in necessitate constitutis legitur factum. Non autem legitur, quod filii Israel ad litteram hoc egerint: quod tamen spiritualiter bene egerunt, bestiales motus exstirpando, et contritione de illis concepta, quasi poculo se replendo. Aliqui autem dicunt eam in his et sequentibus verbis mentitam. Glossa vero ait, quod locuta sit, non adulatorie neque mendaciter, sed mystice atque prophetice. Et sancta Domini Dei sui, quæ Deus præcepit non contingi, id est vasa sacra templi, quæ tangere non licebat, nisi templi ministris, ut quidam exponunt; vel primitias et decimas sacerdotibus ac Levitis deputatas; in frumento, vino et oleo hæc cogitaverunt impendere, id est in proprium usum redigere, vel alienigenis dare seu commutare pro frumento, vino et oleo; et volunt consumere, quæ nec manibus deberent contingere, scilicet sacra vasa: quod ad litteram verum non fuit. Porro in necessitate poterant decimæ et primitiæ comedi [tam] ab aliis, quam a templi ministris, quemadmodum David et exsistentes cum eo comederunt panes propositionis, ut primo Regum volumine narratur. Ergo quoniam hæc faciunt, certum est quod in perditionem tradantur. Quod secundum superficiem litteræ ita non fuit; tamen spiritualiter, etiam justi in hac vita perditionibus, id est damnis et tribulationibus ac mortibus, exponuntur.
paras.en: [[11:11|And they have a design even to kill their cattle|Denique hoc ordinant, ut interficiant pecora sua]], [[11:11|and to drink the blood of them|et sanguinem eorum bibant]], which is forbidden in Leviticus[[Lev 7:26||]] [the margin gives Lev. vii, 26, 27, partly misread]. We read that this was sometimes done by men besieged or in necessity. But we do not read that the children of Israel did it according to the letter; yet spiritually they did it well, by rooting out their beastly impulses, and filling themselves, as with a cup, with the contrition conceived for them. Some say that in these and the following words she lied. But the Gloss says that she spoke neither in flattery nor falsely, but mystically and prophetically. [[11:12|And the consecrated things of the Lord their God which God forbade them to touch|Et sancta Domini Dei sui, quæ Deus præcepit non contingi]], that is, the sacred vessels of the temple, which none but the ministers of the temple were allowed to touch[[Num 4:15||]] [the margin's Num. iv, 15 is partly misread], as some explain it; or the firstfruits and tithes set apart for the priests and Levites; [[11:12|in corn, wine, and oil, these have they purposed to make use of|in frumento, vino et oleo hæc cogitaverunt impendere]], that is, to turn to their own use, or to give to foreigners, or to exchange for corn, wine and oil; [[11:12|and they design to consume the things which they ought not to touch with their hands|et volunt consumere, quæ nec manibus deberent contingere]], namely the sacred vessels: which was not true according to the letter. Moreover, in necessity the tithes and firstfruits could be eaten by others as well as by the ministers of the temple, as David and those who were with him ate the loaves of proposition, as is told in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 21:6||]] [the margin, partly unreadable, seems to give I Reg. xxi]. [[11:12|therefore because they do these things, it is certain they will be given up to destruction|Ergo quoniam hæc faciunt, certum est quod in perditionem tradantur]] [the margin gives the reading *dabuntur*, the Vulgate's]. This was not so on the surface of the letter; yet spiritually even the just are exposed in this life to destructions, that is, to losses and tribulations and deaths.

paras.t: Quod ego ancilla tua cognoscens, fugi ab illis, id est, per modum fugientis veni ad te, seu mente recessi a peccatis eorum. Et misit me Dominus hæc ipsa nuntiare tibi: quia a Deo inspirata est Judith, ut veniret ad Holofernem. Ego enim ancilla tua Deum colo, etiam nunc apud te; et exiet ancilla tua, et orabo Deum, et dicet mihi, quando eis reddet peccatum eorum, id est, quando infliget eis debitam pœnam pro eorum peccatis, videlicet in particulari ac universali futuro judicio, quantum ad impenitentes; et veniens nuntiabo tibi, si Deus hoc jusserit mihi. Vel, Nuntiabo tibi mentis meæ conceptum. Ita ut ego adducam te per mediam Jerusalem. Et habebis omnem populum Israel, sicut oves quibus non est pastor; et non latrabit vel unus canis contra te, quoniam mihi hæc dicta sunt per providentiam Dei. Ironice dicit hoc, vel figurative, vel quia per apprehensionem imaginariam poterat Holofernem sic ducere. Sive ut quidam dicunt, officiosa mendacia protulit.
paras.en: [[11:13|And I thy handmaid knowing this, am fled from them|Quod ego ancilla tua cognoscens, fugi ab illis]], that is, I have come to thee in the manner of one fleeing, or I have withdrawn in mind from their sins. [[11:13|and the Lord hath sent me to tell thee these very things|Et misit me Dominus hæc ipsa nuntiare tibi]]: for Judith was inspired by God to come to Holofernes. [[11:14|For I thy handmaid worship God even now that I am with thee, and thy handmaid will go out, and I will pray to God|Ego enim ancilla tua Deum colo, etiam nunc apud te; et exiet ancilla tua, et orabo Deum]], [[11:15|And he will tell me when he will repay them for their sins|et dicet mihi, quando eis reddet peccatum eorum]] [the margin gives the reading *suum*, the Vulgate's], that is, when he will inflict on them the punishment due for their sins, namely in the particular judgement and in the universal judgement to come, as regards the impenitent; [[11:15|and I will come and tell thee|et veniens nuntiabo tibi]], if God bids me so. Or: I will tell thee what my mind has conceived. [[11:15|so that I may bring thee through the midst of Jerusalem|Ita ut ego adducam te per mediam Jerusalem]]. [[11:15|and thou shalt have all the people of Israel, as sheep that have no shepherd, and there shall not so much as one dog bark against thee|Et habebis omnem populum Israel, sicut oves quibus non est pastor; et non latrabit vel unus canis contra te]], [[11:16|Because these things are told me by the providence of God.|quoniam mihi hæc dicta sunt per providentiam Dei]] She says this ironically, or figuratively, or because in imagination she could lead Holofernes so. Or, as some say, she told officious lies [that is, lies told to help someone, not to harm].

paras.t: Placuerunt autem omnia verba hæc coram Holoferne: qui accepit ea secundum quod sonuerunt, et pro ipso esse favorabilia videbantur. Et mirabantur sapientiam ejus, et dicebant alter ad alterum, hoc est, servi Holofernis mutuo loquebantur: Non est talis, id est tam perfecta, mulier super terram in conspectu, id est apparatu venustateque morum, in pulchritudine et in sensu, id est sententiositate, verborum: quasi dicant, Digna esset conjugio principis nostri.
paras.en: [[11:18|And all these words pleased Holofernes|Placuerunt autem omnia verba hæc coram Holoferne]], who took them as they sounded, and they seemed to be in his favour. [[11:18|and they admired her wisdom, and they said one to another|Et mirabantur sapientiam ejus, et dicebant alter ad alterum]], that is, the servants of Holofernes spoke among themselves: [[11:19|There is not such another|Non est talis]], that is, so perfect, [[11:19|woman upon earth|mulier super terram]] [[11:19|in look|in conspectu]], that is, in bearing and graceful manners, [[11:19|in beauty, and in sense|in pulchritudine et in sensu]], that is, in the weightiness, [[11:19|of words|verborum]]: as if they said: She would be worthy to be our prince's wife.

paras.t: Et dixit ad illam Holofernes: Bene fecit [Deus], qui misit te ante populum, ut des illum tu in manibus nostris. Et quoniam bona est promissio tua, si fecerit mihi hoc Deus tuus, quod promittis, erit et Deus meus. Hoc videtur dixisse ex quadam emollitione circa mulierem, cujus amore exstitit victus, ad complacendum eidem. Alias magnum non reputabat filios Israel superare. Et tu in domo, id est familia seu palatio, Nabuchodonosor regis magna eris, videlicet conjux aut concubina mea.
paras.en: [[11:20|And Holofernes said to her: God hath done well who sent thee before the people, that thou mightest give them into our hands:|Et dixit ad illam Holofernes: Bene fecit [Deus], qui misit te ante populum, ut des illum tu in manibus nostris]] [[11:21|And because thy promise is good|Et quoniam bona est promissio tua]], [[11:21|if thy God shall do this for me|si fecerit mihi hoc Deus tuus]], which thou promisest, [[11:21|he shall also be my God|erit et Deus meus]]. He seems to have said this out of a certain softening towards the woman, by love of whom he had been overcome, so as to please her; otherwise he did not think it a great thing to overcome the children of Israel. [[11:21|and thou shalt be great in the house of Nabuchodonosor|et tu in domo Nabuchodonosor magna eris]], that is, in the household or palace of King Nabuchodonosor: namely, as my wife or concubine.

12.title: Expositio capituli duodecimi: Tunc jussit eam introire ubi repositi erant thesauri ejus
12.title_en: Exposition of the twelfth chapter: Then he ordered that she should go in where his treasures were laid up

paras.t: Hic recitatur, qualiter usque secretum cubiculi Holofernis perducta sit Judith.
paras.en: Here it is told how Judith was brought as far as the privacy of Holofernes's bedchamber.

paras.t: Tunc jussit eam introire ubi repositi erant thesauri ejus, et jussit illic manere eam, et constituit quid daretur illi de convivio suo. Ex quo patet, quod valde honoravit eam, et de ejus fidelitate non dubitavit. Cui dixit Judith: Nunc non potero manducare ex his quæ mihi præcipis tribui, scilicet de cibariis tuis, in quibus sunt aliqua lege prohibita, ne veniat super me offensio, hoc est, ne Deum meum offendam, et offensus non revelet mihi, quando daturus sit populum. Ex his autem quæ mihi detuli, manducabo. Cui Holofernes ait: Si defecerint tibi ista, quid tibi faciemus? Et dixit Judith: Vivit anima tua, domine meus, quoniam non expendet omnia hæc victualia, quæ mecum portavi, ancilla tua, donec faciat Deus in manu mea, id est per obsequium manus meæ seu virtutis operativæ, ea quæ cogitavi. Quod fuit impletum, quia antequam omnia illa comedit, Holofernem occidit.
paras.en: [[12:1|Then he ordered that she should go in where his treasures were laid up, and bade her tarry there, and he appointed what should be given her from his own table.|Tunc jussit eam introire ubi repositi erant thesauri ejus, et jussit illic manere eam, et constituit quid daretur illi de convivio suo]] From this it is plain that he honoured her greatly, and did not doubt her faithfulness. [[12:2|And Judith answered him and said|Cui dixit Judith]]: [[12:2|Now I cannot eat of these things which thou commandest to be given me|Nunc non potero manducare ex his quæ mihi præcipis tribui]], namely of thy foods, among which there are some things forbidden by the law, [[12:2|lest sin come upon me|ne veniat super me offensio]] [*offensio*, “offence”], that is, lest I offend my God, and he, being offended, should not reveal to me when he is to give up the people. [[12:2|but I will eat of the things which I have brought|Ex his autem quæ mihi detuli, manducabo]]. [[12:3|And Holofernes said to her: If these things|Cui Holofernes ait: Si defecerint tibi ista]] [[12:3|fail thee, what shall we do for thee?|quid tibi faciemus?]] [[12:4|And Judith said: As thy soul liveth, my lord|Et dixit Judith: Vivit anima tua, domine meus]], [[12:4|thy handmaid shall not spend all these things|quoniam non expendet omnia hæc]], these victuals which I have brought with me, [[12:4|till God do by my hand|donec faciat Deus in manu mea]], that is, by the service of my hand, or of my power to act, [[12:4|that which I have purposed|ea quæ cogitavi]]. This was fulfilled, for before she had eaten all those things she killed Holofernes.

paras.t: Et induxerunt illam servi ejus in tabernaculum, quo præceperat; et petiit, dum introiret, hoc est, quando incepit ab Holoferne recedere ad locum thesaurorum ejus, rogavit Holofernem, ut daretur ei copia, id est libertas et facultas, nocte et ante lucem egrediendi foras ad orationem, et deprecandi Dominum, ut instante aurora, oraret devotius sola cum sua ancilla. Et præcepit Holofernes cubiculariis suis, ut sicut placeret, id est, ipsa Judith ad placitum suum, exiret et introiret locum sibi deputatum, et adoraret ubi et quando vellet, Deum suum per triduum: post quod intendebat dormire cum illa.
paras.en: [[12:4|And his servants brought her into the tent which he had commanded|Et induxerunt illam servi ejus in tabernaculum, quo præceperat]]; [[12:5|And when she was going in, she desired|et petiit, dum introiret]], that is, when she began to withdraw from Holofernes to the place of his treasures, she asked Holofernes [[12:5|that she might have liberty|ut daretur ei copia]], that is, freedom and leave, [[12:5|to go out at night and before day to prayer, and to beseech the Lord|nocte et ante lucem egrediendi foras ad orationem, et deprecandi Dominum]], so that at the coming of dawn she might pray more devoutly, alone with her maid. [[12:6|And he commanded his chamberlains|Et præcepit Holofernes cubiculariis suis]] that [[12:6|as she pleased|sicut placeret]], that is, Judith herself at her own pleasure, [[12:6|she might go out and in|exiret et introiret]] the place assigned to her, and [[12:6|adore|adoraret]] [[12:6|her God|Deum suum]] where and when she would, [[12:6|for three days|per triduum]]; after which he meant to sleep with her.

paras.t: Et exibat noctibus in vallem Bethuliæ, quæ fuit extra urbem illam non longe, et baptizabat, id est lavabat se, scilicet manus, faciem, seu plura membra, in fonte, qui erat ibi, ut mundior oraret secundum consuetudinem Judæorum, et pulchrior remaneret ob causam præhabitam. Et ut ascendebat de fonte, orabat Dominum Deum Israel, ut dirigeret viam suam ad liberationem populi sui. Et introiens, munda, id est non inquinata cibis gentilium, aut aliqua legis irregularitate, manebat in tabernaculo thesaurorum Holofernis, usque dum acciperet escam suam in vesperum. Unde apparet, quod jejunabat illis diebus usque de sero.
paras.en: [[12:7|And she went out in the nights into the valley of Bethulia|Et exibat noctibus in vallem Bethuliæ]], which was outside that city, not far off, [[12:7|and washed|et baptizabat]] [literally *baptized*], that is, washed herself, namely her hands, face, or more of her members, [[12:7|in a fountain|in fonte]] that was there, so that she might pray the cleaner, after the custom of the Jews, and remain the more beautiful, for the reason given before. [[12:8|And as she came up|Et ut ascendebat]] from the fountain, [[12:8|she prayed to the Lord the God of Israel, that he would direct her way to the deliverance of his people|orabat Dominum Deum Israel, ut dirigeret viam suam ad liberationem populi sui]] [the print of this verse is badly damaged; it is read with the help of the Vulgate, with *viam suam* for the Vulgate's *viam ejus*]. [[12:9|And going in|Et introiens]], [[12:9|she remained|manebat]] [[12:9|pure|munda]], that is, not defiled by the food of the Gentiles, or by any irregularity against the law, [[12:9|in the tent|in tabernaculo]] of the treasures of Holofernes, [[12:9|until she took her own meat in the evening|usque dum acciperet escam suam in vesperum]]. Hence it appears that she fasted in those days until evening.

paras.t: Et factum est in quarto die ab exitu Judith de Bethulia, Holofernes fecit cœnam servis suis solennem, volens post cœnam cum Judith uniri. Et aliqui putant, quod voluit eam accipere conjugem. Et dixit ad Vagao eunuchum: Vade et suade, id est, informa seu induc, Hebræam illam, ut sponte consentiat habitare mecum. Ex quibus verbis videtur insinuari, quod voluerit eam secum de cetero detinere quasi uxorem. Fœdum est enim apud Assyrios, ut femina irrideat virum, agendo ut immunis, id est incognita et non humiliata a viro, transeat ab eo.
paras.en: [[12:10|And it came to pass on the fourth day|Et factum est in quarto die]] after Judith's going out from Bethulia, [[12:10|that Holofernes made a supper for his servants|Holofernes fecit cœnam servis suis]], a solemn one, wishing to be united with Judith after supper. And some think that he wished to take her as his wife. [[12:10|and said to Vagao|Et dixit ad Vagao]] [[12:10|his eunuch|eunuchum]]: [[12:10|Go, and persuade|Vade et suade]], that is, instruct or induce, [[12:10|that Hebrew woman, to consent of her own accord to dwell with me|Hebræam illam, ut sponte consentiat habitare mecum]]. From these words it seems to be hinted that he wished to keep her with him from then on as a wife. [[12:11|For it is looked upon as shameful among the Assyrians, if a woman mock a man|Fœdum est enim apud Assyrios, ut femina irrideat virum]], [[12:11|by doing so as to pass free|agendo ut immunis]], that is, unknown [that is, not known carnally] and not humbled by the man, [[12:11|from him|transeat ab eo]].

paras.t: Tunc introivit Vagao ad Judith, et dixit: Non vereatur bona puella: forte putavit eam adhuc virginem esse; introire ad dominum meum, ut honorificetur ante faciem ejus, et manducet cum eo, et bibat vinum in jucunditate. Cui Judith respondit: Quæ ego sum, ut contradicam domino meo? Omne quod erit ante oculos ejus bonum et optimum, id est quædam de omnibus illis, faciam: quantum ad aliqua, scilicet veniendo ad mensam ejus, et manducando cum ipso, atque intrando cubiculum ejus. Quidquid autem placuerit illi, de præambulis ad dormiendum cum ipso, hoc mihi erit optimum omnibus diebus vitæ meæ, id est, erit mihi occasio et medium exsequendi in eo quod cupio, scilicet interficiendi eum secrete in suo cubiculo.
paras.en: [[12:12|Then Vagao went in to Judith, and said: Let not my good maid be afraid|Tunc introivit Vagao ad Judith, et dixit: Non vereatur bona puella]] (perhaps he thought she was still a virgin) [[12:12|to go in to my lord, that she may be honoured before his face, that she may eat with him and drink wine and be merry|introire ad dominum meum, ut honorificetur ante faciem ejus, et manducet cum eo, et bibat vinum in jucunditate]]. [[12:13|And Judith answered him: Who am I, that I should gainsay my lord?|Cui Judith respondit: Quæ ego sum, ut contradicam domino meo?]] [[12:14|All that shall be good and best before his eyes|Omne quod erit ante oculos ejus bonum et optimum]], that is, some of all those things, [[12:14|I will do|faciam]]: as regards certain things, namely by coming to his table, and eating with him, and going into his bedchamber. [[12:14|And whatsoever shall please him|Quidquid autem placuerit illi]] of the things leading up to sleeping with him, [[12:14|that shall be best to me all the days of my life|hoc mihi erit optimum omnibus diebus vitæ meæ]], that is, it will be my occasion and means of carrying out upon him what I desire, namely to kill him secretly in his bedchamber.

paras.t: Et surrexit, et ornavit se vestimento suo, et ingressa stetit ante faciem ejus. Cor autem Holofernis concussum est, id est, repente impletum motu concupiscentiæ prædominantis et ardore libidinis, statim ut Judith venit ad ejus præsentiam. Erat enim ardens in concupiscentia ejus. Et dixit ad eam: Bibe nunc, et accumbe, hoc est comede, in jucunditate, quoniam gratiam invenisti coram me. Et dixit Judith: Bibam, domine, quoniam magnificata est anima mea hodie præ omnibus diebus meis: id est, nunquam fui tantum honorata honore mundano, seu a principe tam potente, ut modo. Et hoc ad litteram potuit esse verum. Et præsertim, in quantum honoratio illa fuit ei dispositio valde propinqua ad exsequendum suum intentum in Holoferne, fuit præcipua sublimatio sua. Ipsa tamen tam reverenter et quasi favorabiliter loquebatur, quatenus Holofernes nequaquam se observaret ab ea.
paras.en: [[12:15|And she arose and dressed herself out with her garments, and going in she stood before his face.|Et surrexit, et ornavit se vestimento suo, et ingressa stetit ante faciem ejus]] [[12:16|And the heart of Holofernes was smitten|Cor autem Holofernis concussum est]], that is, was suddenly filled with the stirring of an overmastering concupiscence and with the heat of lust, as soon as Judith came into his presence. [[12:16|for he was burning with the desire of her|Erat enim ardens in concupiscentia ejus]]. [[12:17|And Holofernes said to her: Drink now, and sit down|Et dixit ad eam: Bibe nunc, et accumbe]], that is, eat, [[12:17|and be merry; for thou hast found favour before me|in jucunditate, quoniam gratiam invenisti coram me]]. [[12:18|And Judith said: I will drink my lord, because my life is magnified this day above all my days|Et dixit Judith: Bibam, domine, quoniam magnificata est anima mea hodie præ omnibus diebus meis]]: that is, I have never been so honoured with worldly honour, or by so mighty a prince, as now. And this could be true according to the letter. And above all, inasmuch as that honour was for her a very near preparation for carrying out her purpose upon Holofernes, it was her chief exaltation. Yet she spoke so reverently and as it were so favourably that Holofernes in no way guarded himself against her.

paras.t: Et accepit ipsa Judith, et manducavit et bibit coram ipso Holoferne, ea quæ paraverat ei ancilla ejus. Et jucundus factus est Holofernes ad eam, id est ex ejus præsentia, præsupponens se mox fruiturum objecto tam concupito. Bibitque vinum multum nimis, quantum una die nunquam biberat in vita sua. Quod fecit ex immoderata lætitia; et quia impetus passionis suæ concupiscentiæ, et ardor libidinis mentem ejus obcæcaverunt, ita quod sine discretione ingurgitavit se.
paras.en: [[12:19|And she took|Et accepit]], Judith herself, [[12:19|and ate and drank before him|et manducavit et bibit coram ipso]], Holofernes himself, [[12:19|what her maid had prepared for her|ea quæ paraverat ei ancilla ejus]]. [[12:20|And Holofernes was made merry on her occasion|Et jucundus factus est Holofernes ad eam]], that is, from her presence, taking it for granted that he would soon enjoy the object he so desired. [[12:20|and drank exceeding much wine|Bibitque vinum multum nimis]], [[12:20|so much as|quantum]] in one day [[12:20|he had never drunk in his life|nunquam biberat in vita sua]]. This he did out of immoderate joy, and because the onrush of his passion of concupiscence and the heat of lust had blinded his mind, so that he gorged himself without discretion.

13.title: Declaratio capituli tertiidecimi: Ut autem sero factum est
13.title_en: Explanation of the thirteenth chapter: And when it was grown late

paras.t: Describitur hic decapitatio Holofernis.
paras.en: Here the beheading of Holofernes is described.

paras.t: Ut autem sero factum est, finita jam cœna, festinaverunt servi ejus ad hospitia sua, hoc est tentoria in quibus repausabant. Et conclusit Vagao ostia cubiculi, Holoferne et Judith exsistentibus in cubiculo, et abiit. Erant autem omnes, videlicet Holofernes et servi ejus, fatigati a vino, id est valde inebriati seu ingurgitati. Eratque Judith sola in cubiculo cum Holoferne. Porro Holofernes jacebat in lecto nimia ebrietate sopitus, hoc est, graviter dormiens. Dixitque Judith puellæ suæ, ut staret foris ante cubiculum, et observaret an aliquis adveniret, quatenus sibi hoc insinuaret. Hoc dixit abræ suæ antequam introivit in cubiculum Holofernis. Vel, egresso Vagao eunucho, aperuit ostium cubiculi, et paulisper egrediens, dixit istud ancillæ suæ.
paras.en: [[13:1|And when it was grown late|Ut autem sero factum est]], supper being now over, [[13:1|his servants made haste to their lodgings|festinaverunt servi ejus ad hospitia sua]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], that is, to the tents in which they rested; [[13:1|and Vagao shut the chamber doors|Et conclusit Vagao ostia cubiculi]], Holofernes and Judith being in the chamber, [[13:1|and went his way|et abiit]]. [[13:2|And they were all|Erant autem omnes]], namely Holofernes and his servants, [[13:2|overcharged with wine|fatigati a vino]], that is, very drunk or gorged. [[13:3|And Judith was alone in the chamber|Eratque Judith sola in cubiculo]] with Holofernes. [[13:4|But Holofernes lay on his bed, fast asleep, being exceedingly drunk|Porro Holofernes jacebat in lecto nimia ebrietate sopitus]], that is, sleeping heavily. [[13:5|And Judith spoke to her maid to stand without before the chamber, and to watch|Dixitque Judith puellæ suæ, ut staret foris ante cubiculum, et observaret]] whether anyone was coming, so that she might let her know of it. She said this to her maid before she went into the bedchamber of Holofernes; or else, when Vagao the eunuch had gone out, she opened the door of the chamber, and going out for a little while, said it to her handmaid.

paras.t: Stetitque Judith ante lectum Holofernis, orans cum lacrimis, et labiorum motu in silentio, dicens: Confirma me, Deus Israel, et respice in hac hora ad opera manuum mearum, ut sicut promisisti, Jerusalem civitatem tuam erigas, etc., hoc est, ab Assyriorum istorum invasione eripias, et eam exaltes, seu reædificari perfectius facias. Quemadmodum enim Isaias, Jeremias, Ezechiel prænuntiaverunt urbis illius destructionem ante Babylonicam captivitatem, sic prædixerunt ejus reparationem post reditum ab eadem captivitate futuram.
paras.en: [[13:6|And Judith stood before the bed|Stetitque Judith ante lectum]] of Holofernes, [[13:6|praying with tears, and the motion of her lips in silence|orans cum lacrimis, et labiorum motu in silentio]], [[13:7|Saying: Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel|dicens: Confirma me, Deus Israel]], [[13:7|and in this hour look on the works of my hands, that as thou hast promised, thou mayst raise up Jerusalem thy city|et respice in hac hora ad opera manuum mearum, ut sicut promisisti, Jerusalem civitatem tuam erigas]], etc.; that is, that thou mayest snatch it from the invasion of these Assyrians, and exalt it, or have it more perfectly rebuilt. For as Isaias, Jeremias and Ezechiel foretold the destruction of that city before the Babylonian captivity[[Jer 19:1||]], so they foretold its restoration, to come after the return from that same captivity[[Is 49:1||]][[Ezech 36:1||]] [the margin here is faint and much misread: it seems to cite several chapters, among them Is. xlix, Jer. xix, Ezech. xxviii and xxxvi; the references given are those chapters, at verse 1].

paras.t: Et quum hæc dixisset, accessit ad columnam, quæ erat ad caput lectuli. Et pugionem ejus exsolvit, id est, ensem parvum bis acutum Holofernis dissolvit. Cumque evaginasset illum, apprehendit comam capitis ejus, et ait: Confirma me, Deus, in hac hora. Et percussit bis in cervicem, hoc est collum ejus; et abscidit caput ejus. Unde constat quod fortiter viriliterque percussit. Et abstulit conopeum ejus, videlicet ipsius Holofernis: de quo conopeo dictum est supra; quod secum portavit, ut infra elucescit. Et evolvit corpus ejus truncum, hoc est, corpus Holofernis capite truncatum traxit a lecto in terram, ut patet sequenti capitulo, quatenus cubicularius, ingressurus ante alios cubiculum, majori concuteretur horrore, viso cadavere.
paras.en: [[13:8|And when she had said this, she went to the pillar that was at his bed's head|Et quum hæc dixisset, accessit ad columnam, quæ erat ad caput lectuli]], [[13:8|and loosed his sword|Et pugionem ejus exsolvit]] [*pugio*, a dagger], that is, she loosed the short two-edged sword of Holofernes. [[13:9|And when she had drawn it out, she took him by the hair of his head, and said|Cumque evaginasset illum, apprehendit comam capitis ejus, et ait]]: [[13:9|Strengthen me, O Lord God, at this hour|Confirma me, Deus, in hac hora]]. [[13:10|And she struck twice upon his neck|Et percussit bis in cervicem]] [*cervix*, the nape], that is, his neck; [[13:10|and cut off his head|et abscidit caput ejus]]. From this it is clear that she struck strongly and manfully. [[13:10|and took off his canopy|Et abstulit conopeum ejus]], namely the canopy of Holofernes himself, of which mention was made above[[Jdt 10:19||]], and which she took with her, as appears below; [[13:10|and rolled away his headless body|Et evolvit corpus ejus truncum]], that is, she dragged the body of Holofernes, cut off from its head, from the bed to the ground, as is plain in the following chapter[[Jdt 14:14||]], so that the chamberlain, who would go into the chamber before the others, might be struck with the greater horror at the sight of the corpse.

paras.t: Et post pusillum exivit, et tradidit caput Holofernis ancillæ suæ, et jussit ut mitteret illud in peram suam. Et exierunt duæ secundum consuetudinem suam, quasi ad orationem, hoc est, quasi ad orandum in valle Bethuliæ, sicut jam ante fecerunt noctibus tribus; et transierunt castra, id est, tentoria ac militiam Assyriorum pertransierunt: ita quod exploratores seu vigiles Assyriorum eas non accesserunt, nec interrogaverunt, quoniam data fuit libertas exeundi ad orationem ipsi Judith ab Holoferne, saltem per tres noctes: et forsan non viderunt eam. Et gyrantes, id est circumeuntes, vallem Bethuliæ, venerunt ad portam civitatis remotiorem a circumjacente Assyriorum exercitu. Et dixit Judith a longe custodibus murorum: quibus præ gaudio acclamavit, certa quod ab Assyriis audiri non posset: Aperite portas, quoniam nobiscum est Deus, per specialem effectum misericordiæ atque potentiæ suæ. Ideo subditur: Qui fecit virtutem in Israel, id est, per me feminam Israelitam, fecit magnum et potentem effectum.
paras.en: [[13:11|And after a while she went out, and delivered the head of Holofernes to her maid, and bade her put it into her wallet.|Et post pusillum exivit, et tradidit caput Holofernis ancillæ suæ, et jussit ut mitteret illud in peram suam]] [[13:12|And they two went out according to their custom, as it were to prayer|Et exierunt duæ secundum consuetudinem suam, quasi ad orationem]], that is, as if to pray in the valley of Bethulia, as they had done already for three nights; [[13:12|and they passed the camp|et transierunt castra]], that is, they passed through the tents and soldiery of the Assyrians, so that the scouts or watchmen of the Assyrians did not come up to them nor question them, since leave to go out to prayer had been given to Judith by Holofernes, at least for three nights; and perhaps they did not see her. [[13:12|and having compassed|Et gyrantes]], that is, going round, [[13:12|the valley|vallem]] of Bethulia, [[13:12|they came to the gate of the city|venerunt ad portam civitatis]] that was farther from the army of the Assyrians lying round about. [[13:13|And Judith from afar off cried to the watchmen upon the walls|Et dixit Judith a longe custodibus murorum]], to whom she called out for joy, sure that she could not be heard by the Assyrians: [[13:13|Open the gates for God is with us|Aperite portas, quoniam nobiscum est Deus]], by a special working of his mercy and power. Therefore it is added: [[13:13|who hath shewn his power in Israel|Qui fecit virtutem in Israel]], that is, through me, an Israelite woman, he has done a great and mighty work.

paras.t: Et factum est quum audissent viri vocem ejus, vocaverunt presbyteros civitatis ac ceteros principales; et concurrerunt ad eam omnes, a minimo usque ad maximum, quoniam speraverunt, id est timuerunt paulo ante, eam jam non esse venturam. Sicque Sperare, quod proprie sumptum, est præstolatio de bono futuro, sumitur hic multum improprie pro Timere. Itaque timuerunt eam non esse reversuram, sed ab Assyriis detentam et violatam, aut ob suam renitentiam interfectam. Et accendentes luminaria, congyraverunt, id est, in circuitu steterunt, circa eam universi, cupientes nova audire in tam arduo casu.
paras.en: [[13:14|And it came to pass, when the men had heard her voice, that they called the ancients of the city|Et factum est quum audissent viri vocem ejus, vocaverunt presbyteros civitatis]] and the other chief men; [[13:15|And all ran to meet her from the least to the greatest|et concurrerunt ad eam omnes, a minimo usque ad maximum]], [[13:15|for they now had no hopes that she would come|quoniam speraverunt]] [literally, “for they hoped that she would not now come”], that is, a little before they had feared that she would not now come. And so *to hope*, which taken properly is the awaiting of a future good, is taken here very improperly for *to fear*. So they feared that she would not return, but had been detained and violated by the Assyrians, or killed for her resistance. [[13:16|And lighting up lights they all gathered round about her|Et accendentes luminaria, congyraverunt circa eam universi]] [the print of vv. 15–16 is damaged; their words are read with the help of the Vulgate], that is, they stood round about her, all of them, wanting to hear the news in so grave a case.

paras.t: Illa autem ascendens in eminentiorem locum, ut videretur et audiretur a cunctis, jussit fieri silentium. Quumque omnes tacuissent, dicit Judith: Laudate Dominum Deum nostrum, qui non deseruit sperantes in se, videlicet nos, qui in tanto periculo cum fiducia invocavimus eum, et in me ancillam suam adimplevit misericordiam suam, id est, multiplicem effectum suæ pietatis copiose exhibuit mihi, et interfecit in manu mea, id est per obsequium manuum mearum, quarum una tenuit comam Holofernis, alia intulit ictum, hostem populi sui in hac nocte. Et proferens de pera caput Holofernis, ostendit illis, dicens: Ecce caput Holofernis principis militiæ Assyriorum. Ecce conopeum illius, quod fuit expansum ante lectum ipsius ad repellendum muscas et culices, in quo recumbebat, id est, infra quod jacebat, in ebrietate sua. Deinde jurat se intactam rediisse, sicut patet in textu qui planus est.
paras.en: [[13:16|and she went up to a higher place|Illa autem ascendens in eminentiorem locum]], so that she might be seen and heard by all, [[13:16|and commanded silence to be made. And when all had held their peace|jussit fieri silentium. Quumque omnes tacuissent]], [[13:17|Judith said: Praise ye the Lord our God, who hath not forsaken them that hope in him|dicit Judith: Laudate Dominum Deum nostrum, qui non deseruit sperantes in se]], namely us, who in so great a danger called upon him with confidence; [[13:18|And by me his handmaid he hath fulfilled his mercy|et in me ancillam suam adimplevit misericordiam suam]], that is, he has shown me abundantly the manifold working of his goodness; [[13:18|and he hath killed|et interfecit]] [[13:18|by my hand|in manu mea]], that is, by the service of my hands, one of which held the hair of Holofernes while the other struck the blow, [[13:18|the enemy of his people|hostem populi sui]] [[13:18|this night|in hac nocte]]. [[13:19|Then she brought forth the head of Holofernes out of the wallet, and shewed it them, saying: Behold the head of Holofernes the general of the army of the Assyrians|Et proferens de pera caput Holofernis, ostendit illis, dicens: Ecce caput Holofernis principis militiæ Assyriorum]]. [[13:19|and behold his canopy|Ecce conopeum illius]], which was spread before his bed to keep off flies and gnats, [[13:19|wherein he lay|in quo recumbebat]], that is, beneath which he lay, [[13:19|in his drunkenness|in ebrietate sua]]. Then she swears that she has come back untouched, as is plain in the text, which is clear.

paras.t: Universi autem adorantes Dominum cum laude et gratiarum actione, quemadmodum jam Judith admonuit, dixerunt: Benedixit te Dominus in virtute sua, id est, in omnipotentia sua multiplicavit in te dona et beneficia sua, per quæ fecit te benedictam, atque ab omnibus benedicendam, quia per te ad nihilum redegit inimicos nostros, id est, cœpit redigere, et mox plenius rediget. Jam enim præsupponebant se prævalituros exercitui, cujus princeps fuit occisus.
paras.en: [[13:22|And they all adored the Lord|Universi autem adorantes Dominum]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate] with praise and thanksgiving, as Judith had just bidden them, [[13:22|and said|dixerunt]]: [[13:22|The Lord hath blessed thee by his power|Benedixit te Dominus in virtute sua]], that is, in his omnipotence he has multiplied in thee his gifts and benefits, by which he has made thee blessed, and to be blessed by all, [[13:22|because by thee he hath brought our enemies to nought|quia per te ad nihilum redegit inimicos nostros]], that is, he has begun to bring them to nought, and will soon do so more fully. For they now took it for granted that they would prevail over the army whose prince had been slain.

paras.t: Porro Ozias princeps populi Israel, dicit ad eam: Benedicta es tu, filia, a Domino Deo excelso præ omnibus mulieribus divisim acceptis, super terram exsistentibus tempore isto. Verumtamen an tempore illo non fuerit aliqua mulier in hoc mundo sanctior quam hæc Judith, videtur incertum: nec Ozias scire hoc potuit sine revelatione divina. Sed constat, quod quantum ad specialia quædam beneficia, et quoad aliqua bellica gesta, fuerat pro tunc præ ceteris mulieribus benedicta. Quo modo de quolibet sancto dicitur confessore: Non est inventus similis illi. Benedictus Dominus, qui creavit cœlum et terram, qui te direxit in vulnera capitis principis inimicorum nostrorum, id est ad vulnerandum et amputandum caput principis inimicorum nostrorum; quia hodie, id est in hac nocte, nomen tuum, id est te ipsam, ita magnificavit, per præclarissimos actus, quos fecit per te, et ad quos agendos te inspiravit, direxit, corroboravit, ut non recedat laus tua de ore hominum, qui memores fuerint virtutis Domini in æternum, pro quibus non pepercisti animæ tuæ propter angustias tribulationum generis tui, sed subvenisti ruinæ ante conspectum Dei nostri. Et dixit omnis populus, Fiat, fiat: sicut videmus impletum.
paras.en: [[13:23|And Ozias the prince of the people of Israel, said to her: Blessed art thou, O daughter, by the Lord the most high God, above all women|Porro Ozias princeps populi Israel, dicit ad eam: Benedicta es tu, filia, a Domino Deo excelso præ omnibus mulieribus]] taken severally [that is, each one singly, not all together], [[13:23|upon the earth|super terram]], living at that time. Yet whether at that time there was not some woman in this world holier than this Judith seems uncertain; nor could Ozias know this without divine revelation. But it is clear that as regards certain special benefits, and certain deeds of war, she was then blessed above other women: in the way in which it is said of any holy confessor: [[Ecclus 44:20|there was not found the like to him|Non est inventus similis illi]] [the margin's reading is unclear; the words are those of Ecclus 44:20, said of Abraham and sung in the Office of a confessor]. [[13:24|Blessed be the Lord who made heaven and earth, who hath directed thee to the cutting off the head of the prince of our enemies.|Benedictus Dominus, qui creavit cœlum et terram, qui te direxit in vulnera capitis principis inimicorum nostrorum]] [*in vulnera capitis*, literally “to the wounding of the head”], that is, to wound and cut off the head of the prince of our enemies; [[13:25|Because|quia]] [[13:25|this day|hodie]], that is, this night, [[13:25|he hath so magnified|ita magnificavit]] [[13:25|thy name|nomen tuum]], that is, thyself, by the most glorious acts which he did through thee, and to the doing of which he inspired, directed and strengthened thee, [[13:25|that thy praise shall not depart out of the mouth of men who shall be mindful of the power of the Lord for ever|ut non recedat laus tua de ore hominum, qui memores fuerint virtutis Domini in æternum]], [[13:25|for that thou hast not spared thy life, by reason of the distress and tribulation of thy people, but hast prevented our ruin in the presence of our God|pro quibus non pepercisti animæ tuæ propter angustias tribulationum generis tui, sed subvenisti ruinæ ante conspectum Dei nostri]]. [[13:26|And all the people said: So be it, so be it|Et dixit omnis populus, Fiat, fiat]]: as we see fulfilled.

paras.t: Porro Achior vocatus venit. Gentilis namque et incircumcisus exsistens, non se ingessit in populum Dei, nisi vocatus. Et dixit ei Judith: Deus Israel, cui tu testimonium dedisti quod ulciscatur se de inimicis suis, ipse caput omnium incredulorum incidit hac nocte in manu mea. Videns autem Achior caput Holofernis, angustiatus, id est horrore concussus ex tam inopinato et arduo facto, præ pavore, id est admiratione et quadam formidine, cecidit in faciem suam super terram. Tales etenim vehementes passiones partis sensitivæ fiunt cum grandi et immoderata alteratione corporalis naturæ, sicque debilitatem inducunt et casum. Et æstuavit anima ejus, id est, ad anxietatem, sudorem, ecstasim quamdam devenit anima ejus, quia et omnipotentiam ac providentiam Dei in isto intuebatur negotio.
paras.en: [[13:27|And Achior being called for came|Porro Achior vocatus venit]]. For being a Gentile and uncircumcised, he did not thrust himself among the people of God unless he was called. [[13:27|and Judith said to him: The God of Israel, to whom thou gavest testimony, that he revengeth himself of his enemies, he hath cut off the head of all the unbelievers this night by my hand|Et dixit ei Judith: Deus Israel, cui tu testimonium dedisti quod ulciscatur se de inimicis suis, ipse caput omnium incredulorum incidit hac nocte in manu mea]]. [[13:29|Then Achior seeing the head of Holofernes|Videns autem Achior caput Holofernis]], [[13:29|being seized|angustiatus]], that is, shaken with horror at so unlooked-for and hard a deed, [[13:29|with a great fear|præ pavore]], that is, with wonder and a kind of dread, [[13:29|he fell on his face upon the earth|cecidit in faciem suam super terram]]. For such vehement passions of the sensitive part come with a great and immoderate change in the bodily nature, and so bring on weakness and falling. [[13:29|and his soul swooned away|Et æstuavit anima ejus]] [*æstuavit*, literally “was in a ferment”], that is, his soul came to anguish, sweat and a kind of ecstasy, because he beheld in this affair both the omnipotence and the providence of God.

paras.t: Postea vero quam resumpto spiritu recreatus est, id est rationis judicio et viribus paulatim recuperatis, procidit ad pedes ejus, videlicet Judith, et adoravit eam adoratione duliæ, propter eminentiam virtuositatis ac sapientiæ suæ. Et dixit: Benedicta tu a Deo tuo, id est a Deo vero, et ad ejus honorem et laudem, in omni tabernaculo Jacob, id est tota posteritate Jacob patriarchæ, quoniam in omni gente quæ audierit nomen tuum, id est, gesta tua perceperit, magnificabitur Deus Israel super te, id est, Deus omnipotens magnifice laudabitur ex consideratione beneficiorum quæ contulit tibi, et mirabilium quæ fecit per te. Ecce quam infinita est perfectio providentiæ ac sapientiæ Dei: qui cuncta tam præclare disponit, et superbos humiliat, imo eos qui animosius se extollunt, confusibilius dejicit.
paras.en: [[13:30|But after he had recovered his spirits|Postea vero quam resumpto spiritu recreatus est]] [the print is badly damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], that is, when the judgement of his reason and his strength had little by little been recovered, [[13:30|he fell down at her feet|procidit ad pedes ejus]], namely Judith's, [[13:30|and reverenced her|et adoravit eam]] with the adoration of dulia [that is, the honour paid to a creature, as distinct from *latria*, the worship due to God alone], for the eminence of her virtue and wisdom. [[13:30|and said|Et dixit]]: [[13:31|Blessed art thou by thy God|Benedicta tu a Deo tuo]], that is, by the true God, and to his honour and praise, [[13:31|in every tabernacle of Jacob|in omni tabernaculo Jacob]], that is, in all the posterity of the patriarch Jacob, [[13:31|for in every nation which shall hear thy name|quoniam in omni gente quæ audierit nomen tuum]], that is, shall learn of thy deeds, [[13:31|the God of Israel shall be magnified on occasion of thee|magnificabitur Deus Israel super te]], that is, God almighty shall be magnificently praised in consideration of the benefits he has bestowed on thee, and of the wonders he has done through thee. Behold how infinite is the perfection of the providence and wisdom of God, who disposes all things so gloriously, and humbles the proud[[Is 10:33||]][[Dan 4:34||]][[Luke 14:11||]], nay, casts down the more shamefully those who exalt themselves the more boldly [the margin here is partly unreadable: it seems to give Ps. xxi (?), 38; Is. x, 33; Ezech. xvi; Dan. iv (?); Luc. xiv, 11].

14.title: Elucidatio capituli quartidecimi: Dixit autem Judith ad omnem populum
14.title_en: Explanation of the fourteenth chapter: And Judith said to all the people

paras.t: Congressus Hebræorum contra Assyrios hic recitatur.
paras.en: Here the encounter of the Hebrews with the Assyrians is told.

paras.t: Dixit autem Judith ad omnem populum: Audite me, fratres; suspendite caput hoc super muros vestros, in signum divini subsidii, et ut capitis hujus intuitione concipiatis majorem contra hostes audaciam: quemadmodum secundo Machabæorum fertur de Juda Machabæo: Suspendit autem caput Nicanoris in summa arce, ut esset manifestum signum adjutorii Dei. Et erit, quum exierit sol de hemisphærio inferiori ad hemisphærium superius, scilicet valde mane, unusquisque aptus ad prælium, scilicet vir qui sit viginti annorum, prout describitur in libro Numerorum, accipiat arma sua, et exite cum impetu, id est audacter et cito, quasi nihil timentes, non ut descendatis deorsum, eundo tarde et timide, sed quasi impetum facientes. Tunc exploratores necesse erit ut fugiant, ad principem suum excitandum ad pugnam. Quumque duces eorum cucurrerint ad tabernaculum Holofernis: quoniam sine scitu, nutu et dispositione principis militiæ, non audebant prælium inchoare aut gerere; et invenerint eum truncum, id est capite truncatum, decidet super eos timor. Quumque cognoveritis fugere eos, ite post eos securi de victoria, quoniam Dominus conteret eos sub pedibus vestris.
paras.en: [[14:1|And Judith said to all the people|Dixit autem Judith ad omnem populum]]: [[14:1|Hear me, my brethren, hang ye up this head upon our walls|Audite me, fratres; suspendite caput hoc super muros vestros]] [Denis's text has *vestros*, “your”; the margin gives *nostros*, the Vulgate's], as a sign of God's help, and so that from the sight of this head you may conceive greater boldness against the enemy: as is told in the second book of Machabees of Judas Machabeus: [[2 Mach 15:35|And he hung up Nicanor's head in the top of the castle|Suspendit autem caput Nicanoris in summa arce]], that it might be a [[2 Mach 15:35|manifest sign of the help of God|manifestum signum adjutorii Dei]] [the margin gives II Mach. xv, 35; Denis's wording differs a little from the Vulgate's]. [[14:2|And as soon as the sun shall rise|Et erit, quum exierit sol]] from the lower hemisphere to the upper, that is, very early, [[14:2|let every man|unusquisque]] fit for battle, namely a man of twenty years, as is laid down in the book of Numbers[[Num 1:3||]], [[14:2|take his arms|accipiat arma sua]], [[14:2|and rush ye out|et exite cum impetu]], that is, boldly and quickly, as men who fear nothing, [[14:2|not as going down beneath|non ut descendatis deorsum]], going slowly and fearfully, [[14:2|but as making an assault|sed quasi impetum facientes]]. [[14:3|Then the watchmen must needs run to awake their prince for the battle|Tunc exploratores necesse erit ut fugiant, ad principem suum excitandum ad pugnam]]. [[14:4|And when the captains of them shall run to the tent of Holofernes|Quumque duces eorum cucurrerint ad tabernaculum Holofernis]], since without the knowledge, nod and ordering of the prince of the army they did not dare to begin or wage battle, [[14:4|and shall find him without his head|et invenerint eum truncum]], that is, cut off from his head, [[14:4|fear shall fall upon them|decidet super eos timor]]. [[14:5|And when you shall know that they are fleeing, go after them securely|Quumque cognoveritis fugere eos, ite post eos securi]] of victory, [[14:5|for the Lord will destroy them under your feet|quoniam Dominus conteret eos sub pedibus vestris]] [the print of this verse is damaged; it is read with the help of the Vulgate].

paras.t: Tunc Achior, videns virtutem quam fecit Deus Israel, id est magnificum illum effectum Dei, relicto gentilitatis ritu, id est cultu idolorum, credidit Deo, id est, legem Moysis acceptavit, credens contentis in ea. Et circumcidit carnem præputii sui, id est, circumcidi fecit secundum legis tenorem: et appositus est ad populum Israel, et omnis successio generis ejus. Præterea quæri potest, qualiter licuit Hebræis ipsum Achior ad suam communionem ita suscipere, quum in Deuteronomio jusserit Dominus: Ammonites et Moabites etiam post decimam generationem non intrabunt in Ecclesiam Dei in æternum. Respondetur, quod illud præceptum dispensationem admisit ex inspiratione divina in certis personis, propter earum præcipuam devotionem et benevolentiam circa Deum legis et populum ejus, sicut in Ruth Moabitide, et isto Achior Ammonite: prout Thomas in prima secundæ magis declarat.
paras.en: [[14:6|Then Achior seeing the power that the God of Israel had wrought|Tunc Achior, videns virtutem quam fecit Deus Israel]], that is, that magnificent work of God, [[14:6|leaving the religion of the Gentiles|relicto gentilitatis ritu]], that is, the worship of idols, [[14:6|he believed God|credidit Deo]], that is, he accepted the law of Moses, believing what it contains; [[14:6|and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin|Et circumcidit carnem præputii sui]], that is, had himself circumcised according to the tenor of the law; [[14:6|and was joined to the people of Israel, with all the succession of his kindred|et appositus est ad populum Israel, et omnis successio generis ejus]]. It may be asked besides how it was lawful for the Hebrews to receive this Achior into their communion so, since the Lord commanded in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:3|The Ammonite and the Moabite, even after the tenth generation shall not enter into the church of the Lord for ever|Ammonites et Moabites etiam post decimam generationem non intrabunt in Ecclesiam Dei in æternum]]. The answer is that this precept admitted of dispensation by divine inspiration in certain persons, on account of their special devotion and good will towards the God of the law and his people, as in Ruth the Moabitess[[Ruth 1:1||]] and in this Achior the Ammonite, as Thomas explains more fully in the First Part of the Second Part [that is, of the *Summa theologiae*, I-II, q. 105, a. 3].

paras.t: Mox autem ut orta est dies. Hic refertur, qualiter exsecuti sint filii Israel jussionem Judith: nec est difficultas in littera, idcirco nec immorandum. Quod videntes exploratores ad tabernaculum Holofernis cucurrerunt; vel ad tentoria Assyriorum, intelligendo plurale per singulare. Porro hi qui in tabernaculo erant Holofernis, ante ingressum cubiculi perstrepentes, et sonitum facientes cum motu pedum, ac aliis signis, inquietudinem arte moliebantur, ut non ab excitantibus, sed a sonantibus Holofernes evigilaret, id est, cum industria exercebant resonantiam quamdam. Nullus enim audebat tabernaculum virtutis Assyriorum, id est ædem, cameram seu cubiculum regis aut principis Assyriorum, pulsando aut intrando per januam, aperire. Sed quum venissent duces, qui singulis præerant aciebus, et tribuni, qui dicuntur præfuisse mille viris, dixerunt cubiculariis, qui confidentius intrant cubilia dominorum suorum: Intrate, et excitate illum, quoniam egressi mures de cavernis, id est latibulis suis, ausi sunt nos provocare ad prælium. Tam aspernanter locuti sunt Assyrii de Israelitis ex magnitudine elationis, ideo meruerunt ab his, quos pro nihilo reputabant, dejici.
paras.en: [[14:7|And immediately at break of day|Mox autem ut orta est dies]]. Here it is told how the children of Israel carried out Judith's command; there is no difficulty in the letter, and so no need to dwell on it. [[14:8|And the watchmen seeing this, ran to the tent of Holofernes|Quod videntes exploratores ad tabernaculum Holofernis cucurrerunt]]; or to the tents of the Assyrians, understanding the plural by the singular. [[14:9|And they that were in the tent|Porro hi qui in tabernaculo erant]] of Holofernes [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], [[14:9|made a noise, before the door of the chamber|ante ingressum cubiculi perstrepentes]], making a sound with the movement of their feet and other signs, [[14:9|endeavouring by art to break his rest|inquietudinem arte moliebantur]], [[14:9|that Holofernes might awake, not by their calling him, but by their noise|ut non ab excitantibus, sed a sonantibus Holofernes evigilaret]], that is, they made a kind of resounding on purpose. [[14:10|For no man durst knock, or open and go into|Nullus enim audebat]] [[14:10|the chamber of the general of the Assyrians|tabernaculum virtutis Assyriorum]] [Denis reads *tabernaculum*, “tent”, for the Vulgate's *cubiculum*: literally “the tent of the might of the Assyrians”], that is, the house, room or bedchamber of the king or prince of the Assyrians, by knocking, or by going in at the door. [[14:11|But when his captains|Sed quum venissent duces]], who commanded the several battle-lines, [[14:11|and tribunes were come|et tribuni]], who are said to have commanded a thousand men, [[14:11|they said to the chamberlains|dixerunt cubiculariis]], who go more freely into their masters' bedchambers: [[14:12|Go in, and awake him|Intrate, et excitate illum]], [[14:12|for the mice, coming out of their holes|quoniam egressi mures de cavernis]], that is, their hiding-places, [[14:12|have presumed to challenge us to fight|ausi sunt nos provocare ad prælium]]. So scornfully did the Assyrians speak of the Israelites, out of the greatness of their pride; therefore they deserved to be cast down by those whom they counted as nothing.

paras.t: Tunc Vagao ingressus cubiculum ejus, stetit ante cortinam, et plausum fecit manibus suis: suspicabatur enim illum cum Judith dormire. Sed quum nullum motum jacentis sensu aurium caperet, accessit proximans ad cortinam. Et elevans eam, vidensque cadaver absque capite Holofernis in suo sanguine tabefactum, id est infectum atque fœdatum, jacere super terram, exclamavit voce magna cum fletu, et scidit vestimenta sua; et ingressus tabernaculum Judith, non invenit eam. Et exsilivit foras ad populum, et dixit: Una mulier Hebræa fecit confusionem, id est confusibile homicidium, occidendo principem nostrum, in domo regis Nabuchodonosor, id est in populo ejus. Ecce enim Holofernes jacet in terra, et caput ejus non est in illo. Quod quum audissent principes virtutis, id est exercitus seu acierum, Assyriorum, sciderunt vestimenta sua præ dolore. Et intolerabilis timor et tremor cecidit super eos, et turbati [sunt] animi eorum valde. Et factus est clamor incomparabilis in medio castrorum eorum. Audientes enim principem suum esse occisum a muliere Hebræa, non confidebant se posse resistere viris Hebræis contra se venientibus et armatis.
paras.en: [[14:13|Then Vagao going into his chamber, stood before the curtain, and made a clapping with his hands: for he thought that he was sleeping with Judith.|Tunc Vagao ingressus cubiculum ejus, stetit ante cortinam, et plausum fecit manibus suis: suspicabatur enim illum cum Judith dormire]] [[14:14|But when with hearkening, he perceived no motion of one lying, he came near to the curtain|Sed quum nullum motum jacentis sensu aurium caperet, accessit proximans ad cortinam]]. [[14:14|and lifting it up, and seeing the body of Holofernes|Et elevans eam, vidensque cadaver]] [[14:14|without the head, weltering in his blood|absque capite Holofernis in suo sanguine tabefactum]], that is, stained and befouled, [[14:14|lying upon the ground|jacere super terram]], [[14:14|he cried out with a loud voice, with weeping, and rent his garments|exclamavit voce magna cum fletu, et scidit vestimenta sua]]; [[14:15|And he went into the tent of Judith, and not finding her|et ingressus tabernaculum Judith, non invenit eam]], [[14:15|he ran out to the people|Et exsilivit foras ad populum]], [[14:16|And said: One Hebrew woman hath made confusion|et dixit: Una mulier Hebræa fecit confusionem]], that is, a shameful killing, by killing our prince, [[14:16|in the house of king Nabuchodonosor|in domo regis Nabuchodonosor]], that is, among his people. [[14:16|for behold Holofernes lieth upon the ground, and his head is not upon him|Ecce enim Holofernes jacet in terra, et caput ejus non est in illo]]. [[14:17|Now when the chiefs of the army|Quod quum audissent principes virtutis]], that is, of the host or of its battle-lines, [[14:17|of the Assyrians had heard this|Assyriorum]], [[14:17|they all rent their garments|sciderunt vestimenta sua]] for grief. [[14:17|and an intolerable fear and dread fell upon them, and their minds were troubled exceedingly|Et intolerabilis timor et tremor cecidit super eos, et turbati [sunt] animi eorum valde]]. [[14:18|And there was a very great cry in the midst of their camp.|Et factus est clamor incomparabilis in medio castrorum eorum]] For hearing that their prince had been killed by a Hebrew woman, they did not trust that they could resist the Hebrew men coming against them in arms.

15.title: Declaratio capituli quintidecimi: Quumque omnis exercitus decollatum Holofernem audisset
15.title_en: Explanation of the fifteenth chapter: And when all the army heard that Holofernes was beheaded

paras.t: Fuga et debellatio Assyriorum hic describuntur.
paras.en: Here the flight and overthrow of the Assyrians are described.

paras.t: Quumque omnis exercitus Assyriorum decollatum Holofernem audisset, fugit mens, id est usus rationis quoad multa, et consilium ab eis: ita quod non conferebant, nec inquirebant de modo resistendi Hebræis, qui respectu Assyriorum paucissimi erant, ac ulciscendi tam confusibilem mortem principis sui. Et solo tremore et metu agitati, fugæ præsidium sumunt, id est, fugam pro remedio ac subsidio assumpserunt, ita ut nullus loqueretur cum proximo suo, sed inclinato capite, relictis omnibus, evadere festinabant Hebræos, quos armatos super se venire audierant. Sic enim timor prædominans et perturbatio obtenebraverant corda eorum; nec egerunt quemadmodum primo Machabæorum exercitus Jonathæ narratur fecisse: qui cognoscens Jonathan dominum suum perisse, hortati sunt se mutuo ad resistendum hostibus suis super se venientibus, et ipsos hostes verterunt in fugam. Fugientes Assyrii per vias camporum et semitas collium: fugientes enim de bello, divisim per diversas fugiunt vias. Itaque filii Israel [fugientes secuti sunt...] ululantes, id est alte clamantes, post ipsos Assyrios fugientes. Et quoniam Assyrii non adunati, in fugam ibant præcipites, id est huc illucque ruentes seu vacillantes; filii autem Israel uno agmine, id est pariter adunati persequentes Assyrios, debilitabant, vulnerando aut occidendo, omnes quos invenire potuissent.
paras.en: [[15:1|And when all the army heard that Holofernes was beheaded|Quumque omnis exercitus Assyriorum decollatum Holofernem audisset]], [[15:1|courage|fugit mens]] [*mens*, “mind”], that is, the use of reason in many respects, [[15:1|and counsel fled from them|et consilium ab eis]], so that they did not confer together nor inquire how to resist the Hebrews, who compared with the Assyrians were very few, and to avenge so shameful a death of their prince. [[15:1|and being seized with trembling and fear|Et solo tremore et metu agitati]], [[15:1|they thought only to save themselves by flight|fugæ præsidium sumunt]] [literally, “they take the safeguard of flight”], that is, they took to flight as their remedy and help, [[15:2|So that no one spoke to his neighbour, but hanging down the head, leaving all things behind, they made haste to escape from the Hebrews, who, as they heard, were coming armed upon them|ita ut nullus loqueretur cum proximo suo, sed inclinato capite, relictis omnibus, evadere festinabant Hebræos, quos armatos super se venire audierant]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate; the margin gives the reading *audiebant*, the Vulgate's]. For overmastering fear and confusion had so darkened their hearts; nor did they do as the army of Jonathan is told in the first book of Machabees to have done, which, learning that Jonathan its lord had perished, exhorted one another to resist their enemies who were coming upon them, and turned those enemies to flight[[1 Mach 12:50||]]. [[15:2|and fled by the ways of the fields, and the paths of the hills|Fugientes Assyrii per vias camporum et semitas collium]]: for men fleeing from battle flee scattered by different ways. [[15:3|So the children of Israel|Itaque filii Israel]] [[15:3|seeing them fleeing, followed after them|fugientes secuti sunt]] [the print gives these words in brackets, shortened: *fugientes secuti sunt…*], [[15:3|and shouting|ululantes]], that is, crying aloud, after the fleeing Assyrians. [[15:4|And because the Assyrians were not united together, they went without order in their flight|Et quoniam Assyrii non adunati, in fugam ibant præcipites]], that is, rushing or staggering this way and that; [[15:4|but the children of Israel|filii autem Israel]], [[15:4|in one body|uno agmine]], that is, all united together, [[15:4|pursuing|persequentes]] the Assyrians, [[15:4|defeated|debilitabant]] [*debilitabant*, literally “weakened”], by wounding or killing, [[15:4|all that they could find|omnes quos invenire potuissent]].

paras.t: Misitque nuntios Ozias per omnes civitates et regiones, id est per terras duodecim tribuum Israel. Omnis itaque regio illa, omnisque urbs electam juventutem, id est elegantes robustosque juvenes bellatores, armatam misit post eos, id est ad insequendum Assyrios; et persecuti sunt eos in ore gladii, quousque pervenirent ad extremitatem finium suorum. Reliqui autem qui erant in Bethulia, ingressi sunt castra Assyriorum, et prædam abstulerunt. Hi vero qui victores reversi sunt ab insecutione Assyriorum, omnia quæ erant illorum, quæ scilicet Assyrii fugientes reliquerunt in campis atque tentoriis, abstulerunt.
paras.en: [[15:5|And Ozias sent messengers through all the cities and countries|Misitque nuntios Ozias per omnes civitates et regiones]], that is, through the lands of the twelve tribes [[15:5|of Israel|Israel]]. [[15:6|And every country, and every city, sent their chosen young men|Omnis itaque regio illa, omnisque urbs electam juventutem]], that is, fine and sturdy young warriors, [[15:6|armed after them|armatam misit post eos]], that is, to pursue the Assyrians; [[15:6|and they pursued them with the edge of the sword until they came to the extremities of their confines|et persecuti sunt eos in ore gladii, quousque pervenirent ad extremitatem finium suorum]]. [[15:7|And the rest that were in Bethulia went into the camp of the Assyrians|Reliqui autem qui erant in Bethulia, ingressi sunt castra Assyriorum]], [[15:7|and took away the spoils|et prædam abstulerunt]]. [[15:8|But they that returned conquerors|Hi vero qui victores reversi sunt]] from the pursuit of the Assyrians took away [[15:8|all things that were theirs|omnia quæ erant illorum]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], namely what the Assyrians in their flight left in the fields and tents [Denis's text has *abstulerunt*, “took away”, for the Vulgate's *attulerunt secum*, “brought with them”].

paras.t: Joachim autem summus pontifex: qui supra vocatus est Eliachim, secundum probabiliorem opinionem; venit in Bethuliam cum universis presbyteris suis, ut videret Judith. Naturale namque est homini, libenter videre eos qui magna et mira atque insolita operantur. Nam et in ipsis auctoribus mirabilia gesta eorum quodammodo conspiciuntur, sicut effectus in sua causa. Similiter homines eminenter sapientes et sancti, libenter videntur, sicut et cetera quæ magnæ excellentiæ sunt.
paras.en: [[15:9|And Joachim the high priest|Joachim autem summus pontifex]], who above was called Eliachim[[Jdt 4:5||]] [the margin seems to give Judith iv], according to the more probable opinion, [[15:9|came|venit]] [[15:9|to Bethulia with all his ancients to see Judith|in Bethuliam cum universis presbyteris suis, ut videret Judith]]. For it is natural to man to like to see those who do great, wonderful and unwonted things. For in their very doers their wonderful deeds are in a manner beheld, as an effect in its cause. Likewise men eminently wise and holy are gladly seen, as are other things of great excellence.

paras.t: Quæ quum exisset ad illum, benedixerunt, id est laudaverunt, illam omnes, videlicet pontifex et sacerdotes, una, id est consona voce, dicentes, seu uno verba alterius approbante et confirmante: Tu gloria Jerusalem, id est objectum, causa et materia gloriæ et honoris civitatis Jerusalem et habitatorum ipsius, quoniam eruisti eam et templum ac habitantes in ea a magnis periculis, et a violatione divini cultus. Sic quoque tu es lætitia Israel, id est Israeliticæ plebis, quam nunc magnifice lætificasti. Tu honorificentia populi tui, id est causa et materia honoris et sublimationis tuorum concivium, propinquorum et amicorum. Quia fecisti viriliter, non muliebriter, et gratiam sic agendi accepisti a Domino, et confortatum est cor tuum, eo quod castitatem amaveris vidualem ex caritate, hoc est Dei intuitu et amore, sine quo nihil est meritorium apud Deum, et post virum tuum alterum nescieris, quum tamen sis juvenis, pulchra, opulenta, nobilis, et multam familiam habens. Et ideo manus Domini confortavit te, ad faciendum opus tam magnum. Et eris benedicta in æternum, id est, in Ecclesia militante laudaberis usque in finem mundi, atque in triumphante Ecclesia eris perpetue gloriosa.
paras.en: [[15:10|And when she was come out to him|Quæ quum exisset ad illum]], [[15:10|they all blessed her|benedixerunt]], that is, praised her, all of them, namely the high priest and the priests, [[15:10|with one|una]], that is, with a harmonious, [[15:10|voice|voce]], [[15:10|saying|dicentes]], or each approving and confirming the words of another: [[15:10|Thou art the glory of Jerusalem|Tu gloria Jerusalem]], that is, the object, cause and matter of the glory and honour of the city of Jerusalem and of its inhabitants, since thou hast rescued it, and the temple and those who dwell in it, from great dangers and from the violation of the divine worship. So too [[15:10|thou art the joy of Israel|tu es lætitia Israel]], that is, of the Israelite people, whom thou hast now made magnificently glad. [[15:10|thou art the honour of our people|Tu honorificentia populi tui]] [Denis's text has *tui*, “thy”; the margin gives *nostri*, the Vulgate's], that is, the cause and matter of honour and exaltation for thy fellow citizens, kinsfolk and friends. [[15:11|For thou hast done manfully|Quia fecisti viriliter]], not as a woman, and thou hast received from the Lord the grace to act so, [[15:11|and thy heart has been strengthened, because thou hast loved chastity|et confortatum est cor tuum, eo quod castitatem amaveris]], a widow's chastity, out of charity, that is, with regard to God and for love of him, without which nothing is meritorious before God, [[15:11|and after thy husband hast not known any other|et post virum tuum alterum nescieris]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], though thou art young, beautiful, wealthy, noble, and with a large household. [[15:11|therefore also the hand of the Lord hath strengthened thee|Et ideo manus Domini confortavit te]] to do so great a work. [[15:11|and therefore thou shalt be blessed for ever|Et eris benedicta in æternum]], that is, thou shalt be praised in the Church militant until the end of the world, and in the Church triumphant thou shalt be glorious for ever.

paras.t: Per dies autem triginta vix collecta sunt spolia Assyriorum a populo Israel. Porro universa quæ Holofernis peculiaria fuisse probata sunt, id est, cuncta quæ Judith et populus certe aut probabiliter cognoverunt proprie pertinuisse ad Holofernem et usum ipsius, dederunt Judith in auro et argento, et vestibus, et gemmis, et omni supellectili, et tradita sunt illi omnia a populo, tanquam victrici principis tanti, et procuratrici totius victoriæ.
paras.en: [[15:13|And thirty days were scarce sufficient for the people of Israel to gather up the spoils of the Assyrians.|Per dies autem triginta vix collecta sunt spolia Assyriorum a populo Israel]] [[15:14|But all those things that were proved to be the peculiar goods of Holofernes|Porro universa quæ Holofernis peculiaria fuisse probata sunt]], that is, all the things that Judith and the people knew certainly or probably to have belonged properly to Holofernes and to his use, [[15:14|they gave to Judith in gold, and silver, and garments and precious stones, and all household stuff|dederunt Judith in auro et argento, et vestibus, et gemmis, et omni supellectili]], [[15:14|and they all were delivered to her by the people|et tradita sunt illi omnia a populo]], as to the conqueror of so great a prince, and the one who brought about the whole victory.

16.title: Elucidatio capituli sextidecimi: Tunc cantavit canticum hoc Domino Judith
16.title_en: Explanation of the sixteenth chapter: Then Judith sung this canticle to the Lord

paras.t: Finaliter introducitur hic laus et gratiarum actio Judith, quam obtulit Deo in recognitionem beneficiorum suorum ac tanti triumphi. Consuetudo autem fuit Judæis, de magnis beneficiis atque victoriis canticum Deo offerre.
paras.en: Finally, here is brought in the praise and thanksgiving of Judith, which she offered to God in acknowledgement of his benefits and of so great a triumph. For it was the custom of the Jews to offer a canticle to God for great benefits and victories.

paras.t: Tunc cantavit canticum hoc Domino Judith, dicens: Incipite Domino in tympanis, id est, cum talibus musicis instrumentis incipite Deum laudare, quatenus ex melodia musicorum provocemini ad devotionem majorem; et eadem ratione, cantate Domino in cymbalis. Porro tympanum est pellis seu corium super lignum extentum ex una parte: et significat carnis castigationem ac mortificationem, spiritualemque jucunditatem in tali virtuoso exercitio consistentem. Cymbalum vero est musicum instrumentum, ex permixtis metallis sonum reddens acutum: per quod unanimis plurima psalmodia, seu laus Deo oblata, exprimitur. Idcirco qui carnem suam cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigit, atque cum aliis concorditer psallit, spiritualiter cantat Domino Deo in cymbalis, juxta illud ad Romanos: Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum. Modulamini, id est, cantate illi, psalmum novum, id est recens præconium pro novis beneficiis istis. Exsultate spirituali lætitia, et invocate nomen ejus, id est, ex intimo cordis affectu ipsum orate.
paras.en: [[16:1|Then Judith sung this canticle to the Lord, saying|Tunc cantavit canticum hoc Domino Judith, dicens]]: [[16:2|Begin ye to the Lord with timbrels|Incipite Domino in tympanis]], that is, begin to praise God with such musical instruments, so that by the melody of the music you may be roused to greater devotion; and for the same reason, [[16:2|sing ye to the Lord with cymbals|cantate Domino in cymbalis]]. Now a timbrel is a skin or hide stretched over wood on one side; and it signifies the chastising and mortifying of the flesh, and the spiritual gladness that lies in such virtuous exercise. A cymbal is a musical instrument giving a high sound from mixed metals, by which the psalmody of many voices of one mind, or the praise offered to God, is signified. Therefore he who crucifies his flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]], and sings psalms in concord with others, spiritually sings to the Lord God with cymbals[[Ps 150:5||]] [the margin's Ps. cl, 5 is partly misread], according to the word to the Romans: [[Rom 15:6|That with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify God|Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum]]. [[16:2|tune unto him|Modulamini]], that is, sing unto him, [[16:2|a new psalm|psalmum novum]], that is, a fresh proclamation for these new benefits. [[16:2|extol|Exsultate]] [Denis's text has *exsultate*, “exult”, for the Vulgate's *exaltate*] with spiritual gladness, [[16:2|and call upon his name|et invocate nomen ejus]], that is, pray to him from the inmost affection of the heart.

paras.t: Dominus conterens bella, id est, bellatores et bella injusta contra populum suum insurgentia destruens, dando victoriam suis fidelibus, sicut in Exodo, Josue, Judicum, librisque Regum, Paralipomenon et Machabæorum, copiose describitur. Invisibilium quoque hostium tentamenta et prælia facit superari ac destrui, juxta illud ad Romanos: Deus conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter. Dominus nomen est illi. Qui posuit castra sua, id est tentoria seu exercitus suos, vel angelorum subsidia: de quibus Joel, Multa (inquit) sunt nimis castra Dei, fortia et facientia verbum ejus. Unde visis angelis sibi obviantibus, Jacob ait in Genesi: Castra Dei sunt hæc. In medio populi sui, ut eriperet nos de manu omnium inimicorum nostrorum visibilium et invisibilium: juxta illud in Psalmo, Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis. De quibus et quarto Regum libro loquitur Elisæus: Plures nobiscum sunt quam cum illis, id est cum pravis hominibus.
paras.en: [[16:3|The Lord putteth an end to wars|Dominus conterens bella]], that is, destroying the warriors and the unjust wars that rise against his people, by giving victory to his faithful, as is abundantly described in Exodus, Josue, Judges, and the books of Kings, Paralipomenon and Machabees.
