He also makes the temptations and battles of invisible enemies to be overcome and destroyed, according to the word to the Romans: God will [[Rom 16:20|crush Satan under your feet speedily|conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]]. [[16:3|the Lord is his name|Dominus nomen est illi]]. [[16:4|He hath set his camp|Qui posuit castra sua]], that is, his tents or his armies, or the help of the angels, of which Joel says: [[Joel 2:11|for his armies are exceedingly great, for they are strong, and execute his word|sunt nimis castra Dei, fortia et facientia verbum ejus]]. Hence, when he saw the angels coming to meet him, Jacob said in Genesis: [[Gen 32:2|These are the camps of God|Castra Dei sunt hæc]]. [[16:4|in the midst of his people, to deliver us from the hand of all our enemies|In medio populi sui, ut eriperet nos de manu omnium inimicorum nostrorum]], visible and invisible, according to the word in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:11|For he hath given his angels charge over thee; to keep thee in all thy ways|Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis]]. Of these too Eliseus speaks in the fourth book of Kings: [[4 Kings 6:16|there are more with us than with them|Plures nobiscum sunt quam cum illis]], that is, than with wicked men.

paras.t: Venit Assur, id est exercitus Assyriorum cum principe suo, ex montibus ab aquilone, id est per loca montuosa a plaga septentrionali secundum unum respectum, ut tactum est supra, in multitudine fortitudinis suæ: cujus multitudo obturavit torrentes, eos terra replendo aut epotando per se et per sua jumenta. Dixit se incensurum fines meos, id est oppida, villas, castella terræ promissionis, et juvenes meos occisurum gladio, infantes meos dare in prædam, et virgines in captivitatem. Dominus autem omnipotens: qui ait in Jeremia: Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo? nocuit, id est læsit, eum (secundum antiquam grammaticam), et tradidit in manus feminæ principem Assyriorum. Et confudit eum, id est, confusibiliter fecit occidi.
paras.en: [[16:5|The Assyrian came|Venit Assur]], that is, the army of the Assyrians with its prince, [[16:5|out of the mountains from the north|ex montibus ab aquilone]], that is, through mountainous country, from the northern quarter in one respect, as was touched on above, [[16:5|in the multitude of his strength: his multitude stopped up the torrents|in multitudine fortitudinis suæ: cujus multitudo obturavit torrentes]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], filling them with earth, or drinking them dry, themselves and their beasts. [[16:6|He bragged that he would set my borders on fire|Dixit se incensurum fines meos]], that is, the towns, villages and strongholds of the land of promise, [[16:6|and kill my young men with the sword, to make my infants a prey, and my virgins captives|et juvenes meos occisurum gladio, infantes meos dare in prædam, et virgines in captivitatem]]. [[16:7|But the almighty Lord|Dominus autem omnipotens]] [these words too are damaged in the print], who says in Jeremias: [[Jer 49:19|for who is like to me? and who shall abide me? and who is that shepherd that can withstand my countenance?|Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo?]] [the margin gives Jer. xlix, 19; the same words stand at 50:44] [[16:7|hath struck him|nocuit eum]], that is, harmed him (so according to the old grammar) [*nocere*, “to harm”, here takes the accusative], [[16:7|and hath delivered|et tradidit]] the prince of the Assyrians [[16:7|into the hands of a woman|in manus feminæ]]. [[16:7|and hath slain him|Et confudit eum]] [Denis's text has *confudit*, “confounded”, for the Vulgate's *confodit*, “pierced”], that is, he had him killed shamefully.

paras.t: Non enim cecidit potens eorum a juvenibus, id est Holofernes, princeps et potentior inter suos. Quemadmodum enim naturale robur corporis præcipue consistit in corde, sic fortitudo exercitus in principe militiæ. Hinc libro de Re militari ait Vegetius, quod sicut cor est in medio corporis, sic princeps militiæ esse debet in medio sui exercitus. Itaque potens ille non cecidit a juvenibus, id est, interfectus non est manu juvenum, qui in bellis frequenter se exponunt periculis, ut magnum aliquid agere videantur, et probitatem ostendant. Unde secundo libro Regum Abner dixit ad Joab: Surgant pueri et ludant coram nobis. Quorum unusquisque defixit gladium suum in latus contrarii. Et vocatus est locus ille, ager Fortium. Nec filii Titan percusserunt eum. Filii Titan dicuntur quidam Græcorum valde excellentes in viribus, qui interdum vocantur Titanes. Titan quoque nonnunquam pro sole accipitur: a quo dicuntur Titanes, quasi mundum sua proprietate illuminantes. Idcirco inepta videtur expositio intelligentium per filios Titan, filios gigantis sive gigantum. De quibus et subditur: Nec excelsi gigantes opposuerunt se illi.
paras.en: [[16:8|For their mighty one did not fall by young men|Non enim cecidit potens eorum a juvenibus]], that is, Holofernes, the prince and the mightiest among his own. For as the natural strength of the body lies chiefly in the heart, so the strength of an army lies in the prince of the host. Hence Vegetius says in his book On Military Matters that as the heart is in the middle of the body, so the prince of the host ought to be in the middle of his army. So that mighty one did not fall by young men, that is, he was not killed by the hand of young men, who in wars often expose themselves to dangers so as to be seen to do something great and to show their prowess. Hence in the second book of Kings Abner said to Joab: [[2 Kings 2:14|Let the young men rise, and play before us|Surgant pueri et ludant coram nobis]]. Of whom each one [[2 Kings 2:16|thrust his sword into the side of his adversary|defixit gladium suum in latus contrarii]]; and that place was called the Field of the Strong [the margin, partly misread, gives II Reg. ii, 14, 16]. [[16:8|neither did the sons of Titan strike him|Nec filii Titan percusserunt eum]]. Certain Greeks of very great strength are called the sons of Titan, and they are sometimes called Titans. Titan is also sometimes taken for the sun, from which they are called Titans, as if they lit up the world by their property. Therefore the exposition of those who understand by the sons of Titan the sons of the giant, or of the giants, seems unfitting. Of these it is also added: [[16:8|nor tall giants oppose themselves to him|Nec excelsi gigantes opposuerunt se illi]].

paras.t: Sed Judith filia Merari: cujus genealogia supra descripta est; in specie faciei suæ dissolvit eum, hoc est, per pulchritudinem traxit eum in laqueum mortis, juxta sensum introductum: ex qua expositione patet sensus verborum sequentium, Exuit se vestimento viduitatis, usque ibi, Amputavit cervicem ejus pugione, id est gladio brevi pungenti. Horruerunt Persæ constantiam ejus, hoc est, horror invasit corda Persarum ex consideratione constantis Judith, quæ tantum principem ausa fuit invadere, et Medi audaciam ejus. Hi Persæ et Medi fuerunt in Assyriorum exercitu, qui cum stupore timuerunt tam horrendam sui principis mortem a femina attentatam.
paras.en: [[16:8|but Judith the daughter of Merari|Sed Judith filia Merari]], whose genealogy was set out above[[Jdt 8:1||]], [[16:8|weakened him with the beauty of her face|in specie faciei suæ dissolvit eum]], that is, by her beauty drew him into the snare of death, in the sense brought in before[[Jdt 10:17||]] [the margin gives Ibid. x, 17]: from which exposition the sense of the following words is plain, from [[16:9|For she put off her the garments of widowhood|Exuit se vestimento viduitatis]] as far as [[16:11|with a sword she cut off his head|Amputavit cervicem ejus pugione]], that is, with a short stabbing sword. [[16:12|The Persians quaked at her constancy|Horruerunt Persæ constantiam ejus]], that is, horror seized the hearts of the Persians at the thought of the steadfast Judith, who had dared to attack so great a prince, [[16:12|and the Medes at her boldness|et Medi audaciam ejus]]. These Persians and Medes were in the army of the Assyrians, and they feared with amazement so horrible a death of their prince, brought about by a woman.

paras.t: Tunc ululaverunt castra Assyriorum, hoc est, acies eorum miserabiliter clamaverunt, sicut in quartidecimi fine capituli legitur: Factus est clamor incomparabilis in medio castrorum eorum; quando apparuerunt humiles mei, hoc est filii Israel, præsertim habitatores Bethuliæ ad Deum humiliter clamitantes, arescentes in siti, hoc est aridi præ potus inopia. Filii puellarum compunxerunt eos, id est, filii Israel ex Hebræis puellis nati, simul vulneraverunt et punxerunt fugientes Assyrios. Et perierunt Assyrii in prælio a facie Domini mei, hoc est, ab adspectu et adjutorio Dei occisi sunt Assyrii, in illa impugnatione eis ab Hebræis illata.
paras.en: [[16:13|Then the camp of the Assyrians howled|Tunc ululaverunt castra Assyriorum]], that is, their battle-lines cried out miserably, as we read at the end of the fourteenth chapter: [[Jdt 14:18|And there was a very great cry in the midst of their camp|Factus est clamor incomparabilis in medio castrorum eorum]]; [[16:13|when my lowly ones appeared|quando apparuerunt humiles mei]], that is, the children of Israel, especially the dwellers in Bethulia, humbly crying out to God, [[16:13|parched with thirst|arescentes in siti]], that is, dry for want of drink. [[16:14|The sons of the damsels have pierced them through|Filii puellarum compunxerunt eos]], that is, the children of Israel born of Hebrew maidens together wounded and pierced the fleeing Assyrians. And the Assyrians [[16:14|perished in battle before the face of the Lord my God|perierunt Assyrii in prælio a facie Domini mei]], that is, by the regard and help of God the Assyrians were slain, in that attack made on them by the Hebrews.

paras.t: Hymnum cantemus Domino; hymnum novum cantemus Deo nostro. Adonai Domine, magnus es tu. Adonai, est nomen Hebraicum, quod interpretatur Dominus. Sicque duo hic nomina, idem significant; et unum est expositivum alterius, sicut quum dicitur, Abba pater. Atque, ut asserit Glossa, Adonai est unum de decem nominibus Dei apud Hebræos. Præterea aliqui libri habent: Adonai Domine Deus. Et sic Magister in historiis ponit, addens: Super hoc canticum invenis, quod dicit Hieronymus super Psalmum, Domine Dominus noster: quia quum in Hebræo legitur nomen Domini geminatum, sicut hic, Adonai Domine Deus, primum est τετραγράμματον, apud Hebræos ἄρρητον, hoc est ineffabile: secundum vero est nomen Domini commune. Itaque, Adonai Domine, magnus es tu, non corporis quantitate, sed incircumscriptibili majestate, et prorsus infinita perfectione. Et præclarus in virtute tua, hoc est excellentissimus potestate et sanctitate, ac in te ipso supersplendidissimus et superpulcherrimus, inaccessibilem lucem inhabitans.
paras.en: [[16:15|Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, let us sing a new hymn to our God.|Hymnum cantemus Domino; hymnum novum cantemus Deo nostro]] [[16:16|O Adonai, Lord, great art thou|Adonai Domine, magnus es tu]]. Adonai is a Hebrew name, which is interpreted Lord. And so the two names here signify the same thing, and the one explains the other, as when it is said: [[Mark 14:36|Abba, Father|Abba pater]][[Rom 8:15||]][[Gal 4:6||]] [the margin gives Marc. xiv (?), Rom. viii, 15 and Gal. iv, 6]. And, as the Gloss asserts, Adonai is one of the ten names of God among the Hebrews. Besides, some books have: Adonai, Lord God. And so the Master puts it in the Histories [that is, Peter Comestor in the *Historia scholastica*], adding: On this canticle you find what Jerome says on the Psalm [[Ps 8:2|O Lord our Lord|Domine Dominus noster]]: that when in the Hebrew the name of the Lord is read twice, as here, Adonai, Lord God, the first is the *tetragrammaton* [the name of four letters], among the Hebrews *arreton*, that is, unspeakable, while the second is the common name of the Lord. So then: O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, not in bodily size, but in uncircumscribable majesty and wholly infinite perfection. [[16:16|and glorious in thy power|Et præclarus in virtute tua]], that is, most excellent in power and holiness, and in thyself more than most splendid and more than most beautiful, who [[1 Tim 6:16|inhabiteth light inaccessible|inaccessibilem lucem inhabitans]].

paras.t: Tibi serviat omnis creatura tua: quia dixisti, et facta sunt; misisti spiritum tuum, et creata sunt, id est, imperium effudisti, seu Spiritus Sancti potestatem in opus procedere voluisti: juxta illud Psalmistæ, Verbo Domini cœli firmati sunt, et spiritu oris ejus omnis virtus eorum. Et non est qui resistat voci tuæ, hoc est tuo imperio, quo absolute vis aliquid fieri. Nullus quoque potest verbis divinarum jussionum de jure resistere: quibus tamen de facto multi resistunt. Montes a fundamentis movebuntur cum aquis, quando tu jusseris: juxta illud, Qui respicit terram, et facit eam tremere; qui tangit montes, et fumigant. Petræ sicut cera liquescent ante faciem tuam, hoc est ex majestatis tuæ præsentia et præcepto. Quod tamen imminente futuro generali judicio, maxime fiet per ignem conflagrationis, secundum illud, Ignis ante ipsum præcedet; itemque, Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini. Hinc fertur in Job: Qui transtulit montes, et nescierunt hi quos subvertit: qui commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutientur. Ecclesiasticus quoque ait: Ecce cœlum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur; montes simul et colles, et fundamenta terræ, et quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur. Qui autem timent te filiali timore, perseveranter usque in finem, magni erunt apud te per omnia: quia fulgebunt sicut sol in regno suo, et nihil deerit eis.
paras.en: [[16:17|Let all thy creatures serve thee|Tibi serviat omnis creatura tua]]: [[16:17|because thou hast spoken, and they were made: thou didst send forth thy spirit, and they were created|quia dixisti, et facta sunt; misisti spiritum tuum, et creata sunt]], that is, thou didst pour forth thy command, or didst will the power of the Holy Spirit to go forth into the work, according to the word of the Psalmist: [[Ps 32:6|By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth|Verbo Domini cœli firmati sunt, et spiritu oris ejus omnis virtus eorum]]. [[16:17|and there is no one that can resist thy voice|Et non est qui resistat voci tuæ]], that is, thy command, by which thou willest absolutely that something be done. Nor can anyone by right resist the words of the divine commands, though in fact many resist them. [[16:18|The mountains shall be moved from the foundations with the waters|Montes a fundamentis movebuntur cum aquis]], when thou shalt command, according to the word: [[Ps 103:32|He looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble: he troubleth the mountains, and they smoke|Qui respicit terram, et facit eam tremere; qui tangit montes, et fumigant]]. [[16:18|the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face|Petræ sicut cera liquescent ante faciem tuam]], that is, at the presence and command of thy majesty. Yet this will be done chiefly by the fire of the conflagration, when the future general judgement is at hand, according to the word: [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet]]; and again: [[Ps 96:5|The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord|Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini]]. Hence it is said in Job: [[Job 9:5|Who hath removed mountains|Qui transtulit montes]], and they knew it not, [[Job 9:5|they whom he overthrew|hi quos subvertit]]: [[Job 9:6|Who shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble|qui commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutientur]]. Ecclesiasticus also says: [[Ecclus 16:18|Behold the heaven, and the heavens of heavens, the deep, and all the earth, and the things that are in them, shall be moved in his sight|Ecce cœlum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur]]; [[Ecclus 16:19|The mountains also, and the hills, and the foundations of the earth: when God shall look upon them, they shall be shaken with trembling|montes simul et colles, et fundamenta terræ, et quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur]]. [[16:19|But they that fear thee|Qui autem timent te]] with filial fear, persevering to the end, [[16:19|shall be great with thee in all things|magni erunt apud te per omnia]]: for they [[Matt 13:43|shall the just shine as the sun|fulgebunt sicut sol]] in their kingdom[[Dan 12:3||]], and nothing shall be wanting to them.

paras.t: Væ genti insurgenti super genus meum, id est contra filios Israel, et nunc contra Christianos injuste se erigenti. Dominus enim omnipotens vindicabit in eis peccata eorum contra fideles commissa: juxta illud Deuteronomii, Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur, et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum. In die judicii generalis ac particularis visitabit illos, visitatione pœnæ et condemnationis. De qua loquitur per Sophoniam: Visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur; et visitabo super viros defixos in fæcibus suis. De qua visitatione loquitur Isaias, Post dies multos visitabuntur: quia damnati post quamcumque seu quantumlibet longam durationem punientur. Dabit enim ignem et vermes in carnes eorum; juxta illud Isaiæ, Vermis eorum non morietur, et ignis eorum non exstinguetur. Ideo subditur: Ut urantur et sentiant usque in sempiternum. Et de igne illo nulla est dubitatio, quin vere sit corporalis et acerrime puniens, sed non consumens. Porro de verme communiter dicitur, quod sit spiritualis, videlicet remorsus synderesis. Verum, quia hic dicitur, Dabit ignem et vermes in carnes eorum; aliqui, ut Haymo et eum sequentes, de corporalibus, edacibus, horrendissimis ac monstruosissimis vermibus istud exponunt. De quo nuper plenius scripsi super illud Ecclesiastici, Humilia valde spiritum tuum, quoniam vindicta carnis impii, ignis et vermis: idcirco hoc loco pertranseo.
paras.en: [[16:20|Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people|Væ genti insurgenti super genus meum]], that is, against the children of Israel, and now that rises up unjustly against Christians. [[16:20|for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them|Dominus enim omnipotens vindicabit in eis]] for their sins committed against the faithful, according to the word of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:43|for he will revenge the blood of his servants: and will render vengeance to their enemies|Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur, et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum]]. [[16:20|in the day of judgment|In die judicii]], general and particular, [[16:20|he will visit them|visitabit illos]] with the visitation of punishment and condemnation; of which he speaks through Sophonias: [[Soph 1:9|And I will visit in that day upon every one that entereth arrogantly|Visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur]]; [[Soph 1:12|and will visit upon the men that are settled on their lees|et visitabo super viros defixos in fæcibus suis]]. Of this visitation Isaias speaks: [[Is 24:22|and after many days they shall be visited|Post dies multos visitabuntur]]; for the damned will be punished after any duration, however long. [[16:21|For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh|Dabit enim ignem et vermes in carnes eorum]] [the print of this verse is damaged; it is read with the help of the Vulgate], according to the word of Isaias: [[Is 66:24|their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched|Vermis eorum non morietur, et ignis eorum non exstinguetur]]. Therefore it is added: [[16:21|that they may burn, and may feel for ever|Ut urantur et sentiant usque in sempiternum]]. And of that fire there is no doubt that it is truly bodily and punishes most sharply, but does not consume. Of the worm it is commonly said that it is spiritual, namely the remorse of synderesis [that is, of the conscience's inborn grasp of right, which in the damned gnaws as remorse]. But because it is said here, [[16:21|he will give fire, and worms into their flesh|Dabit ignem et vermes in carnes eorum]], some, as Haymo and those who follow him, explain this of bodily worms, devouring, most horrible and most monstrous. Of this I wrote more fully lately on the word of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 7:19|Humble thy spirit very much: for the vengeance on the flesh of the ungodly is fire and worms|Humilia valde spiritum tuum, quoniam vindicta carnis impii, ignis et vermis]]; therefore I pass over it in this place.

paras.t: Amplius, veneranda hæc Judith ac populus, non laudibus tantum, sed et sacrificiis Deum honoraverunt, sicut subjungitur. Et factum est post hæc, omnis populus, id est quidam de omnibus, præsertim majores ac bellatores, post victoriam venit ad Jerusalem, ubi erat locus sacrificiorum, adorare Dominum: quem in omni loco poterant adorare, sed adorare eum sacrificiis non licebat nisi in templo, nisi ex inspiratione et dispensatione divina. Et mox ut purificati sunt omnes secundum legem. De purificatione autem redeuntium a bello, legitur in Numerorum libro: qui purificabantur adspersione aquæ lustrationis, de qua iterum Numerorum libro habetur. Obtulerunt holocausta: quæ ad divinæ majestatis honorem totaliter incendebantur, in signum quod rationalis creatura debet se totam Deo offerre, ac divino mancipare obsequio; et vota, id est votivas seu spontaneas hostias, et repromissiones suas, id est oblationes quas facere promiserunt. De quibus omnibus in Levitico legitur. Porro Judith universa vasa, id est arma, bellica Holofernis, quæ dedit illi populus, et conopeum, de quibus jam dictum est, obtulit Deo totius victoriæ donatori, in recognitionem et jugem commemorationem beneficiorum ipsius. Propter quod subditur: In anathema oblivionis, id est ad condemnationem et exclusionem immemorationis beneficiorum tantorum. Fecit enim ea suspendi vel reservari in templo, ut filii Israel ea intuendo, memores semper essent beneficiorum istorum.
paras.en: Moreover, this venerable Judith and the people honoured God not with praises only but also with sacrifices, as is added. [[16:22|And it came to pass after these things, that all the people|Et factum est post hæc, omnis populus]], that is, some of all, especially the elders and the warriors, [[16:22|after the victory, came to Jerusalem|post victoriam venit ad Jerusalem]], where the place of sacrifice was, [[16:22|to adore the Lord|adorare Dominum]]: whom they could adore in every place, but to adore him with sacrifices was not lawful except in the temple, unless by divine inspiration and dispensation. [[16:22|and as soon as they were purified|Et mox ut purificati sunt]], all of them, according to the law. Of the purification of those returning from war we read in the book of Numbers[[Num 31:19||]]: they were purified by the sprinkling of the water of expiation, of which we have again in the book of Numbers[[Num 19:9||]] [the margin notes here are partly unreadable; they seem to give Num. xxxi, 19–24 and xix]. [[16:22|they all offered holocausts|Obtulerunt holocausta]], which were wholly burnt to the honour of the divine majesty, in sign that the rational creature ought to offer itself wholly to God and give itself over to the divine service; [[16:22|and vows|et vota]], that is, votive or freewill victims, [[16:22|and their promises|et repromissiones suas]], that is, the offerings they had promised to make. Of all these we read in Leviticus. [[16:23|And Judith|Porro Judith]], [[16:23|all the arms of Holofernes|universa vasa bellica Holofernis]] [literally “the vessels”, that is, the arms, “of war”], [[16:23|which the people gave her, and the canopy|quæ dedit illi populus, et conopeum]], of which we have spoken already, [[16:23|offered|obtulit]] to God, the giver of the whole victory, in acknowledgement and perpetual remembrance of his benefits. Therefore it is added: [[16:23|for an anathema of oblivion|In anathema oblivionis]] [*anathema*, a thing set apart for God], that is, for the condemnation and shutting out of forgetfulness of such great benefits. For she had them hung up or kept in the temple, so that the children of Israel, looking at them, might always be mindful of these benefits.

paras.t: Erat autem populus jucundus secundum faciem sanctorum, id est spirituali lætitia secundum apparatum hominum virtuosorum, et sicut in faciebus sanctorum virorum solet ex interiori sinceritate et jucunditate interna, jucunditas quædam forinsecus ac claritas relucere. Et per tres menses gaudium hujus victoriæ celebratum est cum Judith. Post dies autem illos unusquisque rediit in sua. Et Judith magna facta est in Bethulia, quia crevit quotidie in sapientia et virtute, et in honore habebatur præcipuo, et præclarior erat universæ terræ Israel, id est clarissima mulierum Israelitarum tempore illo. Erat autem virtuti castitas adjuncta, ita ut non cognosceret virum omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, ex quo defunctus est Menasses vir ejus. Erat autem festis diebus procedens cum magna gloria: non utique cum fastu et pompa, sed ex devotione, et pro Dei honore, qui eam sic exaltavit, et cujus gratia considerabatur in ea. Processit autem cum decenti ornatu atque familia, prout decuit excellentiam; et gloriabatur in Domino.
paras.en: [[16:24|And the people were joyful in the sight of the sanctuary|Erat autem populus jucundus secundum faciem sanctorum]] [*secundum faciem sanctorum*, which Denis takes as “after the countenance of the saints”], that is, with spiritual gladness after the bearing of virtuous men; even as in the faces of holy men a kind of outward gladness and brightness is wont to shine from their inward sincerity and inner gladness. [[16:24|and for three months the joy of this victory was celebrated with Judith|Et per tres menses gaudium hujus victoriæ celebratum est cum Judith]]. [[16:25|And after those days every man returned to his house|Post dies autem illos unusquisque rediit in sua]]. [[16:25|and Judith was made great in Bethulia|Et Judith magna facta est in Bethulia]], for she grew daily in wisdom and virtue, and was held in special honour, [[16:25|and she was most renowned in all the land of Israel|et præclarior erat universæ terræ Israel]], that is, the most renowned of the Israelite women at that time. [[16:26|And chastity was joined to her virtue, so that she knew no man all the days of her life, after the death of Manasses her husband.|Erat autem virtuti castitas adjuncta, ita ut non cognosceret virum omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, ex quo defunctus est Menasses vir ejus]] [[16:27|And on festival days she came forth with great glory|Erat autem festis diebus procedens cum magna gloria]]: not indeed with haughtiness and pomp, but out of devotion, and for the honour of God, who had so exalted her, and whose grace was seen in her. She went forth with fitting array and household, as befitted her eminence; and she gloried in the Lord.

paras.t: Mansit autem in domo viri sui annis centum et quinque: non quod tot annis habitaverit in domo mariti defuncti, sed tamdiu quod pervenit ad annos vitæ suæ centum et quinque. Et dimisit abram suam liberam, id est, liberavit, imo et locupletavit eam abunde: quam dilexit ut filiam, juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Servus fidelis sit tibi dilectus quasi anima tua, et quasi filium tracta eum. Et defuncta est, ac sepulta cum viro suo in Bethulia, luxitque eam populus diebus septem, sicut in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Luctus mortui, dies septem; luctus autem fatui et iniqui, omnes dies vitæ eorum.
paras.en: [[16:28|And she abode in her husband's house a hundred and five years|Mansit autem in domo viri sui annis centum et quinque]]: not that she lived so many years in the house of her dead husband, but that she lived until she reached a hundred and five years of her life. [[16:28|and made her handmaid free|Et dimisit abram suam liberam]], that is, she freed her, and indeed enriched her abundantly, for she loved her as a daughter, according to the word of Ecclesiasticus: Let a faithful servant be loved by thee [[Ecclus 33:31|as thy own soul|quasi anima tua]], and treat him as a son [the margin gives Ecclus. xxxiii, 31, where the Vulgate has *quasi fratrem*, “as a brother”; Denis's first words are closer to Ecclus 7:23, “Let a wise servant be dear to thee as thy own soul”]. [[16:28|and she died, and was buried with her husband in Bethulia|Et defuncta est, ac sepulta cum viro suo in Bethulia]], [[16:29|And all the people mourned for seven days|luxitque eam populus diebus septem]], as it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 22:13|The mourning for the dead is seven days: but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of their life|Luctus mortui, dies septem; luctus autem fatui et iniqui, omnes dies vitæ eorum]].

paras.t: In omni autem spatio vitæ ejus non fuit qui perturbaret Israel. Hoc non potest intelligi sicut sonat, quum ea vivente Assyrii gravissime perturbaverint Israelem. Sed sensus est, quod in spatio vitæ ejus post præfatam victoriam, nullus generalem persecutionem Israelitico intulit populo. Et post mortem ejus multis annis: et hoc meritis sanctæ feminæ hujus. Dies autem victoriæ hujus festivitatis, ab Hebræis in numero sanctorum et festivorum dierum accipitur, et colitur a Judæis ex illo tempore usque in præsentem diem; atque, ut in Scholastica historia fertur, Cambysa est vocata a Cambyse seu Nabuchodonosor rege, ad Dei honorem ac impii regis confusionem.
paras.en: [[16:30|And all the time of her life there was none that troubled Israel|In omni autem spatio vitæ ejus non fuit qui perturbaret Israel]]. This cannot be understood as it sounds, since while she was living the Assyrians troubled Israel most grievously. But the sense is that in the span of her life after the victory spoken of, no one brought a general persecution on the Israelite people; [[16:30|nor many years after her death|Et post mortem ejus multis annis]]: and this by the merits of this holy woman. [[16:31|But the day of the festivity of this victory is received by the Hebrews in the number of holy|Dies autem victoriæ hujus festivitatis, ab Hebræis in numero sanctorum]] and festal [[16:31|days|dierum]], [[16:31|and is religiously observed by the Jews from that time until this day|et colitur a Judæis ex illo tempore usque in præsentem diem]]; and, as is told in the Scholastic History, it was called Cambysa, from Cambyses, or King Nabuchodonosor, to the honour of God and the confusion of the wicked king.

paras.t: Præterea constat, hanc magnanimem, castam et fervidam Judith, fuisse figuram Virginis gloriosæ atque Ecclesiæ: Holofernem autem et ejus exercitum, designasse diabolum et angelos tenebrarum, qui semper impugnant Ecclesiam. Beatissima autem Maria virgo prorsus devicit diabolum, sicut de ea Deus prædixit illi iniquo: Inimicitias ponam inter te et mulierem, ipsa conteret caput tuum. Et quanto Christifera Virgo et sancta Ecclesia in omni virtute et gratia pulchriores exsistunt, tanto plus impius ille eas subvertere nisus est. Sed ipsæ prostraverunt eum proprio pugione ipsius, dum tentamenta illius penitus confutantes, per ea sibi ipsis meruerunt coronam, et illi procuraverunt confusionem; cunctis quoque fidelibus formam resistendi dæmonibus ostenderunt, ita quod fideles exemplis et documentis Virginis benedictæ et almæ matris Ecclesiæ succensi ac roborati, fugaverunt et vicerunt dæmones tentatores, suamque victoriam Deo cum omni humilitate, laude, gratiarumque actione, et sacrificio evangelicæ legis attribuerunt et obtulerunt. Pretiosissimas demum opes, id est animas deceptas, quas abstulerunt Holoferni, id est diabolo, incorporaverunt Domino Jesu Christo in anathema oblivionis, quatenus nunquam obliviscamur beneficiorum Salvatoris. Sed et Virgini benedictæ optime convenit laus illa: Tu gloria Jerusalem, tu lætitia Israel, tu honorificentia populi tui.
paras.en: Moreover it is certain that this great-souled, chaste and fervent Judith was a figure of the glorious Virgin and of the Church, while Holofernes and his army signified the devil and the angels of darkness, who are always attacking the Church. Now the most blessed Virgin Mary utterly overcame the devil, as God foretold of her to that wicked one: [[Gen 3:15|I will put enmities between thee and the woman|Inimicitias ponam inter te et mulierem]], [[Gen 3:15|she shall crush thy head|ipsa conteret caput tuum]]. And the more beautiful the Virgin who bore Christ and the holy Church are in every virtue and grace, the more that wicked one has striven to overthrow them. But they laid him low with his own dagger, when, wholly refuting his temptations, they earned by them a crown for themselves and brought confusion on him; and they showed all the faithful the way to resist the demons, so that the faithful, kindled and strengthened by the examples and teachings of the blessed Virgin and of our kindly mother the Church, have put to flight and overcome the tempting demons, and have ascribed and offered their victory to God with all humility, praise and thanksgiving, and with the sacrifice of the law of the Gospel. Lastly, the most precious riches, that is, the deceived souls which they took from Holofernes, that is, from the devil, they have incorporated into the Lord Jesus Christ for an anathema of oblivion, so that we may never forget the benefits of the Saviour. And to the blessed Virgin that praise is most fitting: [[Jdt 15:10|Thou art the glory of Jerusalem, thou art the joy of Israel|Tu gloria Jerusalem, tu lætitia Israel]], [[Jdt 15:10|thou art the honour|tu honorificentia]] of thy people.

paras.t: Postremo, de præfato Nabuchodonosor seu Cambyse in Historiis recitatur: Cambyses post prædicta cum grandi exercitu intravit et vastavit Ægyptum, et abominatus religionem Ægypti, cærimonias ejus ac templa deposuit, ædificavitque urbem Babylonem in Ægypto: a qua dum regrederetur, ægrotavit ac ferebatur cervicibus regum, et mortuus est in Damasco; reddente illi quod meruit Judice summo, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Lastly, of the aforesaid Nabuchodonosor, or Cambyses, it is told in the Histories: After these things Cambyses entered Egypt with a great army and laid it waste; and abhorring the religion of Egypt, he did away with its ceremonies and temples, and built the city of Babylon in Egypt; and while he was returning from it, he fell sick, and was carried on the necks of kings, and died at Damascus: the supreme Judge, who is God over all, exalted and blessed, rendering to him what he deserved. Amen.
